GN_Sip until a cursor key or Enter, converts it with GN_Gtm (an invalid time beeps and is
edited again) and stores it at IX. The cursor is on while editing.
Entry: IX = 3-byte internal time; B = column; C = row.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1; A = the key that ended the input; (IX+0..2) = the new time.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from GN_Ptm or GN_Sip.
Changes: AF, DE, HL, AF'.
Keeps: BC, IX.

10688.synopsis:
Fetches the handle of the standard output (OS_Nq, NQ_Out). The Clock, Calendar and Alarm
copy; the Diary has its own.
Entry: none.
Exit: IX = standard output handle.
Keeps: BC.

10696.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to a column of the current row (SOH "2X").
Entry: B = column.
Changes: AF.

10708.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to a position in the current window (SOH "3@").
Entry: B = column; C = row.
Changes: AF.

10725.synopsis:
Applies the current hardware toggles (reverse, flash, grey, underline) to the next
characters from the cursor (SOH "2A").
Entry: A = 32 + number of characters.

10750.synopsis:
Toggles tiny type, then falls into ToggleRvrs to toggle reverse video.
Entry: none.

10753.synopsis:
Entry inside ToggleTR: toggles reverse video (SOH "R").
Entry: none.

10765.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to (0,0) and clears the current window.
Entry: none.

10784.synopsis:
Clears from the cursor to the end of the line.
Entry: none.

10792.synopsis:
The text "DATE", null-terminated: the name of the mailbox the Calendar reads and writes with
OS_Sr (SR_RPD, SR_WPD).

10797.synopsis:
The Clock popdown's entry, reached from the vector at the start of the code.
1. Enables escape detection and checks the OZ version (OS_Nq, NQ_Voz); leaves with OS_Bye on
an older OZ.
2. Opens window 5 with GN_Win (MainWindowDef) and reserves 7 bytes at IX: a time, a date and
the menu selector (IX+6).
3. Clears the window, prints the "ESC SET" menu on the bottom line and highlights it
(ClkHighlight1).
4. Reads the date (GN_Gmd), formats it in full (GN_Pdt) and prints the weekday, the day and
month, and the year on three centred lines.
5. Prints the time with seconds at (3,5) (DisplayTime); when GN_Gmt finds the time
inconsistent with the date read (Fz = 0), redraws from step 3.
6. Waits 25 centiseconds for a key (OS_Tin) and dispatches it through ClkKeyCmds_tbl;
success redraws from step 3, RC_Susp and RC_Time update the time, RC_Fail waits again,
anything else (RC_Esc acknowledged) leaves through Exit.

11054.synopsis:
The Clock's command table for KeyJump: Right (Clock_Right), Left (Clock_Left) and Enter
(Clock_Enter), ended by 0.

11075.synopsis:
Left in the Clock: toggles the menu selector (IX+6) between ESC and SET and redraws the
highlight. Clock_Right continues here.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail, so the clock waits for the next key without redrawing.
Keeps: BC.

11097.synopsis:
Right in the Clock: toggles the menu selector (IX+6) between ESC and SET; continues in
Clock_Left to redraw the highlight.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail.
Keeps: BC.

11111.synopsis:
Draws the Clock's menu highlight on row 6: removes the reverse from the 16-character bar,
then reverses the 7 characters of the selected entry (column 0 for ESC, 7 for SET, from bit
0 of IX+6); then toggles tiny and reverse back.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame.
Changes: AF, BC.

11150.synopsis:
The Clock's SET command, reached through ClkCmds_tbl: clears the window, shows the "NEW
DATE" and "NEW TIME" titles, reads the time into (IX+0..2) (GN_Gmt) and the date into
(IX+3..5) (GN_Gmd), shows the time and runs the two fields of ClkSet_tbl with NavigateTable.
After Enter, sets the time (GN_Pmt) and the date (GN_Pmd) with alarm handling suspended
(OS_Alm AH_AINC, AH_ADEC). Selects ESC in the menu again.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from NavigateTable; the date and time are not set.

11255.synopsis:
The date field of the Clock's SET form: edits the date at IX+3 at (2,2) with AskDate.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame Exit, Error: as AskDate.
Keeps: IX.

11271.synopsis:
The time field of the Clock's SET form: edits the time at IX at (3,5) with AskTime.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame Exit, Error: as AskTime.

11277.synopsis:
Prints the time at IX with seconds and leading zeroes at (3,5); continues in DisplayTime.
Entry: IX = 3-byte internal time.

11288.synopsis:
The fields of the Clock's SET form for NavigateTable: a 0 start mark, SetDate, SetTime and
the $FFFF end mark.

11296.synopsis:
The Clock's menu commands for TableJump, indexed by the selector: Exit (ESC) and Cl_Set
(SET).

11300.synopsis:
The Clock's GN_Win window definition: window 5 with bars, shelf brackets and an 8-pixel
banner ($A5), at (78,0), 14 columns by 8 rows, banner clock_banner.

11313.synopsis:
The Calendar popdown's entry, reached from the vector at the start of the code and again
after RC_Draw.
1. Enables escape detection and checks the OZ version (OS_Nq, NQ_Voz); leaves with OS_Bye on
an older OZ.
2. Clears its 33 bytes of workspace and opens window 5 (CalWindow_txt).
3. Reads a date and a diary entry from the "DATE" mailbox (OS_Sr, SR_RPD); with one, follows
the diary's entry list from it. Without one, or when InitMonth rejects it, takes today's
date (GN_Gmd), and a fixed date when that is rejected too.
4. Writes the date into the mailbox (SR_WPD), draws its month (DrawMonth), highlights the
day and runs the keys of CalKeyCmds_tbl with KeyJump0.
5. Restarts after RC_Draw; leaves through Exit otherwise.

11460.synopsis:
The Calendar's command table for KeyJump0: Enter (Cal_Enter), Shift Up and Down (Cal_SUp,
Cal_SDown), Diamond Up and Down (Cal_DUp, Cal_DDown), Down, Left, Up and Right (Cal_Down,
Cal_Left, Cal_Up, Cal_Right), Square Right and Left (Cal_ARight, Cal_ALeft), ended by 0.

11530.synopsis:
Left in the Calendar: moves to the previous day; from the 1st, draws the previous month and
highlights its last day.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11564.synopsis:
Down in the Calendar: moves a week on; past the month's end, draws the next month and
highlights the same weekday in its first week.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11613.synopsis:
Up in the Calendar: moves a week back; in the first week, draws the previous month and
highlights the same weekday in its last week.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11651.synopsis:
Shift Down in the Calendar: moves to the same day of the next month (the month's last day if
it is shorter); continues in Cal_SUpDn.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11656.synopsis:
Shift Up in the Calendar: moves to the same day of the previous month (the month's last day
if it is shorter). Falls into Cal_SUpDn, which takes the 1st of the new month in ABC, draws
the month and highlights the day.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11693.synopsis:
Diamond Down in the Calendar: moves to the same day of the same month a year later; joins
Cal_DUp to make the date (GN_Dei) and continues in Cal_SUpDn.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11703.synopsis:
Diamond Up in the Calendar: moves to the same day of the same month a year earlier; makes
the 1st of that month (GN_Dei) and continues in Cal_SUpDn.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11724.synopsis:
Enter in the Calendar: asks for a date after "Look for : " on row 7, starting from today's,
and moves to it (MoveToDay), redrawing the month when needed; asks again when MoveToDay
fails. Escape abandons the input (tj_2). Then clears the prompt line and highlights the day.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from AskDate other than RC_Esc.
Changes: IX (left pointing at the freed 3-byte buffer).

11798.synopsis:
Makes the 1st of the month before the one in ubMonth and swYear (December of the year before
for January); shares its end with NextMonth.
Entry: none (ubMonth, swYear).
Exit: ABC = internal date of the 1st of the month.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from GN_Dei.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.
Keeps: DE.

11819.synopsis:
Makes the 1st of the month after the one in ubMonth and swYear (January of the year after
for December) with GN_Dei.
Entry: none (ubMonth, swYear).
Exit: ABC = internal date of the 1st of the month.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from GN_Dei.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.
Keeps: DE.

11848.synopsis:
Fills the Calendar's month variables from a date: MonthStart (the 1st, internal format),
swYear, ubMonth, ubNMonthDays, ubDay (the date's day of the month) and ubWeekday (the
weekday of the 1st), using GN_Die and GN_Dei.
Entry: ABC = internal date.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 from GN_Die or GN_Dei.
Changes: F, HL.
Keeps: A, BC, DE.

11908.synopsis:
Makes a date the Calendar's current day: fills the month variables (InitMonth), stores the
date in CurrentDay and redraws the month (DrawMonth) when the date is outside the month
drawn.
Entry: ABC = internal date.
Exit: Fc = 0; E = A.
Error: Fc = 1 from InitMonth; the month variables may be partly updated.

11971.synopsis:
Draws the month set up by InitMonth.
1. Clears the window; records the month's first day (DrawnMonthStart, SearchDay) and the
first day of the next month (NextMonthStart); positions the diary list before the month
(FindPrevDiaryEntry).
2. Prints the month name (GN_Ldm) and the year (GN_Pdn, at least 4 digits below 100, " BC"
for a negative year) centred on the first line, and reverses that line.
3. Prints the short weekday names, Monday first, in tiny underlined type.
4. Prints the day numbers from the weekday of the 1st, five columns each, with a bullet in
front of a day that has a diary entry (DrawMonthDay).
Entry: none (the month variables).
Keeps: DE.

12202.synopsis:
Square Right in the Calendar: moves to the next day after the current one that has a diary
entry (FindNextDiaryEntry, MoveToDay) and highlights it; continues in Cal_ALeft's tail.
Nothing moves when there is none.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.

12210.synopsis:
Square Left in the Calendar: moves to the previous day before the current one that has a
diary entry (FindPrevDiaryEntry, MoveToDay) and highlights it. Nothing moves when there is
none.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.

12236.synopsis:
Copies the current day (CurrentDay) to SearchDay, where a diary-entry search starts.
Entry: none.
Changes: A, HL.

12249.synopsis:
Finds the first diary entry dated after SearchDay. The Diary's entries form an XOR-linked
list walked with GN_Xnx (swapping BHL and CDE reverses the direction); the position is kept
in DiaryEntry (previous) and NextDiaryEntry (current). The search walks backward until an
entry dated before the search day, then forward until one dated after it. A walk stops at
the end of the list or back at OrigDiaryEntry, the entry the Diary passed with the date.
Entry: SearchDay = the day to search from; DiaryEntry, NextDiaryEntry = list position.
Exit: Fc = 0: found; NextDiaryDay = its date; DiaryEntry, NextDiaryEntry = position on it.
Error: Fc = 1 when no later entry exists (the position is stored all the same).
Changes: AF, BC, HL.
Keeps: DE.

12286.synopsis:
Finds the last diary entry dated before SearchDay: walks forward until an entry dated on or
after the search day, then backward until one dated before it, and turns the position to
face forward again. Called by DrawMonth (with SearchDay = first day of the drawn month) and
by Cal_ALeft. The list and its end tests are as in FindNextDiaryEnt.
Entry: SearchDay = the day to search from; DiaryEntry, NextDiaryEntry = list position.
Exit: Fc = 0: found; NextDiaryDay = its date; DiaryEntry, NextDiaryEntry = position on it.
Error: Fc = 1 when no earlier entry exists (the position is stored all the same).
Changes: AF, BC, HL.
Keeps: DE.

12332.synopsis:
Stores the diary list position: CDE (the previous entry) in DiaryEntry and BHL (the current
entry) in NextDiaryEntry.
Entry: CDE = previous entry; BHL = current entry.
Changes: A.

12388.synopsis:
Steps one entry along the diary list with GN_Xnx and tests for the end of the walk: Fz = 1
when the new entry is null or is OrigDiaryEntry (the test at loc_EDF7).
Entry: BHL = current entry; CDE = previous entry.
Exit: BHL = next entry; CDE = the entry left; Fz = 1 at the end of the walk.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

12425.synopsis:
Reads the date of the diary entry at BHL, its bytes 3 to 5 read with GN_Rbe, into
NextDiaryDay (a 3-byte internal date).
Entry: BHL = diary entry (extended address).
Exit: NextDiaryDay = the entry's date; A = its high byte; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: HL.

12463.synopsis:
Subtracts BC days from CurrentDay, a 3-byte internal date, and falls into SetCurDay, which
stores the result.
Entry: BC = number of days.
Exit: CurrentDay = AHL = the new date.
Changes: AF, HL.

12481.synopsis:
Records D as the selected day of the month (ubDay) and falls into HighlightDay.
Entry: D = day of the month.
Changes: AF, D.

12485.synopsis:
Shows the selected day (ubDay) in reverse: moves to its cell in the month grid, cell
ubWeekday - 1 + ubDay (MoveToDayXY), turns reverse on, applies it to the cell's 5 characters
and turns reverse off again.
Entry: ubDay = day of the month; ubWeekday = cell of the month's first day.
Changes: AF, D.

12508.synopsis:
Removes the highlight from the selected day: moves to its cell, as HighlightDay does, and
applies the plain attributes (reverse off) to the cell's 5 characters.
Entry: ubDay = day of the month; ubWeekday = cell of the month's first day.
Changes: C.
Keeps: AF.

12528.synopsis:
Prints one day cell of the month grid at the cursor: a space, a bullet (BulletR_txt) when
the day has a diary entry or a space when not, then the day number in 2 digits with a
trailing space (GN_Pdn).
1. Works out the day's date, DrawnMonthStart + C - 1, and compares it with NextDiaryDay.
2. While the day is past NextDiaryDay, steps the diary list forward (GN_Xnx, PutDiaryList,
PutNxtDiaryDay) and compares again; at the end of the list the day gets no bullet.
Entry: C = day of the month (1 = first); NextDiaryDay and the list position from
FindPrevDiaryEnt or the previous cell.
Exit: B = 0.
Changes: AF, B, HL.
Keeps: C, DE.

12610.synopsis:
VDU string SOH, SD_BRGT, 0: the right-pointing bullet DrawMonthDay prints before the number
of a day that has a diary entry.

12613.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to cell A of the month grid (1 = the top left cell, seven cells a row): row
2 + (A - 1) div 7, column 5 * ((A - 1) mod 7), through MoveToXYbc.
Entry: A = cell number.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC.

12636.synopsis: Text " BC", zero-terminated: DrawMonth prints it after the year of a month before year 1.

12640.synopsis: Text "Look for : ", zero-terminated: the date prompt Cal_Enter prints on row 7.

12652.synopsis:
VDU sequence that sets up the Calendar's window: defines window 5 at column 42, row 0, 35
columns wide and 8 rows high (SOH 7 #), selects and clears it (SOH 2 C 5) and turns off
scrolling and the cursor (SOH 3 - S C). Printed by init_calendar with GN_Sop.

12671.synopsis:
Alarm popdown: entry point.
1. Checks the OZ version with OS_Nq (NQ_Voz) and leaves through Exit when it is not this
OZ's version.
2. Enables ESC detection (OS_Esc SC_ENA) and suspends alarms while the popdown runs (OS_Alm
AH_SUSP).
3. At alm_1: draws window 6 with the "ALARMS" title and the column header, and sets up
windows 4 and 5.
4. Clears MailDate and the list state; reads the "DATE" mail into MailDate (OS_Sr SR_RPD).
Without one it takes today's date (GN_Gmd) and reads a "NAME" mail into scratch1; with a
name it loads alarms from that file (AlmLoadMail, AlmLoad2).
5. AlmEntry: draws the list (RedrawAlarms) and runs the key loop (KeyJump0 with
AlmKeyCmds_tbl); RC_Draw starts again at alm_1, anything else falls into AlmExit.
Entry: none.
Exit: does not return.

12892.synopsis:
Leaves the Alarm popdown: re-enables alarms (OS_Alm AH_REV) and jumps to Exit (OS_Bye).
Reached at the end of the key loop, from the ESC button and with command code $04.
Entry: none.
Exit: does not return.

12917.synopsis:
Left arrow in the alarm list: moves the button highlight to the previous of ESC, SET ALARM,
CLEAR ALARM and VIEW ALARM (the low 2 bits of ubAlmActiveButton), from the first to the
last. CLEAR ALARM and VIEW ALARM are refused while no alarm is shown. The shared code at
almlr_2 stores the button and redraws the row (AlmHilightButton).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail (KeyJump0 then reads the next key).
Changes: AF, BC.

12954.synopsis:
Right arrow in the alarm list: moves the button highlight to the next button, from the last
to the first, and joins Alm_Left's code at almlr_2.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail (KeyJump0 then reads the next key).
Changes: AF, BC.

12968.synopsis:
Up arrow in the alarm list: moves the selection bar to the previous alarm.
1. Inside the window it moves the bar up a row (ubSelectedAlmPos).
2. On the top row with alarms above, it scrolls the window (SOH SD_UP), redraws the button
row, and prints the previous alarm on row 0 (ubTopVisibleAlarm - 1).
3. On the first alarm it goes to the last: counts the alarms and, with more than five, shows
the last five (DrawAlarms) and selects the last row. Does nothing while no alarm is shown.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail (KeyJump0 then reads the next key).

13073.synopsis:
Down arrow in the alarm list: moves the selection bar to the next alarm. Inside the window
it moves the bar down a row; on the bottom row with an alarm below, it scrolls the window
(SOH SD_DWN), prints that alarm on row 4 and redraws the button row; on the last alarm it
goes to the first, redrawing the list when the first is not shown. Does nothing while no
alarm is shown.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail (KeyJump0 then reads the next key).

13165.synopsis:
CLEAR ALARM: removes the selected alarm (number ubTopVisibleAlarm + ubSelectedAlmPos) from
the alarm chain with GN_Uab and frees its block with GN_Fab when GN_Uab took it out (Fc = 0,
Fz = 1), then redraws the list. Returns at once while no alarm is shown.
Entry: none.
Exit: AF as GN_Uab or GN_Fab left it; Fc = 0, A = 0 when no alarm is shown.

13200.synopsis:
VIEW ALARM: shows the selected alarm in full (ViewSingleAlarm) and falls into PressEsc_txt,
which waits for ESC. Returns at once while no alarm is shown.
Entry: none.
Exit: as PressEsc_txt; Fc = 0, A = 0 when no alarm is shown.

13219.synopsis:
Entry inside AlmView, also called after alarms are loaded or saved: prints "PRESS ESC WHEN
READY" on row 5 and reads keys (OS_In) until ESC, ignoring keys and RC_Susp. ESC is
acknowledged and the alarm list redrawn (RedrawAlarms). RC_Draw restarts AlmView, whoever
the caller was.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = 0 after ESC.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Quit and the like).

13291.synopsis:
SET ALARM: creates a new alarm and lets the user edit it.
1. Allocates an alarm block (GN_Aab), binds it in segment 1 and clears its 47 bytes.
2. Fills in the current time (GN_Gmt), the date from MailDate, ALMF_BELL and ALRF_NEVER.
3. Runs the edit form (AlmSetMain); on success links the block into the alarm chain
(GN_Lab). When GN_Lab fails with RC_Fail it beeps and returns to the form.
4. On another error or ESC it frees the block (GN_Fab). Errors other than ESC are reported
(GN_Err); RC_Quit returns at once, any other case redraws the alarm list.
Entry: MailDate = the date to start from.
Exit: Fc = 0: the alarm is set.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Esc when the user left with ESC).

13394.synopsis:
Redraws the alarm list (DrawAlarms) and the selection bar (DrawAlmHilight).
Entry: ubTopVisibleAlarm, ubSelectedAlmPos.

13400.synopsis:
Clears the list window and prints up to five alarms from number ubTopVisibleAlarm, one a
line (GetAlarmByNum, PrintAlarm, GN_Nln). When that alarm no longer exists it starts again
from the first, setting ubTopVisibleAlarm and ubSelectedAlmPos to 0. Stores the count in
ubNumVisibleAlarms, makes ESC the active button and falls into DrawAlmWdBottom.
Entry: ubTopVisibleAlarm = number of the alarm on the top row.
Exit: ubNumVisibleAlarms = alarms shown (0 to 5); IX = last alarm block read.

13457.synopsis:
Prints the button row on row 5 in tiny text ("ESC SET ALARM CLEAR ALARM VIEW ALARM") and
falls into AlmHilightButton.
Entry: ubAlmActiveButton = the active button.

13525.synopsis:
Highlights the active button of the button row: with tiny text on, applies the plain
attributes to the 54 characters of row 5, then reverse to the 12 characters of the active
button (low 2 bits of ubAlmActiveButton: 0 ESC at column 1, 1 SET ALARM at 14, 2 CLEAR ALARM
at 27, 3 VIEW ALARM at 40) and turns tiny and reverse off (ToggleTR).
Entry: ubAlmActiveButton = the active button.
Changes: AF, BC.

13562.synopsis:
Entry inside AlmHilightButton: moves to column B, row C, turns reverse on, applies the
attributes to 12 characters and turns tiny and reverse off (ToggleTR).
Entry: B = column; C = row (5); tiny text on.
Changes: AF.

13576.synopsis:
Finds alarm number A (0 = the first) in the alarm chain: starts at the list head pAlarmList
and steps with GetNextAlarm.
Entry: A = alarm number.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = the alarm block, bound in segment 1; B = its bank.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Eof when the chain has fewer alarms.
Changes: AF, B, E, IX.

13594.synopsis:
Follows the link of the alarm block at IX (alm_Next, 3 bytes) to the next alarm and binds
its bank in segment 1.
Entry: IX = alarm block or the list head pAlarmList.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = the next alarm block; B = its bank.
Error: Fc = 1 at the end of the chain (A = 0).
Changes: AF, B, IX.
Keeps: C, HL.

13621.synopsis:
Prints alarm IX on the current line: back to column 0 and clears the line, then the date at
column 0 (GN_Pdt, short form with century and '/'), the time with seconds at column 15
(DisplayTime), the reason or command at column 25 and, when ALMF_SHOWBELL is set, a bell
symbol (SD_BLL) at column 50.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Changes: DE, HL.
Keeps: AF, BC, IX.

13712.synopsis:
The alarm edit form: shows the alarm (ViewSingleAlarm) and runs the fields of AlmSet_tbl
through NavigateTable (date, time, reason, bell, type, repeat, number of times); the arrow
keys move between fields, wrapping round, and ENTER ends the form.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: Fc = 0 after ENTER.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Esc after ESC).

13721.synopsis:
Shows one alarm in full: clears the window, prints the alarm on row 1 (PrintAlarm), the
header "BELL | ALARM TYPE | REPEAT EVERY | No.OF TIMES" on row 3 in tiny reverse, and on row
4 the bell, the type, the repeat interval (GetAlmRepeat, AlmShowRepeat) and the number of
times (AlmShowNTimes).
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.

13821.synopsis:
Date field of the alarm form: edits alm_Date at column 0, row 1 with AskDate.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: as AskDate: A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Keeps: IX.

13837.synopsis:
Time field of the alarm form: edits alm_Time at column 15, row 1 with AskTime.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: as AskTime: A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Keeps: IX.

13853.synopsis:
Reason field of the alarm form: edits alm_Reason at column 25, row 1 with GN_Sip (buffer of
23, returning on special keys) and the cursor shown, until an arrow key or ENTER (TestKeys).
RC_Susp edits again.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: Fz = 1; A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

13901.synopsis:
Bell field of the alarm form: highlights it (DrawBellHilight); up and down toggle ALMF_BELL
in alm_Flags and show it (AlmShowBell); an arrow key or ENTER (TestKeys) ends the edit and
removes the highlight. RC_Susp reads again.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: Fz = 1; A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

13954.synopsis:
Type field of the alarm form: as SetABell, with up and down toggling ALMF_EXECUTE (ALARM or
EXECUTE, AlmShowType).
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: Fz = 1; A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

14007.synopsis:
Repeat field of the alarm form: edits the repeat interval as a value and a unit.
1. Highlights the field and gets the value in the current unit (GetAlmRepeat).
2. Down decrements the value, moving to the previous unit at 0; up increments it, moving to
the next unit from NEVER or past 59 seconds or minutes. Shift-down and shift-up change the
unit (rotating alm_RepeatFlags) and reset the value to 1. Each change is shown
(AlmShowRepeat).
3. An arrow key or ENTER stores the value: days, months or years in alm_RepeatDays, weeks as
days (times 7), seconds, minutes or hours as centiseconds in alm_RepeatTime; NEVER stores
nothing. Then removes the highlight.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (nothing stored).

14217.synopsis:
Returns the alarm's repeat interval in the unit set in alm_RepeatFlags: 1 for NEVER;
alm_RepeatTime (centiseconds) divided by 100, 6000 or 360000 for seconds, minutes or hours
(GN_D24); alm_RepeatDays for days, months or years; alm_RepeatDays / 7 for weeks.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: BHL = the interval.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

14309.synopsis:
Number of times field of the alarm form: edits alm_RepeatNum. Down and up change it by 1,
with shift by 10 and with diamond by 100, showing each value (AlmShowNTimes); an arrow key
or ENTER stores it and removes the highlight. RC_Susp reads again.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (nothing stored).

14407.synopsis:
Prints "ON" or "OFF" for ALMF_BELL at column 4, row 4, through the code it shares with
AlmShowType (almt_1).
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

14424.synopsis:
Prints "ALARM" or "EXECUTE" for ALMF_EXECUTE at column 10, row 4.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

14450.synopsis:
Prints the repeat interval at column 21, row 4: blanks the 13 characters, prints the value
in 5 characters (not for NEVER), the unit name from RepeatUnits_tbl for the lowest set bit
of alm_RepeatFlags, and an 'S' unless the value is 1.
Entry: HL = the value (16 bits are printed); IX = alarm block, bound in.
Changes: AF, DE.
Keeps: BC, HL.

14540.synopsis:
Prints the number of times at column 35, row 4: "NEVER" for 0, "FOREVER" for $FFFF,
otherwise the number in 10 characters.
Entry: HL = number of times; IX = alarm block, bound in.
Changes: AF, BC, DE.
Keeps: HL.

14604.synopsis:
Highlights the type field of the alarm form (column 10, 10 characters) and jumps to
DrawHilight, which moves to row 4, toggles tiny and reverse (ToggleTR) and applies them to
the field. The toggles stay set while the field is edited; RmTypeHilight turns them back.
Changes: AF, BC.

14610.synopsis:
Highlights the repeat field of the alarm form (column 21, 13 characters) through
DrawHilight.
Changes: AF, BC.

14616.synopsis:
Highlights the number of times field of the alarm form (column 35, 11 characters) and falls
into DrawHilight.
Changes: AF, BC.

14633.synopsis:
Removes the highlight from the bell field of the alarm form (column 4, 5 characters) and
jumps to RemoveHiligh, which moves to row 4, toggles tiny and reverse back (ToggleTR) and
applies tiny text alone to the field.
Changes: AF, BC.

14639.synopsis:
Removes the highlight from the type field (column 10, 10 characters) through RemoveHiligh.
Changes: AF, BC.

14645.synopsis:
Removes the highlight from the repeat field (column 21, 13 characters) through RemoveHiligh.
Changes: AF, BC.

14651.synopsis:
Removes the highlight from the number of times field (column 35, 11 characters) and falls
into RemoveHiligh.
Changes: AF, BC.

14674.synopsis:
Draws the selection bar on the selected alarm: turns reverse on, applies it to the row
(RemAlmHilight) and turns reverse off.
Entry: ubSelectedAlmPos, ubNumVisibleAlarms.
Keeps: AF, BC.

14686.synopsis:
Applies the current attributes to the selected alarm's row (49 characters at column 0),
which removes the selection bar with reverse off. ubSelectedAlmPos is first limited to the
last row shown. Does nothing while no alarm is shown.
Entry: ubSelectedAlmPos, ubNumVisibleAlarms.
Keeps: AF, BC.

14912.synopsis:
Asks for a file name: selects window 4, clears it, prints "Filename: " and reads up to 32
characters into scratch1 (GN_Sip), then selects window 5. RC_Susp asks again; ESC is
acknowledged; RC_Quit leaves the popdown (Exit); another error is reported by GN_Err
(do_error), which returns with Fc = 0.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0; scratch1 = the name.
Error: Fc = 1 after ESC.

15161.synopsis:
Field table of the alarm form for NavigateTable: a 0 start mark, the field routines
SetADate, SetATime, SetAReason, SetABell, SetAType, SetARepeat and SetATimes, and a -1 end
mark.

15179.synopsis:
Table of 8 words: the unit names of the repeat interval, one per bit of alm_RepeatFlags from
bit 0 (SEC, MIN, HOUR, DAY, WEEK, MONTH, YEAR, NEVER). Read by AlmShowRepeat.

15195.synopsis:
Table of 4 words: the handlers of the button row (AlmExit, AlmSet, AlmClear, AlmView),
indexed by the active button. Alm_Enter jumps through it with TableJump.

15203.synopsis: Text " ON ", zero-terminated: the bell field when the bell is on (AlmShowBell).

15209.synopsis: Text " OFF ", zero-terminated: the bell field when the bell is off (AlmShowBell).

15215.synopsis: Text " ALARM ", zero-terminated: the type field of an alarm (AlmShowType).

15226.synopsis: Text " EXECUTE ", zero-terminated: the type field of a command (AlmShowType).

15237.synopsis:
Text " NEVER ", zero-terminated: the number of times 0 (AlmShowNTimes) and the NEVER entry
of RepeatUnits_tbl.

15249.synopsis: Text " FOREVER ", zero-terminated: the number of times $FFFF (AlmShowNTimes).

15261.synopsis: Text "SEC", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15265.synopsis: Text "MIN", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15269.synopsis: Text "HOUR", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15274.synopsis: Text "DAY", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15278.synopsis: Text "WEEK", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15283.synopsis: Text "MONTH", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15289.synopsis: Text "YEAR", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15294.synopsis:
Text "NAME", zero-terminated: the name of the mail AlarmEnt reads for a file of alarms to
load.

202.synopsis:
Wraps the edit line when bit 7 of (IY-69) is set and the line has grown past the column's
wrap width; called from the main loop after a typed character, when OS_Xin returns Fc = 1.
1. Returns unless L_8397 says the line can be wrapped and L_835B (for the current row) finds
a break point.
2. When the cursor (IY-87) lies past the break, moves it back by the break's offset, clears
(IY-88) and records the next row as the new position (L_82A2).
3. Runs L_BC66 over the line (output at $1DAA), copies the result back to ($1D3D) and starts
a split with L_8320.
4. Repeatedly cuts the line at the break found by L_8355, stores the first part as a slot
with L_823B (type $80 or $81, with format $0C or $0E when bit 6 of (IY-69) is set,
alternated by bit 1 of (IY-71)), moves the rest to the start of the buffer and pulls words
from the rows below with L_815B.
5. Finishes at L_81BE: ends line editing (L_B411), adjusts the rows below when the number of
rows changed ((IY-3) not 0), sets redraw flags and ends through L_8B80.
Entry: none.

359.synopsis:
Entry inside L_80BE: pulls words from the following rows onto the end of the text in the
edit line buffer, one word at a time through L_82B0, putting a space before each word when
needed. When the line becomes too wide (L_8355 returns Fc = 1) it continues at L_8101 to
split it again; when the paragraph ends it stores the last line with L_823B and finishes at
L_81BE. Also used by Format Paragraph (L_826F).
Entry: DE = end of the text at ($1D3D); (IY-114..-112) = source text pointer and bank, set
up by L_8323.

583.synopsis:
Stores the edit line as a slot: ORs A with (IY-42), gets a slot for the current column at
row (IY-11/-10) through L_8CA2, increments the row counters (IY-3), (IY-9/-8) and
(IY-11/-10), copies the text at ($1D3D) into the slot with L_B493 and clears (IY-42).
Entry: A = slot type byte; (IY-40) = text length + 1.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: jumps to L_EB07, the error reporter, when L_8CA2 fails.

635.synopsis:
Format Paragraph (command code 51, <>R): reflows the paragraph that starts at the cursor's
slot. When L_8397 says the slot cannot be formatted it moves the cursor down instead
(L_8E62). Otherwise it stores the edit line (L_B398), sets up the current slot's text as the
source with L_8323, refills the lines through L_815B and the splitting code of L_80BE, and
falls into L_8296 to move to the row after the paragraph ((IY-9/-8)).
Entry: none.

674.synopsis:
Records column A, row BC as the position to move to, with the row clamped to the last row:
when BC is not below the row count at (IY-97/-96) (L_C9F9), BC becomes that count minus 1.
Falls into L_82A2.
Entry: A = column; BC = row.
Exit: (IY-104) = A; (IY-103/-102) = BC; bit 7 of (IY-100) set.

686.synopsis:
Sets bit 7 of (IY-100) and falls into L_82A6 to record column A, row BC as the position to
move to.
Entry: A = column; BC = row.
Exit: (IY-104) = A; (IY-103/-102) = BC.

690.synopsis:
Stores column A in (IY-104) and row BC in (IY-103/-102), the recorded position to move to.
Entry: A = column; BC = row.
Changes: none.

700.synopsis:
Takes the next word for L_815B from the source text at (IY-114/-113) in bank (IY-112),
binding the bank with L_D887 when it is not (IY-111). When no source text is pending (H = 0)
it first drops the slot whose text was taken (L_8B61 on row (IY-9/-8), decrementing (IY-3)),
toggles bit 1 of (IY-71) and opens the slot on the next row (L_D7AD), which must hold text
that continues the paragraph: a type byte with bit 7 set and not $C0 in bits 7-6, format
bits ($0E) of 0, $0C or $0E, and a first character that is not 0 or a space. It then moves
past one word and its following spaces with L_83C5.
Entry: (IY-114..-112) = source pointer and bank; (IY-9/-8) = row.
Exit: Fc = 0; BC = position after the word and its spaces; (IY-114/-113) = that position, or
0 at the end of the text.
Error: Fc = 1 when the paragraph ends (no next slot, or one that does not continue it).

812.synopsis:
Starts a split with no source text: HL = 0, then falls into L_8323.
Entry: C = bank byte for (IY-112).

815.synopsis:
Sets up the state for wrapping or formatting: the source text pointer (IY-114/-113) = HL and
its bank (IY-112) = C, both row variables (IY-11/-10) and (IY-9/-8) = the current row
(L_D8B5), and (IY-3) and (IY-42) = 0. When the current slot exists and has format bits ($0E
of its type byte (IX+3)) not 0, falls into L_834C.
Entry: HL = source text pointer (0 for none); C = its bank.
Exit: Fc = 1 when there is no current slot (L_D7AA); IX = current slot otherwise.

856.synopsis:
Toggles bit 1 of (IY-71), which L_80BE uses to alternate a new slot's format between $0E and
$0C.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

865.synopsis:
Finds a break point in the edit line for the row in (IY-11/-10); falls into L_835B.
Entry: none.

871.synopsis:
Finds where the edit line must be broken to fit row BC's column: stores BC in (IY-26/-25),
gets the width limit for the current column with L_C917 and walks the text at ($1D3D) word
by word with L_83C5, counting the printing width in C.
Entry: BC = row.
Exit: Fc = 1, HL = start of the first word that does not fit, when the line is wider than
the limit and can be broken after an earlier word; Fc = 0 when it fits or has no break
point.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

931.synopsis:
Says whether the edit line can be wrapped or formatted. Returns Fc = 0 while an expression
is being edited (bit 6 of (IY-71)), when L_D249 returns Fc = 1, or when the current slot's
type byte (IX+3) has bit 7 clear or format bits ($0E) other than 0, $0C and $0E. Otherwise
(and when there is no current slot) it checks the text at ($1D3D) at L_83B8.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1 when the text holds a character other than a space; Fc = 0 otherwise.
Changes: AF, HL.

977.synopsis:
Moves HL over one item of slot text and counts its printing width in C. At a space it skips
the run of spaces and returns the next character. At a word it moves to the space or
terminator after it; highlight codes ($18-$1F, L_CE2A) are not counted, and an '@' field
that L_840A recognises is skipped (one holding a 3-byte compiled reference sets bit 5 of
(IY-42)).
Entry: HL = text pointer; C = width so far.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = first character after the spaces, or A = $20 with HL at the space ending
the word.
Error: Fc = 1 at the end of the text, A = 0 (or $20 after trailing spaces).
Changes: AF, C, HL.

1046.synopsis:
Examines the text after an '@' at HL for L_83C5. A byte $10-$13 after it (L_FE32) marks a
compiled reference. Otherwise it tries to read a slot reference with L_BD57 (keeping
(IY-110..-108)), accepted when an '@' closes it, and then accepts '@T', '@P', '@D' and '@@'.
Entry: HL = address of the '@'.
Exit: Fc = 1, Fz = 1 for a recognised field, HL at its last character; Fc = 1, Fz = 0 for a
compiled reference, HL at the marker byte; Fc = 0 when the '@' starts nothing it knows.
Changes: AF, HL.

1121.synopsis:
Insert/Overtype (command code 56, <>V): toggles bit 2 of (IY-71), the overtype mode that
Rubout and character insertion test.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

1130.synopsis:
Insert Reference (command code 44, <>K): only while an expression is being edited (bit 6 of
(IY-71)), writes the reference of the slot at the cursor (L_D0E2) into the edit line through
L_BBBF, with L_84AE set at ($1D4B) as the routine that receives each character.
Entry: none.

1147.synopsis:
Insert Character (command code 37, <>U): inserts a space at the cursor in insert mode (bit 2
of (IY-71) cleared for the call to L_84E3, then restored) and moves the cursor back onto it
(L_8E97).
Entry: none.

1167.synopsis:
Underline (command code 85, <>PU): inserts highlight code $18 at the cursor through L_84AE.
Entry: none.

1171.synopsis:
Bold (command code 86, <>PB): inserts highlight code $19 at the cursor through L_84AE.
Entry: none.

1175.synopsis:
Ext. Sequence (command code 87, <>PX): inserts highlight code $1A at the cursor through
L_84AE.
Entry: none.

1179.synopsis:
Italic (command code 88, <>PI): inserts highlight code $1B at the cursor through L_84AE.
Entry: none.

1183.synopsis:
Subscript (command code 89, <>PL): inserts highlight code $1C at the cursor through L_84AE.
Entry: none.

1187.synopsis:
Superscript (command code 90, <>PR): inserts highlight code $1D at the cursor through
L_84AE.
Entry: none.

1191.synopsis:
Alt. Font (command code 91, <>PA): inserts highlight code $1E at the cursor through L_84AE.
Entry: none.

1195.synopsis:
User Defined (command code 92, <>PE): inserts highlight code $1F at the cursor through
L_84AE.
Entry: none.

1199.synopsis:
Insert Highlights (command code 93, <>PHI): stores the edit line (L_B398), asks for the
highlight number with L_87BE, reloads the edit line with L_B543 and falls into L_84AE to
insert the code $17 + number.
Entry: none.

1210.synopsis:
Inserts character A at the cursor. Called from the main loop with a typed character, from
the highlight commands and as the character routine of Insert Reference. Codes below $20 are
ignored while an expression is being edited (bit 6 of (IY-71)). The character goes into the
edit line at L_84E9 when the current slot accepts text (its type byte (IX+3) has bit 7 set
and L_C9B8 returns Fc = 0), when there is no slot or an empty one and bit 5 of (IY-69) is
set, or while an expression is being edited. Otherwise it starts expression editing with
L_9276, empties the edit line (L_B56E) and tries again.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: (IY-34) = A.

1263.synopsis:
Inserts the printable character A at the cursor and moves the cursor right; codes below $20
return at once. Only while a line is edited (L_8690). The line may not grow to (IY-86)
characters: in insert mode (bit 2 of (IY-71) clear) the line length is checked, in overtype
mode the cursor. A cursor past the end of the line is reached by padding with spaces. In
insert mode, or at the end, the rest of the line moves up by one. Falls into
MthKey_CrsrRight after marking the line changed (L_8687).
Entry: A = character.
Exit: (IY-34) = A.
Error: Fc = 1 after a beep (L_EFE9) when the line is full.

1342.synopsis:
Cursor Right (command code 22): while a line is edited (bit 7 of (IY-72)), moves the cursor
(IY-87) one place right unless it is at (IY-86); otherwise falls into L_8543 to move to the
next column.
Entry: none.

1359.synopsis:
Next Column (command code 31, TAB): stores the edit line (L_B398) and records move request 3
through L_8E8E ((IY-101) = 3, (IY-100) = 1).
Entry: none.

1367.synopsis:
Add Column (command code 50, <>EAC): stores the edit line (L_B398) and adds a column with
L_D8CD (a 10-byte column entry of width 12), then flags the redraw (L_879F) and moves to the
new last column ((IY-98)) of the current row through L_8D30.
Entry: none.
Error: jumps to L_EB07 when L_D8CD fails.

1388.synopsis:
Start of Slot (command code 15): only while a line is edited (L_8690), puts the cursor
(IY-87) at 0.
Entry: none.

1396.synopsis:
End of Slot (command code 16): only while a line is edited (L_8690), puts the cursor (IY-87)
after the last character of the edit line (L_8572).
Entry: none.

1406.synopsis:
Finds the end of the edit line at ($1D3D).
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = address of its terminating 0; B = its length; A = 0.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

1419.synopsis:
Gets the address of the cursor in the edit line: B = (IY-87), then falls into L_8582.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = ($1D3D) + (IY-87); B = (IY-87).
Changes: B, DE, HL.

1422.synopsis:
Gets the address of position B in the edit line at ($1D3D).
Entry: B = position.
Exit: HL = ($1D3D) + B; DE = B.
Changes: DE, HL.

1430.synopsis:
Rubout (command code 35, DEL): only while a line is edited (L_8690) and the cursor is not at
0. Moves the cursor (IY-87) one place left and clears (IY-88); in overtype mode (bit 2 of
(IY-71)) it replaces the character there with a space and marks the line changed, otherwise
it falls into L_85A7 to delete it.
Entry: none.

1459.synopsis:
Delete Character (command code 36, <>G): only while a line is edited (L_8690), removes the
character at the cursor by moving the rest of the edit line down one place, and marks the
line changed (L_8687). Nothing happens at the end of the line.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1 when a character was removed.

1481.synopsis:
Previous Word (command code 27): while a line is edited, moves the cursor to the start of
the previous word (to the end of the line when the cursor is past it, or to 0). At position
0, or when no line is edited, and unless an expression is being edited, moves to the row
above: the cursor goes to the end of that slot's text when its type byte is $80 (L_B990,
L_B53C), to 0 otherwise, and Cursor Up (L_8E81) follows. Nothing happens on row 0.
Entry: none.

1579.synopsis:
Next Word (command code 26): while a line is edited, moves the cursor to the start of the
next word (L_8697). At the end of the line, or when no line is edited, and unless an
expression is being edited, puts the cursor at 0 (L_8D45) and moves down a row (L_8E62);
nothing happens on the last row (L_CA1E).
Entry: none.

1612.synopsis:
Delete Word (command code 38, <>T): only while a line is edited (L_8690), removes the text
from the cursor to the start of the next word (L_8697) and marks the line changed (L_8687).
Nothing happens when the cursor is at or past the end of the line.
Entry: none.

1634.synopsis:
Swap Case (command code 53, <>S): only while a line is edited (L_8690), inverts the case of
the character at the cursor when GN_Cls classifies it as a letter (InvCase), marks the line
changed and moves the cursor right (MthKey_CrsrRight).
Entry: none.

1658.synopsis:
Inverts the case of letter A. Codes below 191 have bit 5 flipped without a check; from 191
up only the ISO letters in InvCaseTable (capitals) and the same codes with bit 5 set (small
letters) are changed, other codes are returned unchanged.
Entry: A = letter.
Exit: A = the letter in the other case.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, HL.

1691.synopsis:
Table of 9 bytes: the ISO-8859-1 capital letters whose case InvCase inverts (196, 197, 198,
199, 203, 209, 214, 216, 220); the small letter is the code with bit 5 set.

1724.synopsis:
Ends the edit line at HL (writes 0 there), then falls into L_8687 to mark the line changed.
Entry: HL = address in the edit line.
Changes: none.

1726.synopsis:
Marks the edit line changed: sets bits 0 and 5 of (IY-72). Bit 0 is what L_B3D6 tests before
it stores the line back into its slot.
Entry: none.
Changes: none.

1735.synopsis:
Guard at the start of the line-editing commands: returns to its caller while a line is
edited (bit 7 of (IY-72) set); otherwise it drops the caller's return address, so the caller
returns to its own caller and the command does nothing.
Entry: none.
Changes: DE when it drops the return address.

1742.synopsis:
Finds the start of the word after the cursor: when the cursor (IY-87) is before the end of
the edit line, falls into L_86A4 from the cursor's address.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0 as L_86A4 returns.
Error: Fc = 1 when the cursor is at or past the end of the line, B = (IY-87).

1755.synopsis:
Entry inside L_8697: moves HL past the rest of the word (or the spaces) at HL and then past
the spaces that follow, counting the position in B.
Entry: HL = address in the edit line; B = its position.
Exit: Fc = 0; HL, B = the first character of the next word, A = that character and Fz = 0;
or HL, B at the terminator, A = 0 and Fz = 1.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

1782.synopsis:
Dialog description read by L_D98A for Microspace Pitch (L_86E1): 1 field, type $87 with the
prompt "Microspace printed output", two words 0 and 255, then the byte $81; a 0 ends the
list.

1816.synopsis:
Microspace Pitch (command code 84, <>PM): stores the edit line (L_B398) and shows the dialog
at L_86BF (L_D98A). When it is confirmed, clears bit 4 of (IY-70); when the returned A has
bit 0 set, sets bit 4 again and puts the dialog's value (IY+51) into (IY+28), 12 when the
value is 0.
Entry: none.

1849.synopsis:
Margin Left (command code 69): decreases the current column's wrap width (L_D551) by one
when it is 3 or more, writes it with L_D76C as the margin byte of the column's entry and of
the following columns it reaches, and flags the redraw (L_CA8D).
Entry: none.

1863.synopsis:
Margin Right (command code 70): increases the current column's wrap width (L_D551) by one,
unless it would wrap to 0, writes it with L_D76C as the margin byte of the column's entry
and of the following columns it reaches, and flags the redraw (L_CA8D).
Entry: none.

1880.synopsis:
Dialog description read by L_D98A for Width and Set Margin (L_874B, L_8744): 2 fields, a
number field (type $07) "New width" with the words 0 and 255 and a byte 0, and type $8A
"Specify column" with the byte $81; a 0 ends the list.

1915.synopsis:
Set Margin (command code 66, <>H): stores the edit line (L_B398) and continues in L_874B
with C = 1, so the new value goes into the margin byte (+1) of the column's entry.
Entry: none.

1922.synopsis:
Width (command code 65, <>W): stores the edit line (L_B398) and shows the dialog at L_8721
(L_D98A). The column is the current one, or the value at (IY+53) when the returned A has bit
0 set ("Specify column"). The new value (IY+51) goes into byte 0 (width) of the column's
10-byte entry at ($1D3F), or byte 1 (margin) when entered at L_8750 with C = 1. A width of 0
is refused with error $22 (L_EB07) when every other column already has width 0. Ends through
L_879F.
Entry: none.

2006.synopsis:
Shared exit of the column commands: sets bit 0 of (IY-71) (L_B3C1) and jumps to L_CA85,
which sets bits 7 and 1 of (IY-99).
Entry: none.

2012.synopsis:
Dialog description read by L_D98A for Insert Highlights (L_87BE): 1 field, a number field
(type $07) "Highlight number" with the words 1 and 8 and a byte 0; a 0 ends the list.

2037.synopsis:
Asks for a highlight number: stores the edit line (L_B398) and shows the dialog at L_87A5
(L_D98A).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = (IY+51) + $17, the highlight code $18-$1F.
Error: when the dialog is cancelled, drops its caller's return address and returns to the
caller's caller.

2056.synopsis:
Default Format (command code 81, <>LDF): applies the format change A = $40, B = 0, C = 0
through L_8852 (via L_8838).
Entry: none.

2061.synopsis:
Sign Brackets (command code 77, <>LSB): applies the format change A = $40, B = $C0, C = $FF
through L_8852 (via L_8838).
Entry: none.

2066.synopsis:
Sign Minus (command code 78, <>LSM): applies the format change A = $40, B = $40, C = $7F
through L_8852 (via L_8838).
Entry: none.

2071.synopsis:
Trailing Characters (command code 80, <>LCT): applies the format change A = 0, B = $10, C =
$EF through L_8852, which toggles the bit off again when a slot already has it.
Entry: none.

2076.synopsis:
Leading Characters (command code 79, <>LCL): applies the format change A = 0, B = $20, C =
$DF through L_8852, which toggles the bit off again when a slot already has it.
Entry: none.

2082.synopsis:
Dialog description read by L_D98A for Decimal Places (L_881E): 2 fields, a number field
(type $07) "Number of decimal places" with the words 0 and 9 and a byte 0, and type $84
"Floating format" with the byte $81; a 0 ends the list.

2133.synopsis:
Decimal Places (command code 76, <>LDP): stores the edit line (L_B398) and shows the dialog
at L_87EB (L_D98A). Applies the format change A = $40, C = $B0, B = $40 OR the number of
places (IY+51), or B = $4F when the returned A has bit 0 set ("Floating format"), through
L_8852. Returns when the dialog is cancelled.
Entry: none.

2163.synopsis:
LCR Align (command code 74, <>LLCR): applies the format change A = $C0, B = 8, C = $F1
through L_8852 (via L_884E), setting the alignment field (bits 3-1) of the format byte of
each slot in the marked block, or of the current slot.
Entry: none.

2167.synopsis:
Left Align (LAL) command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 71): loads B = 2 and joins L_884E, which sets
A = $C0 and the mask C = $F1 for the shared format routine L_8852. That routine writes
alignment code 2 into bits 1-3 of the type byte (IX+3) of every slot in the marked block, or
of the current slot when no block is marked (L_88C6). A slot that already has this alignment
has the field cleared instead.
Entry: none.
Exit: through L_8852 (marks the sheet as changed with L_B3C1).

2171.synopsis:
Centre Align (LAC) command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 72): loads B = 4 and joins L_884E, which
sets A = $C0 and the mask C = $F1 for the shared format routine L_8852. That routine writes
alignment code 4 into bits 1-3 of the type byte (IX+3) of every slot in the marked block, or
of the current slot when no block is marked (L_88C6). A slot that already has this alignment
has the field cleared instead.
Entry: none.
Exit: through L_8852 (marks the sheet as changed with L_B3C1).

2175.synopsis:
Right Align (LAR) command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 70): loads B = 6 and joins L_884E, which
sets A = $C0 and the mask C = $F1 for the shared format routine L_8852. That routine writes
alignment code 6 into bits 1-3 of the type byte (IX+3) of every slot in the marked block, or
of the current slot when no block is marked (L_88C6). A slot that already has this alignment
has the field cleared instead.
Entry: none.
Exit: through L_8852 (marks the sheet as changed with L_B3C1).

2179.synopsis:
Free Align (LAF) command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 74): loads B = 0 and joins L_884E, which sets
A = $C0 and the mask C = $F1 for the shared format routine L_8852. That routine writes
alignment code 0 into bits 1-3 of the type byte (IX+3) of every slot in the marked block, or
of the current slot when no block is marked (L_88C6). A slot that already has this alignment
has the field cleared instead.
Entry: none.
Exit: through L_8852 (marks the sheet as changed with L_B3C1).

2301.synopsis:
Sets the block range used by the block commands. When a block is marked, L_D014 copies the
two marks into the range, ordered: start column, row at (IY-58..-56) and end column, row at
(IY-55..-53). Otherwise the current slot (L_D0E2) becomes both the start and the end.
Entry: marks at (IY-67..-65) and (IY-64..-62), bit 7 of a mark's column byte set when unset.
Exit: block range at (IY-58..-53).
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX.

2327.synopsis:
Returns at once when bit 6 of A is set (Fz = 0); otherwise falls into L_88E3. Called from
the number formatting code (line 17439 of the source).
Entry: A = format byte; C = format bits.
Exit: as L_88E3 when bit 6 of A is clear.
Changes: AF, C.

2330.synopsis:
Merges the default number format into C: sets bit 7 of C unless bit 2 of (IY-69) is set,
then ORs C with the default format byte at (IY+9). Used by the format routine L_8852 for a
slot with no format of its own.
Entry: C = format bits.
Exit: A = C = merged format byte.
Changes: AF, C.

2344.synopsis:
Word Count command (BWC, MthKeyJmpTable entry 10). Counts the words in the text slots of the
marked block, or of the whole sheet when no block is marked (L_B2CC with A = 0), and shows
the result as "<n> words".
1. Commits any line being edited (L_B398) and starts the block walk (L_FBBD).
2. For each slot, L_8930 gives the text; each word found by L_86A4 adds 1 to DE.
3. L_FB93 moves to the next slot of the block; at the end L_EE7C prints DE, OS_Pout prints "
words" and (IY-84) is set to $0B.
Entry: none.

2406.synopsis:
Looks up the slot at the block walk's position (IY-61..-59) and, when it is a text slot (bit
7 of its type byte IX+3 set, bits 7 and 6 not both set), points HL at its text (L_B503).
Entry: (IY-61..-59) = column, row.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = slot; HL = its text; A = type byte.
Error: Fc = 1 when there is no slot there or it is not a text slot.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX.

2437.synopsis:
Fix Column command (LFC, MthKeyJmpTable entry 67). Walks the column list from ($1D5B) with
L_D0E8 (bit 7 of an entry = fixed, bit 6 = last entry). When any entry is fixed, clears bit
7 of every entry; otherwise sets bit 7 of the entries from ($1D5B) up to the current
column's entry ($1D5D). Ends in L_CA85, which requests a redraw.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

2500.synopsis:
Fix Row command (LFR, MthKeyJmpTable entry 66). Works on the row list at ($1D61), 6-byte
entries in which bit 7 of the first byte marks a fixed row and bit 6 the last entry. When
the first entry is fixed, notes its row in (IY-26..-25), calls L_D3E9 and clears bit 7 of
every entry. Otherwise calls L_D104 and rewrites the entries from ($1D61) up to the current
row's entry ($1D63) with bit 7 set. Ends by requesting a redraw (L_CA8D, bit 7 of (IY-23))
and jumping to L_D45B.
Entry: none.

2606.synopsis:
Clear Mark command (Q, MthKeyJmpTable entry 1), also called after Move and Delete. Unsets
both block marks by writing $80 into their column bytes (IY-67) and (IY-64) and requests a
redraw (L_CA8D).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = $80.
Changes: AF.

2617.synopsis:
Mark Block command (Z, MthKeyJmpTable entry 0). Marks the current slot (L_D0E2): the first
press sets the first mark (IY-67..-65), the second the second mark (IY-64..-62); a further
press starts again, setting the first mark and unsetting the second. Requests a redraw
(L_CA8D).
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

2662.synopsis:
Delete Row command (Y, MthKeyJmpTable entry 40). Deletes the slot of the current row in
every column, 0 to (IY-98) - 1, with L_8B61, then joins L_8A53 with A = $C0: L_B7A5 adjusts
the slot references by one row up, OS_Pur is called (L_EB49) and L_A341 marks the sheet
changed, recounts the rows and requests a redraw.
Entry: none.

2686.synopsis:
Delete Row in Column command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 39). Deletes the current slot (L_8B61),
which moves the slots below it up a row, then adjusts the references with A = $80 (L_B7A5),
calls OS_Pur (L_EB49) and finishes through L_A341.
Entry: none.

2706.synopsis:
Join Lines command (EJL, MthKeyJmpTable entry 42). When the current slot and the slot below
are both text slots, appends the text of the lower slot to the line in the edit buffer
($1D3D): L_BB7E converts it, passing each character to L_8A92. The joined line is stored
(L_B394) and the lower slot deleted (L_8A4E).
Entry: none.
Error: returns with nothing done when either slot is missing or not text; an error from
L_BB7E is reported through L_EB07.

2792.synopsis:
Gives the position of the slot below the current one: L_D0E2, then BC + 1.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = current column; BC = current row + 1; HL = ($1D5D).
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

2797.synopsis:
Remove Highlights command (PHR, MthKeyJmpTable entry 93): sets Fc and joins L_8ABB, which
shifts it into bit 7 of (IY-6) so that the highlight pass only removes the chosen highlight
code.
Entry: none.

2800.synopsis:
Highlight Block command (PHB, MthKeyJmpTable entry 94). Clears bit 7 of (IY-6), asks for the
highlight number (L_87BE, code = number + $17 in (IY-46)) and rebuilds every non-blank text
slot of the marked block in the buffer $1DAA.
1. L_9250 requires a marked block; L_FBBD starts the block walk.
2. Copies the text without the existing highlight codes; in highlight mode, also puts the
code before and after each word (L_8B4E). The 4 bytes after a character $10-$13 (L_FE32) are
copied unchanged.
3. Replaces the slot with the buffer (L_B8C7, L_B490) and flags it (L_C9CA); a line that
would reach $F5 bytes leaves the slot unchanged.
4. Marks the sheet changed (L_B3C1) and requests a redraw (L_CA73).
Entry: none.

2948.synopsis:
Entry inside L_8B51: loads A with the highlight code (IY-46) and stores it.
Entry: HL = buffer position; (IY-40) = length so far.
Exit: as L_8B51.

2951.synopsis:
Appends A to the highlight buffer: stores it at (HL), advances HL and increments the length
(IY-40).
Entry: A = byte; HL = buffer position.
Exit: HL + 1; A kept; Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 when the length has reached $F5.
Changes: F, HL.
Keeps: A, BC.

2967.synopsis:
Deletes the slot at column A, row BC: when it exists (L_D797), unlinks it from its column's
list (L_BA24, L_BA44, L_B9C6) and frees its memory with OS_Mfr (L_D95E).
Entry: A = column; BC = row.
Error: Fc = 1 when there is no slot there.

2998.synopsis:
Recounts the sheet's rows: sets the row count (IY-97..-96) to 1 (L_D1E9), then for each
column 0 to (IY-98) - 1 finds its last row (L_D7A5, L_D788) and raises the count to that row
+ 1 when it is larger (L_CA0F).
Entry: none.
Exit: (IY-97..-96) = number of rows.

3024.synopsis:
Dialog description read by L_D98A for the Insert Page command (L_8BC0): one field, flags
$87, the zero-terminated prompt "Specify no. of unbroken lines", then the bytes $00, $00,
$FF $00 and $81 $00.

3062.synopsis:
Insert Page command (EIP, MthKeyJmpTable entry 44). Asks for the number of unbroken lines
(L_8B9A); B = the number entered when bit 0 of the answer is set, else 0. Inserts a slot of
type $C0, length 2, in column 0 of the current row (L_8CA2) and stores B at its IX+5, then
joins L_8C01 with A = 1 to insert a row in the other columns and adjust the references.
Entry: none.
Error: a failed insert is reported through L_EB07.

3114.synopsis:
Insert Row command (N, MthKeyJmpTable entry 46). Inserts a row at the current row in every
column (L_8C7F from column 0, C = $80: no column skipped), then adjusts the slot references
by one row down (A = $C0, L_B7B0).
Entry: none.
Error: a failed insert is reported through L_EB07.

3140.synopsis:
Insert Row in Column command (EIRC, MthKeyJmpTable entry 45). Inserts an empty text slot
(type $80, L_B8B6) at the current slot, pushing the column's slots below down a row
(L_8CA2), then adjusts the references (A = $80, L_B7B0).
Entry: none.
Error: a failed insert is reported through L_EB07.

3163.synopsis:
Split Line command (ESL, MthKeyJmpTable entry 48). Splits the current text slot at the
cursor position (IY-87), clamped to the line's length: the part before the cursor stays in
the slot (L_B394), the rest goes into a new text slot inserted below it (L_BC66, L_8CA2,
L_B490). Ends the edit (L_B411) and adjusts the references (L_8C20).
Entry: none.
Error: refused while an expression is edited (L_B388); returns when the slot is missing or
not text; a failed conversion or insert is reported through L_EB07.

3253.synopsis:
Inserts a row at row (IY-109..-108) in the columns from A to the last one: in every column
except column C that has a slot at that row (L_D79A), L_8CA5 inserts an empty text slot
(L_B8B6) there.
Entry: A = first column; C = column to skip ($80 for none); (IY-109..-108) = row.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 when an insert fails (out of memory).

3288.synopsis:
Inserts a new slot at column A, row BC: stores the position at (IY-110..-108) (L_D77E) and
falls into L_8CA5.
Entry: A = column; BC = row; (IY-42) = type; (IY-40) = length.
Exit: as L_8CA5.

3291.synopsis:
Inserts a new slot at the position (IY-110..-108) with L_8CAE and, when that succeeds, marks
the sheet changed (L_B3C1).
Entry: position at (IY-110..-108); (IY-42) = type; (IY-40) = length.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 when the slot cannot be made.

3300.synopsis:
Makes a slot at the position (IY-110..-108). When the position is empty, creates it there
(L_B8C7). Otherwise allocates a new slot (L_D920), raises the row count (L_D788, L_CA0E),
links it into the column's list in front of the slot already there (L_BA73, L_BA44, L_B9A8)
and initialises it (L_D8F2), so the column's later slots move down a row.
Entry: position at (IY-110..-108); (IY-42) = type; (IY-40) = length.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 when no memory is left.

3351.synopsis:
Last Column command (CLC, MthKeyJmpTable entry 17): moves the cursor to the last column of
the current row. A = (IY-98), the number of columns, which L_8D30 reduces to the last column
before setting the target (L_8296).
Entry: none.

3362.synopsis:
First Column command (CFC, MthKeyJmpTable entry 16): moves the cursor to column 0 of the
current row through L_8D30.
Entry: none.

3371.synopsis:
Dialog description read by L_D98A for the Go to Slot command (L_8D04): one field, flags $02,
the zero-terminated prompt "Go to slot", then two zero bytes.

3386.synopsis:
Go to Slot command (CGS, MthKeyJmpTable entry 13). Asks for a slot (L_8CF5) and moves the
cursor to the answer's column (IY+56) and row (IY+57..+58) through L_8D30, which keeps the
column inside the sheet.
Entry: none.
Error: returns with Fc = 1 when the dialog is cancelled.

3407.synopsis:
Bottom of Column command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 33): BC = $7FFF and joins L_8D27, which sets
bit 5 of (IY-71) and moves to that row of the current column; L_8296 limits it to the last
row of the sheet.
Entry: none.

3415.synopsis:
Top of Column command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 31): BC = 0, then L_8D27 sets bit 5 of (IY-71)
and moves to row 0 of the current column.
Entry: none.

3451.synopsis:
Clears the cursor position bytes (IY-88) and (IY-87). Also the end of the cursor move path
L_8D30, reached when no expression is edited.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = 0.
Changes: AF.

3459.synopsis:
Restore Position command (CRP, MthKeyJmpTable entry 20). Takes the last saved position off
the stack of saved positions (count in (IY+99), entries from L_8D7B) and moves the cursor
there (L_B4F9, L_8D30). With no saved position, beeps (L_EFE9).
Entry: none.
Error: Fc = 1 after the beep when no position is saved.

3480.synopsis:
Save Position command (CSP, MthKeyJmpTable entry 19). Pushes the current slot's column and
row (L_D0E2) onto the stack of saved positions (3 bytes each, L_8D7B) and increments the
count (IY+99). With 5 positions saved, beeps (L_EFE9) instead.
Entry: none.
Error: Fc = 1 after the beep when the stack is full.

3505.synopsis:
Points HL at entry (IY+99) of the saved-position stack: IY + $54 + 3 * (IY+99).
Entry: (IY+99) = entry number.
Exit: HL = entry; BC = 3 * entry number; A = C.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

3523.synopsis:
Delete Column command (EDC, MthKeyJmpTable entry 41). With more than one column, frees all
slots of the current column (L_BAC8, L_90FE), moves the column entries after it down by one
10-byte entry, decrements the column count (IY-98), calls OS_Pur (L_EB49), adjusts the
references (L_B794) and marks the sheet changed (L_B3C1). Falls into L_8DD5.
Entry: none.

3595.synopsis:
Recounts the rows (L_8B80) and requests a full redraw (L_CA7C, L_CA85).
Entry: none.

3604.synopsis:
Insert Column command (EIC, MthKeyJmpTable entry 47). When fewer than $40 columns exist and
the current column is inside the sheet, moves the column entries from the current one to
entry $3F up by one 10-byte entry, initialises the current entry ($0C then 9 zero bytes,
L_D8D1), adjusts the references (L_B79B) and finishes through L_879F.
Entry: none.
Error: error 5 is reported through L_EB07 when $40 columns exist.

3664.synopsis:
ENTER command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 18). While an expression is edited (bit 6 of (IY-71)),
stores it in its slot (L_B41A; an error is reported through L_EB07), sets bit 1 of (IY-72)
and falls into L_8E2A. Otherwise commits the line being edited (L_B398); when the current
row is the sheet's last, creates an empty text slot in the row below (L_B8C4) and requests a
redraw. Then clears the cursor position (L_8D45) and requests a move one row down (L_8E6D).
Entry: none.

3680.synopsis:
ESCAPE command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 53). When an expression is edited (bit 6 of (IY-71)),
leaves expression editing: clears the bit, ends the line edit (L_B411), requests a redraw
(L_CA73), clears the cursor position (L_8D45) and calls L_EFD5. Otherwise does nothing.
Entry: none.

3736.synopsis:
Cursor Down command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 23): sets bit 4 of (IY-71) and bit 7 of (IY-68),
then requests a move with (IY-100) = 1 and direction (IY-101) = 1.
Entry: none.
Exit: B = 1; C = 1.

3751.synopsis:
Screen Up command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 27): commits any edit (L_B398) and requests a move
with (IY-100) = 2 and direction (IY-101) = 0.
Entry: none.
Exit: B = 2; C = 0.

3758.synopsis:
Screen Down command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 28): commits any edit (L_B398) and requests a move
with (IY-100) = 2 and direction (IY-101) = 1.
Entry: none.
Exit: B = 2; C = 1.

3767.synopsis:
Cursor Up command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 24): sets bit 4 of (IY-71) and bit 7 of (IY-68),
then requests a move with (IY-100) = 1 and direction (IY-101) = 0.
Entry: none.
Exit: B = 1; C = 0.

3789.synopsis:
Cursor Left command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 22). While a line is edited (bit 7 of (IY-72)) and
the cursor position (IY-87) is not 0, moves the cursor one character left. At position 0
does nothing when bit 5 of (IY-70) or bit 6 of (IY-71) is set; otherwise falls into L_8EB1
to move to the previous column.
Entry: none.

3815.synopsis:
Previous Column command (MthKeyJmpTable entry 29): commits any edit (L_B398) and requests a
move with (IY-100) = 1 and direction (IY-101) = 2.
Entry: none.
Exit: B = 1; C = 2.

3822.synopsis:
Move command (BM, MthKeyJmpTable entry 4). Moves the marked block to the current slot.
1. L_9209 requires a marked block and gives C = its width - 1; L_9224 refuses (error $23) a
current column after the block's first and not after its last.
2. For each block column, L_91B2 sets the target (IY-61..-59) and L_9050 moves that column's
slots; the block range (IY-58..-53) is kept on the stack around it.
3. Adjusts the references (L_B7BE with L_B671, offsets from L_919B in (IY-29..-27)), sets
the block range to the destination (L_9161), clears the marks (L_89F8) and finishes through
L_8F92.
Entry: none.

3945.synopsis:
Copy command (BC, MthKeyJmpTable entry 3). Copies the marked block to the current slot.
1. L_9209 requires a marked block and gives C = its width - 1; L_9224 refuses (error $23) a
current column after the block's first and not after its last.
2. For each block column, L_91B2 sets the target (IY-61..-59) and L_8FCD copies that
column's slots; the block range (IY-58..-53) is kept on the stack around it. A failure ends
at L_8FBB.
3. Stores the offsets (L_919B, L_B690), sets the block range to the copy (L_9161), adjusts
the references in it (L_B62E, L_B7BE with L_B69A) and finishes through L_8F92.
Entry: none.

4049.synopsis:
Delete command (BD, MthKeyJmpTable entry 5). Requires a marked block (L_9209), moves the
cursor to its start (L_82A2), deletes its slots column by column (L_908D for (IY-58) up to
(IY-55)), clears the marks (L_89F8) and finishes through L_8FBB: L_D357, marks the sheet
changed (L_B3C1), recounts and redraws (L_8FC1).
Entry: none.

4087.synopsis:
Shared exit of the block commands: recounts the rows and requests a redraw (L_8DD5), then
falls into L_8FC4.
Entry: none.

4090.synopsis:
Sets bits 4 and 1 of (IY-72) (L_B3B8) and runs the recalculation pass L_929B twice.
Entry: none.

4099.synopsis:
Copies the block's slots in source column (IY-58), rows (IY-57..-56) to (IY-54..-53), to the
target (IY-61..-59).
1. L_91DE makes sure a slot exists at the end row; L_9238 finds the start slot.
2. For each slot: L_9128 copies it to the buffer $1DAA, L_D920 and L_D8F2 make a new slot,
which is linked after the previous copy (L_BA44), and L_913E fills it from the buffer.
3. After the end row, L_90B6 links the run of copies into the target column.
Entry: block range at (IY-58..-53); target at (IY-61..-59).
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, the copies made so far freed (L_90FE) and the error reported through L_EB07.

4230.synopsis:
Moves the block's slots in source column (IY-58) to the target (IY-61..-59): makes sure a
slot exists at the block's end row (L_91DE), cuts the run of slots out of the column
(L_91FD, L_91F1, L_90E0) and links it in at the target (L_90B6). When the target is in the
same column below the block, the target row is first reduced by the block's height (L_9183).
Entry: block range at (IY-58..-53); target at (IY-61..-59).
Error: Fc = 1 after the error is reported through L_EB07.

4291.synopsis:
Deletes the block's rows from column (IY-58): cuts the run of slots from the start row to
the end row out of the column's list (L_91F1, L_9244, L_91FD, L_90E0), adjusts the
references (L_B7BE with L_B6F7, BC = minus the block's height) and frees the cut slots
(L_90FE).
Entry: block range at (IY-58..-53).
Exit: bit 7 of (IY-58) clear again.
Error: Fc = 1, nothing done, when there is no slot at the start (L_9238).

4332.synopsis:
Links a run of slots into a column at the target (IY-61..-59). The run's first slot is in
the pointer at (IY+68..+70) and its last in (IY+71..+73). L_BA73 finds the slots before and
at the target; the links between them are undone and the run is linked in between (L_BA44
toggles the XOR links of two slots). Ends in L_B9C6.
Entry: run in (IY+68..+73); target at (IY-61..-59).

4374.synopsis:
Cuts a run of slots out of a column's list. The pointers at (IY+65..+76) hold the slot
before the run, the run's first slot, its last slot and the slot after it; the links before
and after the run are undone and the slots on either side linked to each other (L_BA44
toggles the XOR links of two slots). Ends in L_B9C6.
Entry: pointers at (IY+65..+76).

4404.synopsis:
Frees a chain of slots from HL onwards: for each slot, undoes its link to the next one
(L_BA44), frees its memory with OS_Mfr (L_D95E, size from L_B990) and continues with the
next slot until the link is zero.
Entry: HL, C = address and bank of the first slot, already unlinked from the slot before it.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

4446.synopsis:
Copies the slot's body to the buffer $1DAA: (IY-42) = its type (L_B0C0), (IY-40) = its
length (L_B990, L_B53C), then L_9148 and LDIR.
Entry: slot at (IY-127..-125).
Exit: (IY-42) = type; (IY-40) = length; DE past the copy in $1DAA.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

4468.synopsis:
Copies the buffer $1DAA into the body of the slot at (IY-127..-125) (L_B518, L_9148, LDIR).
Entry: (IY-42) = type; (IY-40) = length.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

4478.synopsis:
Sets up an LDIR between a slot's body and the buffer $1DAA: HL = IX + 4; BC = (IY-40), plus
6 when bit 7 of (IY-42) is clear (a slot that is not text has a 6-byte value first); DE =
$1DAA.
Entry: IX = slot; (IY-40) = length; (IY-42) = type.
Exit: HL = IX + 4; BC = byte count; DE = $1DAA; A = C.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4503.synopsis:
Sets the block range to the destination of a move or copy: start column (IY-58) = (IY-104),
end column (IY-55) = (IY-61), start row (IY-57..-56) = (IY-60..-59), end row (IY-54..-53) =
that row - BC - 1.
Entry: BC = minus the block's height (L_9183).
Changes: AF.

4537.synopsis:
Returns BC = start row - end row - 1 of the block range, (IY-57..-56) and (IY-54..-53):
minus the block's height in rows.
Entry: block range at (IY-58..-53).
Exit: BC = minus the height.
Changes: AF, BC.

4553.synopsis:
Negates BC: BC = 0 - BC.
Entry: BC = the value.
Exit: BC = its negative.
Changes: AF, BC.

4561.synopsis:
Computes how far the scan position, column (iy-61) and row (iy-60)/(iy-59), lies from the
start of the working range, column (iy-58) and row (iy-57)/(iy-56).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = the column difference, Fc from that subtraction; BC = the row difference.
Changes: AF, BC.

4584.synopsis:
Makes sure a slot exists in the cursor's row, B columns right of the cursor's column
(L_D0E2), and makes that the scan position (iy-61), (iy-60)/(iy-59). L_D797 sets the
position and looks the slot up; when there is none, L_B8B6 and L_B8C7 create an empty one.
When B = 0 the position is also recorded through L_82A2.
Entry: B = the column offset; C = the count the caller keeps.
Exit: Fc = 0; BC as on entry.
Error: when the slot cannot be made, jumps to L_EB07 with the entry BC restored, so C is
taken as the message number.

4628.synopsis:
Makes sure a slot exists at the working range's first column (iy-58) and last row
(iy-54)/(iy-53): looks it up with L_9244 and, when there is none, creates an empty one
through L_B8B6 and L_B8C4 (which also set the position (iy-110)-(iy-108)).
Entry: the working range set.
Exit: Fc = 0: the slot exists or was made.
Error: Fc = 1 from L_B8C4; the callers pass C to L_EB07.

4647.synopsis:
Jumps to L_BA73 with the working range's first column and first row: A = (iy-58); BC =
(iy-57)/(iy-56). L_BA73 sets the position (iy-110)-(iy-108) and stores two 3-byte slot-chain
pointers in (iy+65)-(iy+67) and (iy+68)-(iy+70).
Entry: the working range set.

4659.synopsis:
Reads the two 3-byte slot-chain pointers that the column table holds for the working range's
first column (iy-58) (L_BAC8) and stores them in (iy+71)-(iy+73) (L_BAFB) and
(iy+74)-(iy+76) (L_BB19).
Entry: the working range set.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4671.synopsis:
Starts a block command (Copy, Move, Delete block): takes its own return address off the
stack, checks that a command may run (L_B398), loads the marked block into the working range
(L_9250), sets bits 4 and 1 of (iy-72) (L_B3B8) and returns through the saved address.
Because the return address is off the stack, the exits of L_B398 and L_9250 that drop a
return address abandon the calling command.
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = last column - first column of the block; HL = the return address, also kept in
($1D4B).

4697.synopsis:
JP (HL): a CALL here calls the routine whose address is in HL.
Entry: HL = the routine.

4698.synopsis:
Checks a Copy or Move target against the block: compares the cursor's column (L_D0E5) with
the working range's columns. It returns when that column is at or left of the first column
(iy-58) or right of the last (iy-55); otherwise it drops the caller's return address and
reports "Overlap" (C = $23) through L_EB07, which abandons the command.
Entry: the working range set.
Exit: A = the cursor's column.
Changes: AF, HL.

4718.synopsis:
Makes the working range's first column (iy-58) and first row (iy-57)/(iy-56) the position
(iy-110)-(iy-108) and looks the slot up there (jumps to L_D797).
Entry: the working range set.
Exit: Fc = 0: IX = the slot; Fc = 1: there is none.

4730.synopsis:
Looks up the slot at the working range's first column (iy-58) and last row (iy-54)/(iy-53)
(jumps to L_D7AD; the position (iy-110)-(iy-108) is not changed).
Entry: the working range set.
Exit: Fc = 0: IX = the slot; Fc = 1: there is none.

4742.synopsis:
Loads the marked block, (iy-67)-(iy-62) put in order, into the working range (iy-58)-(iy-53)
through L_D014. When no block is marked it reports "No marked block" (C = 9) through L_EB07
and drops its caller's return address, abandoning the caller.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0; the working range set.

4753.synopsis:
The Edit Expression command (MTH code 52, <>X): opens the cursor's slot for editing as an
expression. Returns at once when L_B398 refuses or an expression is already being edited
(bit 6 of (iy-71)). Empties the edit line at ($1D3D) (L_B56E); a slot that exists is
expanded into it through L_BB7B, but a page break slot (bits 7 and 6 of byte 3 set) ends the
command. Falls into L_9276.
Entry: none.

4780.synopsis:
Entry inside L_925B, also called when typing starts an expression: records the cursor's
position (L_D0E2) in (iy-107) (column) and (iy-106)/(iy-105) (row), sets bit 6 of (iy-71)
(an expression is being edited), passes the pointer at ($1D63) to L_CA39, sets the flags of
L_8687 and L_B569, updates the display (L_EF91) and puts the edit cursor at the start
(L_8D45).
Entry: the edit line at ($1D3D) prepared.

4814.synopsis:
The Recalculate command (MTH code 13, <>A): returns when L_B398 refuses, otherwise falls
into L_929B.

4817.synopsis:
Recalculates the sheet. Visits every slot, down each column when bit 4 of (iy-69) is set,
otherwise along each row, through the position (iy-110)-(iy-108), the column stepped by
L_9313. A slot that is not text (bit 7 of byte 3 clear) is evaluated through L_B575 when bit
5 of its byte 3 is set or bit 4 of (iy-72) asks for every slot; a slot with bit 5 set then
goes through L_C9CA. L_EF34 runs between columns or rows. At the end it clears bits 1 and 4
of (iy-72) and restores the status (L_EFBB).
Entry: none.

4937.synopsis:
Steps the column (iy-110) on by one.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = the new column; Fc = 1 when it is past the last column (count in (iy-98)).
Changes: AF.

4948.synopsis:
The New command (MTH code 12, <>BNEW): clears the document after asking. Refused with
"Editing expression" (L_B388) while an expression is being edited; asks "Overwrite text?"
(L_98DC) and returns unless the answer is Y; then clears the document (L_98CD), creates the
default columns (L_D749) and sets bit 7 of (iy-99) (L_CA8D).
Entry: none.

4964.synopsis:
Dialog definition for the Name command, read by L_D98A: control bytes and the field text
"New name of file", zero-terminated.

4985.synopsis:
The Name command (MTH code 60, <>FC): gives the document a new name. Returns when L_B398
refuses or the dialog (NameFilePrompt, L_D98A) is left with Fc = 1. A name that is empty or
only spaces (L_DFD3) removes the name: L_A05A, then bit 3 of (iy-71) cleared. Otherwise the
name at $1FAA becomes the document's (L_ED32), the list file is dropped (L_A05A), the name
is expanded and given to the Index (L_ED3F) and bit 3 of (iy-71) is set.
Entry: none.

5028.synopsis:
Puts the document's name in the filename buffer at $1FAA (L_ED2A copies it from ($1D75))
when it has one (bit 3 of (iy-71) set); otherwise empties the buffer.
Entry: none.
Exit: $1FAA = the name or an empty string.
Changes: F, BC, DE, HL.

5041.synopsis:
