Dialog definition for the Load command, read by L_D98A: control bytes and the field texts
"Name of file to load", "Insert at slot", "Limit to range of rows" and "Load as plain text",
each zero-terminated. The answers come back as bits 0-2 of A.

5129.synopsis:
The Load command (MTH code 58, <>FL): loads a document or a list file.
1. Returns when L_B398 refuses or the dialog (LoadFilePrompt, L_D98A) is left with Fc = 1;
keeps the options in (iy-102): bit 0 insert at slot, bit 1 limit rows, bit 2 plain text.
2. Without insert: asks "Overwrite text?" (L_98DC) when the text has changed (bit 0 of
(iy-71)), makes the typed name the document's (L_ED32), clears the document (L_98CD) and,
for plain text, creates the default columns (L_D749). L_9F34 then looks for a list file of
that name: when one is read, the first file of the list is loaded (L_A019), otherwise the
name itself (L_ED2A).
3. Loads the file (L_9444), reports any error through L_EB07, sets bit 7 of (iy-99) (L_CA8D)
and falls into L_941C.
Entry: none.

5202.synopsis:
Shared exit of the Load command and the loader: creates the default columns (L_D749) when
the sheet has none ((iy-98) = 0).
Entry: AF = the result to return.
Keeps: AF.

5212.synopsis:
Goes to the first file of the list file: returns Fv = 0 at once when the current file
(iy-73) is already the first. Otherwise saves the current file if it has changed (L_999B),
makes entry 0 current with its name in $1FAA (L_A019) and falls into L_9434.
Entry: a list file loaded.
Exit: Fv = 0: the file loaded.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

5226.synopsis:
Entry inside L_9426: restores the current list entry's start values (L_9CB6) and falls into
L_9437.
Entry: (iy-73) = the list entry; its name in $1FAA.

5229.synopsis:
Entry inside L_9426: loads the file named at $1FAA in place of the current one. Frees the
options list and the slots (L_98D6), resets the sheet's variables (L_D6D9), puts the current
list entry's name in $1FAA (L_A01D), clears the load options (iy-102) and falls into L_9444.
The list file stays loaded.
Entry: (iy-73) = the list entry.
Exit: Fv = 0: loaded.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

5242.synopsis:
Loads the file named at $1FAA with the options in (iy-102) (bit 0 insert at slot, bit 1
limit rows, bit 2 plain text).
1. Clears the row counter (iy+3)/(iy+4). Starts at column 0, row 0, or when inserting at the
slot in (iy+56), (iy+57)/(iy+58), which also becomes the working range (L_985D).
2. Opens the file for input with GN_Opf. "File not found" (C = $14) when RC_Onf, any other
error through L_9FFF. Unless inserting, the expanded name becomes the document's (L_ED32).
The handle is kept at ($1D57).
3. Reads each line into the buffer at ($1D3D) through L_9D78, up to $F3 bytes; CR, LF and
the pairs CR LF and LF CR end a line. In plain text a TAB ends a slot and the next slot goes
one column right. Otherwise every "%code%" is looked up (L_973C) and either changes the
slot's type and format in (iy-43)/(iy-44), runs a handler from L_97CE, or stays as text.
4. Stores each slot with L_967B and moves on (next column after a TAB in plain text,
otherwise the next row).
5. At the end restores the status, frees the file buffer (L_9E30), recalculates (L_8FC1) and
closes the file (L_9FE2). A whole load clears the changed flag (bit 0 of (iy-71)), sets the
named flag (bit 3), gives the name to the Index (L_ED3F) and resets the position (L_82A2);
an insert sets the changed flag. A failed whole load drops the list file and the Index name
(L_A05A).
Entry: $1FAA = the name; (iy-102) = the options.
Exit: Fv = 0: loaded.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

5700.synopsis:
A RET. The Next Option command (MTH code 55, <>J) uses it as its handler, so it does nothing
in the sheet; L_967B passes its address to L_B78D as a handler that does nothing. It is also
the end of L_9444.

5809.synopsis:
Stores the slot the loader has read (text at ($1D3D), type (iy-43), format (iy-44)) at the
position (iy-110)-(iy-108).
1. A pending option line ((iy-9) not 0, set by L_98BC) goes to the options list at $1D43
instead (L_960F; not when inserting).
2. With the row limit (bit 1 of (iy-102)) the row counter (iy+3)/(iy+4) is stepped and rows
outside (iy+51)/(iy+52) to (iy+54)/(iy+55) are skipped.
3. Converts the text through L_BC66 unless it is a page break; stores the length in (iy-40)
and the type in (iy-42).
4. Inserting: stores it through L_8CAE and sets the changed flag (L_B3C1); otherwise creates
the slot (L_B8C7), an empty one being skipped. A page break keeps its number in byte 5,
other slots get their text (L_B490), and a slot that is not text its format in byte 9. When
inserting, it then calls L_B7BE (A = 0, BC = 1, L_960E given to L_B78D) with the last column
and row of the working range set to the position. When storing fails and the file buffer can
be given back ((iy-5) not 0), frees it (L_9E30) and tries again.
Entry: the slot read; the position set.
Exit: Fc = 0: stored or skipped.
Error: Fc = 1.

6002.synopsis:
Looks up the format code that the loader found between two '%' signs in the table L_977B.
The code starts after the '%' at (iy-52)/(iy-51); codes need (iy-4) >= 3 (at least one
character). A table name matches when its letters match and the next character is not a
letter (ValidateAlphabetic).
Entry: (iy-52)/(iy-51) = the '%'; (iy-4) = the count.
Exit: Fc = 0: IX = the last letter of the matching entry, (IX+1)-(IX+3) its action; HL = the
character after the code.
Error: Fc = 1: no match.
Changes: AF, HL, IX.

6065.synopsis:
Table of the format codes that the loader (L_973C) understands between '%' signs. Each entry
is the code's letters, the last with bit 7 set, then three bytes: an action and an AND and
an OR mask. An action with bit 7 set is an offset into L_97CE (a handler); otherwise it is
the offset from (iy-44) of the byte that is ANDed and ORed with the masks (offset 1, the
slot type; 0, the format). Codes: V, JL, JR, L, R, C, LCR, P, CO, H, D, B, LC, TC, F, OP, PC
and DF. A zero byte ends it.

6148.synopsis:
Table of 5 words: the handlers of the load codes with an action byte, at offsets 0-8: L_97D8
(CO), L_9878 (H), L_989F (D), L_98BC (OP) and L_9874 (PC).

6158.synopsis:
Load handler of "%CO:col,width,margin%": selects the column the next slots go to. Reads the
column letters (L_BD91) into (iy-110). Without insert: makes sure the column exists (L_D8BF)
and stores the width and the margin, when given (GN_Gdn through L_EE29), in its column table
entry (L_984D); the row restarts at 0. When inserting, columns are placed relative to the
insert column, the first CO setting the base in (iy+56); a column past 63 gives "Edge" (C =
$1D). Clears the row counter (iy+3)/(iy+4).
Entry: HL = the ':' after CO.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0: done; Fv = 0, Fc = 1: not valid, the code stays as text.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

6275.synopsis:
Points HL at the column table entry of the load column (iy-110) (L_D890).
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = the entry.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF.

6291.synopsis:
Makes the working range one slot: first and last column A, first and last row BC. The first
column (iy-58) is stored with bit 7 set.
Entry: A = the column; BC = the row.
Exit: A = the column without bit 7.
Changes: AF.

6314.synopsis:
Load handler of "%PC%": puts a '%' character into the slot text at the code's place (the
pointer (iy-52)/(iy-51), stepped on).
Entry: (iy-52)/(iy-51) = the '%' that opened the code.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0.

6318.synopsis:
Load handler of "%Hn%": puts highlight code n (1-9) into the slot text as the character $17
+ n at the code's place (shares L_988C with L_9874). Reads n with GN_Gdn (L_EE29).
Entry: HL = the text after H.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0: done; Fv = 0, Fc = 1: no number or not 1-9, the code stays as text.

6357.synopsis:
Load handler of "%Dn%": sets the slot's decimal places to n (0-10): (iy-44) keeps bits 7, 5
and 4, takes n in bits 0-3 and sets bit 6.
Entry: HL = the text after D.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0: done; Fv = 0, Fc = 1: no number or above 10, the code stays as text.

6386.synopsis:
Load handler of "%OP%": marks the line as an options line by pointing (iy-10)/(iy-9) at the
character after the code's '%'; L_967B then stores it in the options list.
Entry: (iy-52)/(iy-51) = the '%' that opened the code.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0.

6403.synopsis:
Clears the document: drops the list file and the Index name (L_A05A), frees the options list
and the slots (L_98D6) and resets the sheet's variables (jumps to L_D6CB).
Entry: none.

6412.synopsis:
Frees the options list at $1D43 (L_A072) and the slots of every column (jumps to L_A093).
Entry: none.

6418.synopsis:
Asks "Overwrite text?" on the message line (L_B2C2, OS_Pout) and reads the answer (L_E006),
then clears the line (L_EFD5).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fz = 1: the answer is Y or y; Fz = 0: anything else, or Fc = 1 from L_E006.

6458.synopsis:
Dialog definition for the Save command, read by L_D98A: control bytes and the field texts
"Name of file to save", "Save only range of columns", "Save selection of rows", "Save marked
block" and "Save plain text", each zero-terminated. The answers come back as bits of A (bit
0 columns, bit 1 rows, bit 2 plain text, bit 3 marked block).

6575.synopsis:
Unless bit 3 (marked block) of the save or search options in A is set, sets bit 6, so that
L_B2CC takes the whole sheet instead of the marked block.
Entry: A = the options.
Exit: A = the options.
Changes: AF.

6581.synopsis:
The Save command (MTH code 59, <>FS): returns when L_B398 refuses. Offers the document's
name (L_936E), or the current list entry's when a list file is loaded (L_A01D), in the
dialog (SaveFilePrompt, L_D98A), returns when it is left with Fc = 1, then saves through
L_99AF and reports any error through L_EB07.
Entry: none.

6608.synopsis:
Saves the current file before another is loaded. Puts the current list entry's name in $1FAA
(L_A01D). Returns Fv = 0 when the text has not changed (bit 0 of (iy-71) clear), "No name
for save" (C = $1C) when the document has none (bit 3 of (iy-71) clear); otherwise saves the
whole document (A = 0, falls into L_99AF).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fv = 0: saved or nothing to save.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

6628.synopsis:
Saves the document to the file named at $1FAA with the options in A (bit 0 range of columns,
bit 1 selection of rows, bit 2 plain text, bit 3 marked block).
1. Sets the working range (L_997A, L_B2CC): the marked block (bit 7 then set) or the whole
sheet, limited to (iy+53)-(iy+54) for bit 0; keeps the options in (iy-102). Asking for the
marked block when there is none gives "No marked block" (C = 9).
2. Opens the file for output with GN_Opf (errors through L_9FFF); the handle goes to
($1D57).
3. Unless saving a block or plain text, writes each option of the options list as a line
"%OP%" + its text (L_9CDF, L_9CE4).
4. For each column, unless plain text, writes "%CO:col,width,margin%". Then writes the slots
(L_9B06) row by row, honouring the row selection (L_B30E): in plain text across the columns
with TABs between them and CR at the end of a row; otherwise down the column, a CR after
each slot, until a row without a slot.
5. Flushes the buffer (L_9EC5), frees it (L_9E30), restores the status and closes the file
(L_9FE2). A whole save clears the changed flag (bit 0 of (iy-71)).
Entry: A = the options; $1FAA = the name.
Exit: Fv = 0: saved.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

6971.synopsis:
Writes slot IX to the save file. A page break (bits 7 and 6 of byte 3 set) is "%Pn%" with n
from byte 5, nothing in plain text. Unless plain text, a slot that is not text starts with
"%V%", and the alignment in bits 1-3 of byte 3 is written as its code from L_9BD0. A slot
that is not text then gets the format codes from byte 9: "%B%", "%LC%", "%TC%", and "%Dn%"
or "%DF%" when bit 6 is set. Last, the contents are expanded through L_BB7E with L_9BE2
writing each character ('%' as "%PC%" unless plain text).
Entry: IX = the slot; (iy-102) = the save options.
Exit: Fv = 0: written.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

7141.synopsis:
Writes the two-letter format code C followed by 'C' ("%LC%", "%TC%") when the slot's format
byte (IX+9) has a bit of mask A set (shares the rest of L_9BB4).
Entry: A = the mask; C = the first letter; IX = the slot.
Exit: Fv = 0: written or not needed.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).
Keeps: IX.

7145.synopsis:
Writes the one-letter format code C ("%B%") when the slot's format byte (IX+9) has a bit of
mask A set: puts the code into the code buffer (L_9CCB) and writes it (L_9D00).
Entry: A = the mask; C = the letter; IX = the slot.
Exit: Fv = 0: written or not needed.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).
Keeps: IX.

7164.synopsis:
Reads byte A of the alignment table L_9BD0.
Entry: A = the index.
Exit: A = the byte; HL = its address.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

7173.synopsis:
Table of 18 bytes for the alignment codes. The first 8 bytes give, for each alignment 0-7
(bits 1-3 of a slot's byte 3), the offset in this table of its letters, 0 for none (0 and
5). The letters follow, the last of each code with bit 7 set: L, C, R, LCR, JL, JR.

7234.synopsis:
The Bottom File command (MTH code 64, <>FB): goes to the last file of the list file one file
at a time (L_9C4F) while L_A004 finds a next one. Returns when L_B398 refuses; without a
list file reports "No list file" (L_9C60).
Entry: none.

7250.synopsis:
The Previous File command (MTH code 62, <>FP): loads the file before the current one in the
list file. Returns when L_B398 refuses; "No list file" without one (L_9C60), "End of list"
(L_A00A, C = $1B) at the first file. Saves the current file if it has changed (L_999B),
makes the previous entry current (iy-73) and loads it (L_9434); errors go to L_EB07.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0 when loaded.

7281.synopsis:
The Top File command (MTH code 63, <>FT): goes to the first file of the list file (L_9426).
Returns when L_B398 refuses; "No list file" without one (L_9C60); errors go to L_EB07.
Entry: none.

7294.synopsis:
The Next File command (MTH code 61, <>FN): returns when L_B398 refuses; "No list file"
without one (L_9C60); then falls into L_9C4F.
Entry: none.

7300.synopsis:
Entry inside L_9C49, also used by L_9C0D: goes to the next file of the list file (L_9C6B,
which gives "End of list" after the last) and loads it (L_9437). Errors go to L_EB07.
Entry: a list file loaded.
Exit: Fc = 0 when loaded.

7317.synopsis:
Checks that a list file is loaded (bit 3 of (iy-70)). When not, drops the caller's return
address and reports "No list file" (C = $1A) through L_EB07, abandoning the command.
Entry: none.

7328.synopsis:
Prepares the move to the next file of the list file.
1. Stores the current file's start values (iy+12), (iy+10)/(iy+11) in its list entry
(L_A03C).
2. Finds the next entry (L_A004); without one returns Fc = 1 with C = $1B ("End of list").
3. Saves the current file if it has changed (L_999B).
4. Makes the next entry current in (iy-73), with its name in $1FAA.
5. Works out the next file's start values through L_D3F0 and L_D35D: (iy+12) from (iy-94)
and (iy+10)/(iy+11) from (iy-93)/(iy-92); 0 and one less when L_D35D returns Fc = 1.
Entry: a list file loaded.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0: the next entry is current.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE), C = the message number (0: an OZ error); or Fv = 0, Fc = 1 at the end of
the list.

7403.synopsis:
Restores the current file's start values (iy+12), (iy+10) and (iy+11) from the first three
bytes of its entry ((iy-73)) in the list at $1D41 (L_EA7C).
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

7424.synopsis:
Puts a format code of one or two letters into the code buffer at (iy+35): C, then B when B
is not 0; the length goes to (iy-74).
Entry: C = the first letter; B = the second, or 0.
Exit: C = the length (1 or 2).
Changes: F, C.
Keeps: A, B.

7441.synopsis:
Writes the one-letter format code A as "%A%" (C = A, B = 0, falls into L_9CDF).
Entry: A = the letter.
Exit: Fv = 0: written.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

7444.synopsis:
Writes the format code of letters C and B (B = 0 for one letter) between '%' signs: puts it
into the code buffer (L_9CCB) and writes it (L_9D00).
Entry: C, B = the letters.
Exit: Fv = 0: written.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

7449.synopsis:
Writes character A of a slot's contents to the save file. A highlight code ($18-$1F, L_CE2A)
becomes "%Hn%" with n = A - $17, or nothing in plain text (bit 2 of (iy-102)); any other
character goes to L_9D1A.
Entry: A = the character.
Exit: Fv = 0: written.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

7466.synopsis:
Writes the format code letter A followed by the decimal number C between '%' signs ("%Pn%",
"%Dn%", "%Hn%"): puts A into the code buffer at (iy+35), appends the digits of C (L_EE88)
and falls into L_9D00.
Entry: A = the letter; C = the number.
Exit: Fv = 0: written.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

7477.synopsis:
Writes the code in the code buffer at (iy+35), (iy-74) characters, between two '%' signs
(L_9D18, L_9D1A).
Entry: the code buffer filled.
Exit: Fv = 0: written.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

7501.synopsis:
Writes a '%' to the save file: A = $25, falls into L_9D1A.
Exit: Fv = 0: written.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

7503.synopsis:
Writes character A to the save file through its buffer. In plain text (bit 2 of (iy-102)) a
TAB is not written at once but counted in (iy+5); the counted TABs are written before the
next character that is not a CR, and a CR drops them, so a line carries no trailing TABs.
The buffer at (iy-104)/(iy-103) is filled through (iy-12)/(iy-11), with (iy-8)/(iy-7) bytes
free, and written out with OS_Mv (L_9EC5) when full.
Entry: A = the character.
Exit: Fv = 0: written.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE); C = the PipeDream message number (0: an OZ error).

7549.synopsis:
Writes the byte in A to the file buffer. When no buffer is set up yet ((iy-103) = 0) it sets
one up with L_9E84; when the buffer is full (count (iy-8/-7) = 0) it first writes it to the
file with L_9EC5. Then it stores A at the buffer pointer (iy-12/-11), advances the pointer
and counts the byte off (iy-8/-7).
Entry: A = byte to write.
Exit: Fv = 0; A kept.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE), C = message number (0: OZ error code in A), from the buffer write.
Changes: F, BC, DE, HL, IX.

7597.synopsis:
Reads the next byte from the file buffer. When no buffer is set up ((iy-103) = 0) or its
count (iy-8/-7) is 0, it refills it from the file with L_9DAB. It reads the byte at the
pointer (iy-12/-11), advances the pointer and counts the byte off.
Entry: ($1D57) = file handle.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0: A = byte, Fz = 1 when it is 0; Fv = 0, Fc = 1: end of file.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE), C = message number (0: OZ error code in A).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

7648.synopsis:
Refills the file buffer from the file ($1D57). It sets up a buffer with L_9E84 (a quarter of
the free memory) when there is none, adds the bytes used to the file position (iy-2..+1)
with L_9E53, and moves the file pointer to that position with OS_Fwm (FA_PTR) when OS_Frm
reports a different one. It then reads up to the buffer size (iy-14/-13) with OS_Mv into the
buffer (iy-104/-103), resets the pointer (iy-12/-11) and sets the count (iy-8/-7) to the
bytes read. An end of file during the read is kept in bit 7 of (iy-6); when the position is
unchanged and that bit is set, it returns at once.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0: buffer refilled; Fv = 0, Fc = 1: end of file, nothing read.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE), C = message number (0: OZ error code in A).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

7781.synopsis:
Releases the file buffer when it was allocated with OS_Mal (bit 0 of (iy-5) set). It adds
the bytes used to the file position with L_9E53, clears (iy-103) and (iy-5) and jumps to
L_D976 to free the memory. L_D976 frees the block addressed by (iy-117/-116), so the buffer
address loaded into HL here is not used.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX.

7816.synopsis:
Adds the bytes used in the file buffer (L_9E75) to the 32-bit file position at (iy-2),
(iy-1), (iy+0), (iy+1).
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = 0; HL = high word of the new position.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

7850.synopsis:
Works out how many bytes of the file buffer are used: the pointer (iy-12/-11) minus the
start (iy-104/-103).
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = bytes used.
Changes: AF, BC.

7865.synopsis:
Sets up the file buffer. It asks OS_Nq NQ_Mfs for the free memory and takes DE as the size,
a quarter of it (D shifted right twice) when Fc = 1 on entry. When the high byte is not 0 it
allocates that size with L_D96E (OS_Mal) and sets bit 0 of (iy-5); otherwise it uses the
256-byte area at $1EAA and clears (iy-5). It stores the size in (iy-14/-13) and the start in
(iy-104/-103) and the pointer (iy-12/-11).
Entry: Fc = 1 to use a quarter of the free memory.
Exit: HL = buffer start.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

7930.synopsis:
Writes the used part of the file buffer to the file ($1D57) with OS_Mv and resets the buffer
pointer (iy-12/-11) to the start (iy-104/-103). The count (iy-8/-7) and the file position
are not changed.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE), C = message number (0: OZ error code in A).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.
Keeps: IX.

7964.synopsis:
Resets the file state before a file is opened: clears the flags (iy-6) and (iy-5), the file
position (iy-2..+1), the buffer start's high byte (iy-103), the count (iy+5) and the file
handle ($1D57).
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

7996.synopsis:
Reads one line from the file with OS_Gb into the buffer at $1DAA. A CR or a 0 ends the line
and is stored as 0.
Entry: IX = file handle.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0: line read, C = its length with the terminator, HL = its 0 Fv = 0, Fc =
1: end of file; HL = the byte after the last one stored.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE), C = message number (0: OZ error code in A); C = $18 when the line
reaches 50 bytes.
Changes: AF, C, DE, HL.

8041.synopsis:
Loads the list of files that goes with the file name at ($1D75). It frees the old list
(L_A05A) and copies the name to $1FAA (L_ED2A). When the name's extension is the single
letter L, or the name with the extension "l" (L_9FE0) does not exist, it returns Fc = 1.
Otherwise it opens that file (GN_Opf) and reads it line by line (L_9F07), adding each line
as an entry of the list at $1D41 (L_EA9C) numbered from 0 in (iy+13). It sets bit 3 of
(iy-70) (list loaded) and closes the file through L_9FE6.
Entry: ($1D75) = file name.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 1: no list file; Fv = 0, Fc = 0: list loaded.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE), C = message number (0: OZ error code in A); C = $18 when the last line
has no end.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

8213.synopsis: The file name extension of a list file: "l" and a 0, written by L_9F34 with GN_Esa.

8215.synopsis:
Closes the file whose handle is in ($1D57) with GN_Cl. L_9FE6 is the entry for a handle
already in IX. Nothing is closed when the handle is 0.
Entry: none (L_9FE6: IX = handle).
Exit: AF and BC as on entry.
Error: Fv = 1 and C = 0 when GN_Cl fails, A and the other flags as on entry.
Changes: IX.

8244.synopsis:
Shared error exit for an OZ error: sets C = 0 and Fv = 1 through L_F9B7, keeping the OZ
error code in A.
Entry: A = OZ error code.
Exit: Fv = 1, C = 0.
Changes: F, C.

8249.synopsis:
Looks up the next entry of the file list ((iy-73) + 1) through L_A020 and copies its name to
$1FAA. (iy-73) is not changed.
Entry: (iy-73) = current entry.
Exit: Fc = 1: A = the next entry's number, name at $1FAA Fc = 0: no such entry, C = $1B.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

8255.synopsis:
Looks up the previous entry of the file list ((iy-73) - 1) through L_A020 and copies its
name to $1FAA; returns Fc = 0, C = $1B at once when the current entry is 0. (iy-73) is not
changed.
Entry: (iy-73) = current entry.
Exit: Fc = 1: A = the previous entry's number, name at $1FAA Fc = 0: no such entry, C = $1B.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

8270.synopsis:
Makes entry 0 the current entry of the file list ((iy-73) = 0); falls into L_A01D.
Entry: none.
Exit: as L_A020.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

8274.synopsis:
Copies the name of the current entry of the file list ((iy-73)) to $1FAA; falls into L_A020.
Entry: (iy-73) = current entry.
Exit: as L_A020.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

8277.synopsis:
Finds entry C of the file list at $1D41 (L_EA7C) and copies its name, from the entry's
offset 8, to $1FAA.
Entry: C = entry number.
Exit: Fc = 1: name copied Fc = 0: no such entry, C = $1B.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

8305.synopsis:
Stores (iy+12), (iy+10) and (iy+11) in the three bytes at offset 5 of the current entry of
the file list ((iy-73)). It does not check that the entry exists.
Entry: (iy-73) = current entry.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

8326.synopsis:
Loads C with the current entry of the file list ((iy-73)); falls into L_A054.
Entry: none.
Exit: C = (iy-73); B = 0; HL = $1D41.
Changes: BC, HL.

8329.synopsis:
Sets B = 0 and HL = $1D41, the head of the file list.
Entry: none.
Exit: B = 0; HL = $1D41.
Changes: B, HL.

8335.synopsis:
Frees the file list. It clears bit 3 of (iy-70) (list loaded), sets the application name to
an empty one with DC_Nam, and when the list at ($1D41) is not empty clears ($1D42) and frees
its entries one by one with L_D976 (L_A07C), each entry holding the next one's address in
its first word and its size at offset 2.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

8359.synopsis:
Frees the list whose head is at ($1D43) the same way as L_A05A frees the file list: clears
($1D44) and frees each entry with L_D976 (L_A07C). Does nothing when the list is empty.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

8418.synopsis:
The Search command's dialog for L_D98A: the prompt "String to search for" and the options
"Search only range of columns", "Equate upper and lower case", "Search only marked block",
"Search from current file" and "Search all files in list", each with its control bytes.

8585.synopsis:
The Search command (<>BSE). It asks for the search string and options (L_A0AD through
L_D98A), prepares the search with L_A2CB and goes into the search loop: L_A743 looks for the
next match and L_A2A3 puts the cursor on it. When the sheet has no more matches and the
options name the file list, L_A318 loads the next file of the list and the search goes on;
when there is none, L_A19C shows the number found. Errors are reported with L_EB07.
Entry: none.

8603.synopsis:
The Next Match command (<>BNM). It reports message 8 through L_EB07 when no search string is
set up (bit 6 of (iy+29) clear). Otherwise it starts one character after the cursor ((iy-87)
+ 1), or past the end of the slot when the current slot is not text, and enters the Search
command's loop (inside L_A154).
Entry: none.

8657.synopsis:
Shows the number of matches found ((iy+30/31), through L_EE7C) followed by " found", sets
(iy-84) = $0B and leaves through L_EFE9.
Entry: none.

8685.synopsis:
The Replace command's dialog for L_D98A: the prompts "String to search for" and "Replace
with" and the options "Search only range of columns", "Equate upper and lower case", "Ask
for confirmation", "Search only marked block" and "Search all files in list", each with its
control bytes.

8863.synopsis:
The Replace command (<>BRP). It asks for the strings and options (L_A1B9 through L_D98A),
prepares with L_A2CB, then finds each match with L_A743 and replaces it with L_A34A. When
the sheet has no more matches and the options name the file list, it moves on to the next
file of the list (L_A33B, L_A318). At the end L_A19C shows the number found; errors are
reported with L_EB07. It leaves through L_A33B and L_929B.
Entry: none.

8919.synopsis:
Puts the cursor on a match: stores the slot as the current one with L_82A6, sets the offset
in the slot (iy-87) to the match start (iy-123/-122) less the slot's text address (0 when
the slot is not text), clears (iy-88) and sets bit 7 of (iy-100).
Entry: A = column; BC = row of the slot with the match.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

8959.synopsis:
Prepares a search or a replace from the dialog's options. It stores the options in (iy+34)
(bit 6 added by L_997A when bit 3 is clear), clears the found flag (bit 0 of (iy+29)) and
the number found (iy+30/31). When the options name the file list (bits 1 or 4) it needs a
loaded list, and unless bit 4 is set it loads the list's first file (L_9426). Then L_A2FE
sets up the range.
Entry: A = options from the dialog.
Exit: Fc = 0: A = column; C, B = row of the range's first slot.
Error: Fc = 1, C = message: $17 for options bits 7 and 1 together, $1A for no list loaded;
Fv = 1 also when loading the first file fails.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

9010.synopsis:
Entry inside L_A2CB: shows status $1B (L_EF80), sets up the range of slots from the options
(iy+34) with L_B2CC and clears the offset (iy-44).
Entry: (iy+34) = options.
Exit: Fc = 0: A = (iy-58) column; C, B = (iy-57/-56) row of the range's first slot.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

9036.synopsis:
Moves the search on to the next file of the file list: L_9C6B steps to the next entry,
L_9437 loads it and L_A2FE sets up the range again.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fv = 0, Fc = 0: A = column; C, B = row of the range's first slot Fv = 0, Fc = 1: no
next file.
Error: Fv = 1 (PE), C = message number (0: OZ error code in A).

9051.synopsis:
Decides whether a search goes on to the next file of the file list. It returns Fc = 1 when
no list is loaded (bit 3 of (iy-70)), when option bit 7 is set, when neither option bit 1
nor 4 is set, or when Escape was pressed (L_F023).
Entry: (iy+34) = options.
Exit: Fc = 0: go on to the next file; Fc = 1: stop.
Changes: AF.

9071.synopsis:
Sets display and state flags after a search moved between files: L_CA8D, L_B411, L_B3C1 and
L_8B80, then L_CA7C.
Entry: none.

9086.synopsis:
Replaces one match. It puts the cursor on it (L_A5A2) and stores the slot in (iy+2..+4).
With option bit 5 (ask for confirmation) it shows "Replace: N, Y?" and reads a key: on
Escape it returns Fc = 1, C = 4; on any key but Y it sets (iy-44) to the offset of the
match's end and returns. Otherwise (L_A3AD) it rebuilds the slot's text in the line buffer
at ($1D3D): the text before the match, then the replace string at ($1D6B), whose tokens (a 0
and a code) are run through the table L_A5D0, with the letter case following the found text
when option bit 2 is set.
Entry: A = column; C, B = row of the match.
Exit: Fc = 0: A = column; BC = row to go on searching from, (iy-44) = offset in it.
Error: Fc = 1, C = message.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

9371.synopsis:
Replace token 2 (^R), entered with DE at the token's 0: when the line buffer has no room for
4 more bytes it leaves with C = $1E through L_A4A0. After "#" and a number it adds that
reference found by the search (list at $1DAA, L_A5DE), otherwise the 4-byte slot reference
that follows. Goes on with the next byte of the replace string (L_A44F).

9434.synopsis:
Replace token 4 (^#n), entered with DE at the token's 0: adds the text that wildcard n
matched (list at $1DAA+$48, L_A5DE) to the line buffer with L_A662. Goes on with the next
byte of the replace string.

9454.synopsis:
Replace token 6 (^?n), entered with DE at the token's 0: adds the character that
single-character wildcard n matched (list at $1DAA+$33, L_A5DE) to the line buffer with
L_A662. Goes on with the next byte of the replace string.

9470.synopsis:
Replace token 8 (^S), entered with DE at the token's 0: adds a space to the line buffer with
L_A680. Goes on with the next byte of the replace string.

9478.synopsis:
Replace token 12 (^1 to ^9), entered with DE at the token's 0: adds the byte that follows
the code to the line buffer with L_A680. Goes on with the next byte of the replace string.

9486.synopsis:
Replace token 0, entered with DE at the token's 0: adds nothing and goes on with the next
byte of the replace string.

9528.synopsis:
Replace token 10, the end of the replace string. It skips the found text up to the match's
end (L_A63E, L_A5FB), copies the rest of the slot's text after the match into the line
buffer (4 bytes for a reference), writes the buffer back with L_A6B0, and sets the match
start (iy-123/-122) and (iy-44) to the end of the replaced text so that the search goes on
after it.
Exit: Fc = 0: A = column; BC = row of the slot.
Error: Fc = 1, C = message (through L_A4A0 or L_A49E).

9644.synopsis:
When the replace added or removed slots ((iy-3) not 0), sets (iy-58..-56) to the match's
slot (iy+2..+4) with bit 7 set in the column, calls L_B7B9 with BC = (iy-3) sign-extended
and L_CA8D.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC.

9685.synopsis:
Puts the cursor on the match with L_A2A3 and, with option bit 5 (ask for confirmation),
shows it (L_929B, L_BE08). It calls L_B411 and keeps (iy-60/-59).
Entry: A = column; BC = row of the match.
Exit: A = column; BC = row, as on entry.
Changes: F, DE, HL, IX.

9731.synopsis:
Table of 7 words: the handler of each replace string token (L_A34A), indexed by the token's
code 0, 2, ... 12: L_A4DB, L_A468 (^R), L_A4A7 (^#n), L_A4BB (^?n), L_A4CB (^S), L_A505
(end) and L_A4D3 (^1 to ^9).

9745.synopsis:
Finds entry A of one of the lists the search fills at $1DAA: C = $00 for references, $33 for
single characters, $48 for wildcard texts. Each list starts with its count of entries; each
entry ends with a 0.
Entry: A = entry number from 0; C = the list's offset.
Exit: Fc = 0: BC = address of the entry; Fc = 1: no such entry.
Changes: AF, BC.
Keeps: DE, HL.

9774.synopsis:
Takes the next byte of the found text at HL for the replace, counting the bytes of a slot
reference in (iy-44). At the end of a slot's text inside the match, it writes the line
buffer out (L_A6B0) and returns Fv = 1 to tell its caller to start again on the next slot;
when that fails it drops its caller and leaves through L_A49E.
Entry: HL = text address.
Exit: A = byte; HL = past it; Fc = 1 when the match's end is reached (L_A63E); Fv = 1 at a
slot change.
Changes: AF, C, HL.

9841.synopsis:
Compares the position in the found text (row (iy+3/+4), address HL) with the match's end
(row (iy-9/-8), address (iy-120/-119)).
Entry: HL = text address.
Exit: Fc = 1 when the position is at or past the match's end; A kept.
Changes: F, C.

9877.synopsis:
Adds A to the line buffer with L_A680, adjusting the case of a letter when case matching is
on ((iy-13) not 0): the letter is made lower case unless (iy-12) is not 0, in which case it
is made upper case and (iy-12) is counted down. Falls into L_A680.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: as L_A680.
Changes: AF.

9907.synopsis:
Adds A to the line buffer at ($1D3D) + (iy-40) and counts it in (iy-40). The buffer holds
245 bytes; when it is full the byte that follows is set to 0 and, when bit 7 of (iy-42) is
set, the buffer is written out to a new slot with L_A6FB; otherwise it fails.
Entry: A = byte.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1: C = $15 when the buffer is full and bit 7 of (iy-42) is clear; BC as on entry
when L_A6FB fails.
Keeps: DE, HL.

9955.synopsis:
Writes the line buffer out to a new slot (L_A6FB), then removes the match's slot (iy+2..+4)
with L_8B61 and counts down (iy-3) and the rows (iy-11/-10), (iy-9/-8) and (iy-60/-59). It
sets (iy-42) to the type byte of the slot now at (iy+2..+4).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, C = message.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10030.synopsis:
When the line buffer holds text ((iy-40) not 0), inserts a slot at column (iy+2), row
(iy-11/-10) with L_8CA2, copies the buffer into it (L_B493) and empties the buffer. It
counts the slot in (iy-3), moves the rows (iy-11/-10) and (iy-60/-59) on by one and sets
bits 0 of (iy-42) and 3 of (iy-72).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, C = 1 when the slot cannot be inserted.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10102.synopsis:
Looks for the next match of the search string at ($1D69) from the slot A, BC and the offset
(iy-44), within the range set by the options (iy+34).
1. It returns Fc = 1 when the slot is outside the range's columns or rows.
2. It finds the start address in the slot's text (L_A8C5) and clears the three lists of
found references, characters and wildcard texts at $1DAA.
3. It tries the string word by word with L_A901, skipping spaces in both, moving one text
item on (L_A8BB) when it fails, and to the next slot of the range (L_FB93, L_A8C4) at the
end of a slot's text.
4. On a match it sets bit 0 of (iy+29), counts the match in (iy+30/31) and stores the start
(iy-123/-122) and the last byte (iy-120/-119).
Entry: A = column; BC = row; (iy-44) = offset in the slot.
Exit: Fc = 0: A = column; C, B = row of the slot with the match Fc = 1: no more matches.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10459.synopsis:
Copies the current slot (iy-110..-108) to (iy-61..-59).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = column; C, B = row.
Changes: A, BC.

10478.synopsis:
Moves HL past one item of a slot's text: 4 bytes for a slot reference (A in $10-$13,
L_FE32), 1 byte otherwise.
Entry: A = byte at HL; HL = text address.
Exit: HL = next item.
Changes: F, HL.

10488.synopsis:
Finds the text of the slot (iy-61..-59) at offset A.
Entry: A = offset in the text.
Exit: Fc = 0: HL = text address; IX = slot; B = size of the slot's header; C = type bits
7-6; Fz = 1 when the offset is 0 Fc = 1: no such slot, or its type bits 7-6 are both set.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10532.synopsis:
Search token 4 (^#), entered with DE at the token's code: starts a wildcard. It opens a new
entry of the wildcard text list (L_AA66; none when the list is full), sets bit 7 of C
(wildcard open) and bit 0 when there is an entry, then goes on through L_A909.

10548.synopsis:
Tries to match the search string at DE against the text at HL. L_A909 is the restart point
for a wildcard: it keeps the text address after the current item (iy-40/-39) and the string
address (iy-42/-41). For each byte of the string it compares the text character (upper case
with option bit 2, L_AAA5) or runs a token through the table L_AA97. On a mismatch after a
wildcard, it adds the text character to the wildcard text and starts again after it.
Entry: DE = search string; HL = text address.
Exit: Fz = 1, Fc = 1: the whole string matched; HL = past the match Fz = 1, Fc = 0: matched
up to a space in the string Fz = 0, A = 1: no match.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10611.synopsis:
Search token 0 (^B): matches only when HL is at the start of the slot's text (L_B500); goes
on through L_A9EE.

10628.synopsis:
Search token 2 (^R): the text item must be a slot reference. After "#" any reference matches
and is stored in the reference list at $1DAA (L_AA7C, L_AA47); otherwise its 3 bytes must
equal those that follow in the string.

10686.synopsis:
Search token 12 (^1 to ^9): compares the byte after the code with the text character through
L_A999.

10694.synopsis:
Search token 8 (^S): fails at the end of the text, otherwise compares a space with the text
character through L_A999.

10760.synopsis:
Search token 6 (^?): matches any character but a space and stores it in the single-character
list at $1DAA+$33 (L_AA71, L_AA53).

10807.synopsis:
Search token 10, the end of the search string. It reports a match (L_AA20: Fz = 1, Fc = 1)
when an item matched since the last restart (bit 1 of C); with a wildcard open (bit 7 of C)
it adds a non-space text character to the wildcard and tries again; otherwise no match.

10841.synopsis:
Closes an open wildcard: when bit 7 of C is set, ends its text entry with a 0 (L_AA33) when
bit 0 is set, and clears bits 7 and 0 of C.
Entry: C = match state.
Changes: C (and AF when an entry is ended).

10854.synopsis:
Sets A = 0; falls into L_AA34, which adds A to the wildcard text list at $1DAA + (iy-7) and
moves (iy-7) on (a 0 is stored instead once (iy-7) reaches $FE).
Exit: Fc = 1 when the list is full.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

10855.synopsis:
Entry inside the pattern matcher (L_AA33 sets A = 0 and falls in here): appends A to the
third list of the match buffer at $1DAA, at index (iy-7), and increments (iy-7). When the
index is already $FE or more it stores 0 instead of A. Shares its tail with L_AA47 and
L_AA53.
Entry: A = byte to append; (iy-7) = index.
Exit: A = index used; Fc = 1 when the list was full and 0 was stored.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

10874.synopsis:
Appends A to the first list of the match buffer at $1DAA at index (iy-9) and increments
(iy-9). No limit is checked here: L_AA7C makes room first.
Entry: A = byte to append; (iy-9) = index.
Exit: A = index used.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

10886.synopsis:
Appends A to the second list of the match buffer at $1DAA at index (iy-8) and increments
(iy-8). No limit is checked here: L_AA71 makes room first.
Entry: A = byte to append; (iy-8) = index.
Exit: A = index used.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

10905.synopsis:
Checks that the third list of the match buffer at $1DAA has room ((iy-7) below $FD) and,
when it has, increments its count byte at $1DAA+$48.
Entry: (iy-7) = next index of the list.
Exit: Fc = 0 when the count was incremented; Fc = 1 when the list is full (nothing changed).
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

10916.synopsis:
Checks that the second list of the match buffer at $1DAA has room ((iy-8) below $45) and,
when it has, increments its count byte at $1DAA+$33.
Entry: (iy-8) = next index of the list.
Exit: Fc = 0 when the count was incremented; Fc = 1 when the list is full (nothing changed).
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

10927.synopsis:
Checks that the first list of the match buffer at $1DAA has room ((iy-9) below $2D) and,
when it has, increments its count byte at $1DAA+0.
Entry: (iy-9) = next index of the list.
Exit: Fc = 0 when the count was incremented; Fc = 1 when the list is full (nothing changed).
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

10946.synopsis:
Returns HL pointing at byte A of the match buffer at $1DAA.
Entry: A = offset.
Exit: HL = $1DAA + A.
Changes: F, DE, HL.

10954.synopsis:
Table of 7 words: the handlers the pattern matcher jumps to (at L_A921) when the pattern
holds a 0 byte; the byte after it is the byte offset into this table (0, 2, ... 12). The
handlers are L_A940, L_A951, L_A8F1, L_A9D5, L_A993, L_AA04 and L_A98B.

10968.synopsis:
Converts A to upper case (GetUppercase) when bit 2 of (iy+34) is set; otherwise returns it
as it is. The pattern matcher compares both sides through it.
Entry: A = character; (iy+34) = options.
Exit: A = character, upper case when bit 2 of (iy+34) is set.

10976.synopsis:
Option list of the Print command (PrintCommand), read by L_D98A: control bytes and the
zero-terminated texts "Print only range of columns", "Select rows to print" and "Wait
between pages", closed by $84, $00.

11052.synopsis:
The Print command (<>PO, command table entry 83): stores a pending edit (L_B398), asks for
the options of PrintPrompt (L_D98A; returns when cancelled), sets the block to print with
L_B2CC, keeps the options in (iy-46) and prints through L_AB10, reporting an error it
returns with L_EB07.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1 when cancelled or after a reported error.

11075.synopsis:
Prints the block (iy-58..-53) row by row for PrintCommand, with the options in (iy-46).
1. Saves SP in ($1D59), sets bits 6 and 0 of (iy-70) and starts the output (L_ED6C).
2. Clears the page state: (iy-85) = 0, line count (iy-86) = 1, page number (iy-91..-90) = 1;
when the whole sheet is printed (bit 7 of (iy-46) clear) the page number comes from
(iy+10..11), and with bit 3 of (iy-70) set L_9426 is run first.
3. For each row from L_FBBD on: skips it when "Select rows to print" (bit 1 of (iy-46)) is
set and L_B30E rejects it, otherwise prints it with L_ABC6; stops on Escape (L_F023).
4. With bit 3 of (iy-70) set and no marked block, continues through L_9C6B and L_9437 and
prints again from step 2; finally ends the page (L_AD32) and leaves through L_ABBB.
Entry: (iy-46) = options from L_B2CC; block in (iy-58..-53).
Exit: Fc = 0 when the run ends; Fc = 1 after an error was reported (L_EB07).

11246.synopsis:
Shared exit of the print run: acknowledges Escape (L_E097), ends the output (L_ED53), puts
the row-selection expression back to its first row (L_B363) and returns Fc = 0.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.

11257.synopsis:
Prints row (iy-60..-59) of the block for L_AB10. When column 0 of the row holds a slot with
flag bits 7 and 6 both set (L_D24C), it is not printed but handled as a page control through
L_D263 and L_AC9D. Otherwise it starts a new page when needed (L_AC9D), resets the page
number (L_AC84), prints the left margin (L_AD28) and each column from (iy-58) to (iy-55)
(L_C917, L_D54A, L_D797, L_C9B8, L_CB0E, L_EDE6, L_C5EA), sends (iy+8) carriage returns
(L_AD1B) and advances the line count (iy-86) with L_D28D. Bit 6 of (iy-72) is set while the
row is printed.
Entry: (iy-60..-59) = row; (iy-61) = first column.
Exit: Fc = 1 when the page change was abandoned (Escape at the "Page" wait); Fc = 0
otherwise.

11447.synopsis:
Clears bit 0 of (iy-85); when that bit was set, also copies the start page number
(iy+10..11) into the page number (iy-91..-90).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = the old bit 0 of (iy-85).
Changes: AF.

11472.synopsis:
Page change of the print run; does nothing when the page length (iy+7) is 0. When a page is
open (bit 7 of (iy-85)) it ends it (L_AD37), increments the page number (L_D2BB, then L_D315
on Fc = 1) and returns when C is not 0. Otherwise, or with C = 0, it opens a new page: sets
bit 7 of (iy-85); with "Wait between pages" (bit 2 of (iy-46)) it shows "Page n.." and waits
for a key (L_E006), where C clears the option and any key other than M restarts the output
(L_ED6C); then it prints option $0F carriage returns, the header text of option $14 (L_AD6D)
and option $10 carriage returns.
Entry: C = 0 to open a new page after ending one, other values to end the page only.
Exit: Fc = 1 when Escape was pressed at the wait; Fc = 0 otherwise.

11596.synopsis:
Sends A carriage returns ($0D) to the print output through L_ED93; nothing when A = 0.
L_AD1E is the same loop for the character in A, C times.
Entry: A = count.
Exit: C = 0; A = $0D.
Changes: AF, C.

11609.synopsis:
Sends the number of spaces given by page-layout option $13 (read with L_E790) to the print
output, through the loop in L_AD1B.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, C.

11619.synopsis:
Ends the current page when one is open (bit 7 of (iy-85)); falls into L_AD37.
Entry: none.

11624.synopsis:
Ends the current page of the print run. When the text of option $15 is not empty (L_E54F,
L_E8C3) it sends carriage returns to reach the end of the page (option $11, plus the lines
left from the page length (iy+7) and the line count (iy-86)) and prints that text (L_AD6D).
Then it sends a form feed ($0C), clears bit 7 of (iy-85) and sets the line count (iy-86) to
1.
Entry: none.

11678.synopsis:
Prints the header or footer text at HL. Returns Fc = 1 at once when the text is empty or
only spaces (L_E8C3). With a page number (iy-91..-90) other than 0 it stores HL in ($1D4D),
prints the left margin (L_AD28), adds up the widths of the block's columns (L_D54A, L_D551)
into (iy-36) and prints the text through L_CE31, L_CBD9 and L_EDE6. It ends with one
carriage return (L_AD1B).
Entry: HL = zero-terminated text.
Exit: Fc = 1 when the text was empty.

11764.synopsis:
Option list of the Sort command (SortBlock), read by L_D98A: control bytes and the
zero-terminated texts "Sort on column", "Sort in reverse order" and "Don't update
references".

11833.synopsis:
The Sort command (<>BSO, command table entry 6): sorts the rows of the marked block on one
column.
1. Stores a pending edit (L_B398) and runs L_9250; makes sure every column of the block has
a slot on its last row (L_B8B6, L_B8C7), reporting an error that fails.
2. Asks for SortColumnPrompt (L_D98A; returns when cancelled): the options go to (iy-44) and
the key column from (iy+53) to (iy-46). Returns when the block has only one row.
3. Sorts with a gap that is halved each pass (a Shell sort; gap in (iy+3..4)), comparing and
exchanging rows with L_AF08, then finishes with L_8FC4 and L_EFBB.
Entry: block in (iy-58..-53).

12059.synopsis:
Gets the sort key of row BC: the slot in the key column (iy-46), through L_FA07. Rows whose
column 0 holds a slot with flag bits 7 and 6 both set (L_D24C) have no key.
Entry: BC = row.
Exit: P/V = 1 (pe) when the row has no key; otherwise P/V = 0, Fc = 1 for a text key (HL, B
locate it) and Fc = 0 for a numeric one (in the FPP registers), C = the key's type.

12089.synopsis:
Compares the sort keys of rows (iy-28..-27) and (iy-103..-102) and exchanges the two rows
with L_AF97 when they are out of order. A first row without a key is passed over by moving
(iy-28..-27) down to the next row with one. Numbers compare with Fp_cmp, text with L_F7DF;
keys of different types are ordered by type; bit 1 of (iy-44) (reverse order) inverts the
result.
Entry: (iy-28..-27), (iy-103..-102) = rows; (iy-46) = key column.
Exit: Fc = 1 when the rows were exchanged, or a row without a key ended the comparison; Fc =
0 when they were in order.

12232.synopsis:
Exchanges the slots of rows (iy-28..-27) and (iy-103..-102) in every column of the block,
from (iy-58) to (iy-55) (L_D797, L_D7AD, L_B0B9 and the slot-list routines L_BAC8 to
L_BB69). Unless bit 0 of (iy-44) ("Don't update references") is set, it then runs L_B052
over the references of every slot of the sheet, so that references to either row follow the
exchange.
Entry: rows in (iy-28..-27) and (iy-103..-102).

12500.synopsis:
Compares the two bytes at HL with (IX+1) and (IX+2) (a row number against a reference's
row).
Entry: HL = row word; IX = reference minus 1.
Exit: Fz = 1 when both bytes are equal.
Changes: AF, HL.

12511.synopsis:
Compares row BC with the last row of the block (iy-54..-53).
Entry: BC = row.
Exit: Fc = 1 when BC is lower; Fz = 1 when it is equal.
Changes: AF.

12522.synopsis:
Gets the flag byte of the current slot through L_B0C0 and writes it back to (IX+3), clearing
bit 6 when L_B0C0 does.
Entry: (iy-127..-125) = current slot.
Exit: IX = slot; A = new flag byte.
Changes: AF, C, IX.

12529.synopsis:
Returns the flag byte (IX+3) of the current slot (L_B518), with bit 6 cleared when bits 7-6
are %01 and (IX+4) is 0. The slot itself is not changed.
Entry: (iy-127..-125) = current slot.
Exit: IX = slot; A = C = flag byte.
Changes: AF, C, IX.

12554.synopsis:
Option list of the Replicate command (L_B103), read by L_D98A: control bytes and the
zero-terminated texts "Range to copy from" and "Range to copy to".

12596.synopsis:
The Replicate command (<>BRE, command table entry 2): copies a range of slots over another
range, adjusting the references of each copy.
1. Stores a pending edit (L_B398) and asks for L_B0D9 (L_D98A; returns when cancelled).
Copies the "from" range (iy+53..58) to (iy-4..+1) and the "to" range (iy+59..64) to the
block (iy-58..-53).
2. Measures both with L_B29D; reports "bad range" ($0E) when one is reversed. A single
target slot is widened to the source's size ("Edge", $1D, past the sheet's limits); a
one-row source over a one-column target (or the other way) repeats the source along it (bit
0 of (iy-13)); other shapes are a bad range.
3. For each target position (L_FBBD) copies the source slot (L_9128, L_B8C4, L_913E), stores
the offset (iy-32..-30) and adjusts the copy's references (L_B6FF with L_B6D7); Escape stops
($04). Ends with L_B411, L_EFD5, L_EFBB and L_8FBE.
Entry: none.

13006.synopsis:
Measures the range held at IX+3 (first column, first row word) and IX+6 (last column, last
row word).
Entry: IX = range minus 3.
Exit: Fc = 1; A = E = last column minus first; BC = last row minus first; D bit 7 = more
than one column, D bit 6 = more than one row.
Error: Fc = 0 when the last column is before the first.
Changes: AF, BC, DE.

13043.synopsis:
Runs L_EFD5, then moves the cursor to column $28 of line 0 with the SOH 3 @ sequence
(L_EEE4).
Entry: none.

13053.synopsis:
Sets the block (iy-58..-53) for a command from its options in A. With bit 6 of A set, or
when no block is marked (L_D014), it is the whole sheet: columns 0 to (iy-98)-1, rows 0 to
(iy-97..-96)-1. Otherwise it is the marked block, copied by L_D014. With bit 0 of A set, the
first and last columns are then taken from (iy+53) and (iy+54).
Entry: A = options.
Exit: A = options, with bit 7 set when the marked block is used; Fc = 1 when it is the whole
sheet.
Changes: AF, BC, DE.

13119.synopsis:
Evaluates the row-selection expression at ($1D73) (L_F06F) for row (iy-60..-59), with the
current slot set to column 0 of that row and (iy-61..-53) saved around the evaluation. Then
moves the expression's row references down one row (offset 1 through L_B37E), ready for the
next row.
Entry: (iy-60..-59) = row.
Exit: Fc = 0 when the result is a number that Fp_cmp finds equal to 1 (the row is printed);
Fc = 1 for any other result.

13204.synopsis:
When "Select rows to print" is on (bit 1 of (iy-46)), falls into L_B368; otherwise returns.
Entry: (iy-46) = print options.

13209.synopsis:
Moves the row references of the row-selection expression at ($1D73) back by the rows it was
advanced: the offset is the block's first row (iy-57..-56) minus the current row
(iy-60..-59), with column offset 0; falls into L_B37E.
Entry: none.

13231.synopsis:
Adjusts every slot reference of the expression at ($1D73) by the offset in (iy-32..-30),
through L_B708 with L_B6D7 as the handler.
Entry: (iy-32) = column offset; (iy-31..-30) = row offset.
Changes: IX.

13241.synopsis:
Refuses a command while bit 6 of (iy-71) is set: reports "Editing expression" ($19, L_EB07)
and returns to the caller's caller. Otherwise returns at once.
Entry: none.
Error: Fc = 1, the calling command is abandoned.

13253.synopsis:
Sets bit 1 of (iy-72) and falls into L_B398.
Entry: none.

13257.synopsis:
Stores a pending edit line into its slot (L_B39E). When that fails, the error has been
reported and it returns to the caller's caller, abandoning the calling command.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.

13263.synopsis:
Stores a pending edit line into its slot. Does nothing (Fc = 0) while bit 6 of (iy-71) is
set. With bit 0 of (iy-72) set it also sets bit 1; then L_B3C6 stores the line. On a failure
it sets the redraw flags (L_CA73) and reports the error (L_EB07).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0 when done or nothing to do.
Error: Fc = 1 after the error was reported.

13289.synopsis:
Sets bits 4 and 1 of (iy-72).
Entry: none.
Changes: none.

13298.synopsis:
Sets bit 0 of (iy-71).
Entry: none.
Changes: none.

13303.synopsis:
Writes the edit line back into the current slot when it holds one (bit 7 of (iy-72)) and it
was changed (bit 0 of (iy-72)). Finds the slot (L_D249, L_D0E2, L_D77E), then from L_B3D6:
sets bit 0 of (iy-71), converts the line at ($1D3D) into $1DAA with L_BC66 (Fc = 1 on
entry), builds the flag byte in (iy-42) ($80, or $A0 when L_BC66 returns P/V = 1, keeping
bits 1-3 of an existing text slot) and the length in (iy-40), makes room (L_B8C7) and copies
the body (L_B490). It clears bits 0 and 7 of (iy-72) at the end (L_B410, L_B411).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0 when stored or nothing to do.
Error: Fc = 1, C = error number (from L_BC66, which leaves the bits of (iy-72) set, or
L_B8C7).

13319.synopsis:
Entry inside L_B3C6, used also by L_B4A6: when bit 0 of (iy-72) is set, converts the edit
line at ($1D3D) with L_BC66 (Fc = 1 on entry) and stores it into the current slot
(iy-110..-108); otherwise only clears bits 0 and 7 of (iy-72).
Entry: (iy-110..-108) = slot position.
Exit: Fc = 0 when stored or nothing to do.
Error: Fc = 1, C = error number.

13378.synopsis:
Clears bits 0 and 7 of (iy-72), the edit-line state; the flags are kept.
Entry: none.
Changes: none.

13387.synopsis:
Marks the edit as going to the slot (iy-107..-105): L_82A2 sets bit 7 of (iy-100) and copies
that position to (iy-104..-102); falls into L_B426.
Entry: (iy-107) = column; (iy-106..-105) = row.

13399.synopsis:
Stores the edit line as an expression into the slot at (iy-104..-102), when bit 0 of (iy-72)
says it was changed. Looks up the slot at A, BC (L_D797), sets bit 0 of (iy-71) and converts
the line at ($1D3D) with L_BC66 (Fc = 0 on entry); an empty result goes to L_B3D6 instead.
The flag byte in (iy-42) is built from the old one ($80 for a new slot): bits 1-4 kept, bits
1-3 set to %011 when it was a text slot, bit 5 set when L_BC66 returns P/V = 1; byte 9 of an
old expression slot is kept. It makes room (L_B8C4), copies the body (L_B490), evaluates it
(L_B575) and ends in L_B410.
Entry: A = column; BC = row; (iy-104..-102) = target slot.
Exit: Fc = 0 when stored or nothing to do.
Error: Fc = 1, C = error number.

13505.synopsis:
Copies the converted slot body from $1DAA into the current slot; falls into L_B493.
Entry: (iy-40) = length including the terminator.

13508.synopsis:
Copies (iy-40) - 1 bytes from HL into the body of the current slot (L_B500) and writes a 0
after them.
Entry: HL = source; (iy-40) = length including the terminator.
Exit: A = 0; DE = address of the 0 written; HL = after the source bytes.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

13527.synopsis:
The Number<>Text command (<>ENT, command table entry 56): converts each slot of the block
between expression and text. Refused while an expression is edited (L_B388); stores a
pending edit (L_B398) and runs L_88C6. For each slot (L_FBBD, L_FB93) that is not of the
kind with flag bits 7 and 6 both set, it loads its text into the edit line (L_BB7B), marks
it changed and stores it back: an expression slot as text (L_B3D6), a text slot as an
expression (L_82A6, L_B426); then it sets bit 1 of (iy-72) and runs L_C9CA. Ends with
L_CA73.
Entry: block in (iy-58..-53).

13610.synopsis:
Reads a 3-byte slot reference (column, row word) at HL.
Entry: HL = reference.
Exit: A = column; BC = row; HL = HL + 3.
Changes: A, BC, HL.

13617.synopsis:
Finds the body of the current slot: binds it (L_B518) and falls into L_B503.
Entry: (iy-127..-125) = current slot.
Exit: as L_B503, with IX = slot.

13620.synopsis:
Returns the body of the slot at IX: it starts at offset 4 for a text slot (bit 7 of the flag
byte (IX+3) set) and at offset 10 otherwise.
Entry: IX = slot.
Exit: A = flag byte; B = offset of the body; HL = IX + B; Fz = 1 when bit 7 is clear.
Changes: AF, B, HL.
Keeps: C, DE.

13641.synopsis:
Points IX at the current slot (iy-127..-126), binding its bank (iy-125) through L_D887 when
it is not the bank in (iy-111).
Entry: (iy-127..-125) = current slot.
Exit: IX = slot.
Changes: AF, IX.
Keeps: DE.

13662.synopsis:
Adds the offset of a slot's body to A: 4 when bit 7 of B (the flag byte) is set, 10
otherwise.
Entry: A = value; B = flag byte.
Exit: A = A + 4 or A + 10.
Changes: AF.

13670.synopsis:
Adds the offset of the body of the slot at IX (L_B503) to A.
Entry: A = value; IX = slot.
Exit: A = A + offset; B = offset; HL = body.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

13677.synopsis:
Subtracts the offset of the body of the slot at IX (L_B503) from A.
Entry: A = value; IX = slot.
Exit: A = A - offset; B = offset; HL = body.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

13684.synopsis:
Loads the current slot into the edit line, unless the line already holds one (bit 7 or bit 0
of (iy-72)). When there is no slot (L_D7AA) the edit line is emptied (L_B56E). A text slot
(flag bit 7 set, bits 7-6 not both set) is put into the line with L_BB7B unless bit 6 of
(iy-71) is set; bit 7 of (iy-72) then marks the line as loaded. Other slots leave the line
alone.
Entry: none.

13722.synopsis:
Shared exit of L_B543: sets bit 7 of (iy-72), the "edit line loaded" flag.
Entry: none.
Changes: none.

13727.synopsis:
Empties the edit line (a 0 at the address in ($1D3D)) and marks it loaded (bit 7 of
(iy-72)).
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.

13734.synopsis:
Evaluates the body of the current slot (L_B500, L_F06F) and stores the result in the slot,
by the result type in (iy-79): type 2 is stored by L_F2DC at IX+4; type 0 puts L in IX+4 and
sets bit 4 of the flag byte; type 5 puts 1 in IX+4 and L in IX+5; type 8 is converted
(L_FE8A, L_FEDA) and stored as 4 bytes at IX+5 with 2 in IX+4; any other puts the 3 bytes at
HL in IX+5 with 0 in IX+4. The flag byte (IX+3) keeps bits 0-3 and 5, gets $40 for types 5,
8 and others, and bit 5 when bit 7 of (iy-44) is set.
Entry: (iy-127..-125) = current slot.
Exit: IX = slot.

13919.synopsis:
Adjusts the references of every slot in the block by the offset (iy-32..-30): walks the
columns from (iy-58) (bit 7 cleared) to (iy-55) and the rows from (iy-57..-56) to
(iy-54..-53), running L_B6FF with L_B6D7 on each slot found (L_D79A).
Entry: block in (iy-58..-53); offset in (iy-32..-30).

14017.synopsis:
Sets the reference offset: column A in (iy-32), row BC in (iy-31..-30). L_B671 falls into it
to restore the offset it saved.
Entry: A = column offset; BC = row offset.
Changes: none.

14084.synopsis:
Adjusts both the column and the row of the reference at HL (C = 0); jumps into L_B6D8.
Entry: HL = reference.

14089.synopsis:
Adjusts the 3-byte slot reference at HL (column, row word) by the offset in (iy-32..-30):
adds (iy-32) to the column unless bit 1 of C is set, and (iy-31..-30) to the row unless bit
0 of C is set. A column of $40 or more, or a row that turns negative, sets bit 7 of the
column byte. L_B6D7 enters with C = B, the reference's marker byte.
Entry: HL = reference; C = bits 1 and 0 for a column and a row that stay fixed.
Exit: HL unchanged; Fc = 0 when bit 7 was set.
Changes: AF.

14124.synopsis:
Sets bit 6 of the byte at HL (the column byte of a reference) and returns Fc = 0.
Entry: HL = reference.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Changes: F.

14128.synopsis:
Runs a routine on every cell reference in an expression slot. Returns at once when bit 5 of
the slot's type byte is clear; otherwise walks the slot's content after its header to the
terminating zero and, for each reference token ($10-$13), calls the routine with HL on the
3-byte reference that follows the token.
Entry: IX = slot (bank bound); HL = routine to call.
Exit: IX = the routine; the routine is called with B = token, C = 0, HL = reference.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX, and what the routine changes.

14159.synopsis:
Sets the start of the reference range (iy-58..56) to the cursor's column, with no row bound
(bit 7 of (iy-56) set); falls into L_B721.
Entry: none.
Exit: (iy-58) = cursor column; (iy-57/56) = cursor row with bit 7 of the high byte set.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

14162.synopsis:
Sets the start of the reference range from the cursor position (L_D0E2): (iy-58) = cursor
column OR A, (iy-57) = row low, (iy-56) = row high OR C. In the column byte bit 7 limits the
range to that one column and bits 7 and 6 together accept every column; bit 7 of the row
high byte removes the row bound.
Entry: A = bits for the column byte; C = bits for the row high byte.
Exit: (iy-58..56) = range start.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

14181.synopsis:
Stores a shift (L_B690) and sets the end of the reference range (iy-55..53) from its start.
For a negative shift the end is start + |shift| - 1 (the cells that go); for a positive one
it is the start; an unbounded start gives end column $40 or end row $7FFF. A negative shift
in either direction then installs L_B6F7 as the in-range routine (L_B78A); otherwise L_B785
removes the column end.
Entry: A = column shift; BC = row shift (signed); (iy-58..56) = range start.
Exit: (iy-32..30) = shift; (iy-55..53) = range end; (iy-20/19) = L_B6F7 when a shift is
negative.
Changes: AF, BC, E, HL.

14262.synopsis:
Sets bit 7 of the range's end column (iy-55), so the range has no column end. Shared tail of
L_B734.
Entry: none.

14267.synopsis:
Installs L_B6F7 as the routine L_B8A0 runs for a reference inside the range; L_B6F7 marks
the reference invalid by setting bit 7 of its column byte. Falls into L_B78D.
Entry: none.
Exit: (iy-20/19) = L_B6F7.
Changes: BC.

14270.synopsis:
Stores BC in (iy-20/19) as the routine L_B8A0 runs for a reference inside the range.
Entry: BC = routine.
Exit: (iy-20/19) = BC.

14277.synopsis:
Adjusts the cell references after the cursor's column is deleted: references to that column
become invalid (bit 7 of the column byte) and those to later columns move one column left.
Entry: none (the cursor's column).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

14284.synopsis:
Adjusts the cell references after a column is inserted at the cursor: references to the
cursor's column and later ones move one column right.
Entry: none (the cursor's column).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

14294.synopsis:
Adjusts the cell references after the cursor's row is deleted: the range starts at the
cursor (L_B721 with C = 0) and the row shift is -1, so references to the row become invalid
and those to later rows move one row up. Falls through L_B7B9.
Entry: A = column bits for L_B721 ($80 = the cursor's column only, $C0 = every column).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

14314.synopsis:
Shifts the cell references in a range: sets the range end from the shift (L_B734), then
adjusts every reference with L_B8A0.
1. Saves (iy-42). For each column (iy-110) from 0 to (iy-98) - 1, and for each row from 0
while L_D79A finds a slot, runs L_B8A0 on every reference of the slot (L_B6FF).
2. Runs L_B8A0 (C = 0) on the block marks at (iy-67..65) and (iy-64..62) when they are set
(bit 7 of the column clear).
3. Clears both marks with L_89F8 when either one's bit 7 changed, then restores (iy-42).
Entry: A = column shift; BC = row shift (signed); (iy-58..56) = range start.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX; (iy-110..108).

14319.synopsis:
Entry inside L_B7B9 for a caller that has set the range start, end and in-range routine
itself: stores the shift (L_B690) and adjusts every reference and the block marks.
Entry: A = column shift; BC = row shift (signed); (iy-58..53) = range; (iy-20/19) = in-range
routine.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX; (iy-110..108).

14430.synopsis:
Tests the cell reference at HL against the range (iy-58..53). A reference before the start
(column or row) is left alone. One inside the range in both column and row returns Fc = 1.
One at or after the start but past the end in a direction is shifted by L_B6D8 (C selects
the directions) and returns Fc = 0. A start column with bit 7 set accepts only that column,
with bits 7 and 6 every column; an end column with bit 6 set leaves references past it
alone; bit 7 of the end column or of the start row high byte removes that bound.
Entry: HL = reference (column, row low, row high); C = L_B6D8 flags (0 = shift both).
Exit: Fc = 1 inside the range; Fc = 0 otherwise; HL unchanged.
Changes: AF, B, DE.

14545.synopsis:
The routine L_B7B9 runs on each reference. A reference whose column byte has bit 6 set is
only cleared of it. Otherwise L_B82D tests and shifts it, and a reference inside the range
is passed to the routine at (iy-20/19).
Entry: HL = reference (column, row low, row high); C = L_B6D8 flags.
Changes: AF, B, DE, IX, and what the in-range routine changes.

14565.synopsis:
Jumps to the routine at IX; "call L_B8B4" calls it.
Entry: IX = routine.

14567.synopsis:
Sets the type and length for the next new slot to $80 and 1: (iy-42) = $80, (iy-40) = $01
(the values of L_B8C0).
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = $8001.
Changes: BC.

14577.synopsis:
Loads BC with $8001: type $80 and content length 1, the slot used to fill empty rows.
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = $8001.

14581.synopsis:
Stores the column and row (L_D77E) and falls into L_B8C7 to make sure a slot exists there.
Entry: A = column; BC = row.
Exit: as L_B8C7.
Error: as L_B8C7.

14584.synopsis:
Makes sure a slot of type (iy-42) and content length (iy-40) exists at column (iy-110), row
(iy-109/108).
1. When L_D79A finds a slot there, L_B95D gives it the type and size.
2. Otherwise makes sure the column exists (L_D8BF). An empty column (bit 7 of byte 3 of its
column entry) gets a first slot of type $80 at row 0, recorded in the entry, and the search
starts again.
3. Otherwise appends slots after the column's last slot up to the row: type $80, length 1
for the rows in between, the requested type and length for the last. Each one is allocated
(L_D926), cleared (L_D8F2), linked after the previous one (L_BA44), recorded as the column's
cached position (L_B9D6) and its row recorded with L_CA0E.
Entry: (iy-110..108) = column and row; (iy-42) = type; (iy-40) = content length.
Exit: Fc = 0; the slot is the current one ((iy-127..125)).
Error: Fc = 1 when memory runs out.

14785.synopsis:
Gets the size of the current slot: 6 when bits 7 and 6 of its type are both set, otherwise
the bytes from the slot's start to its terminating zero (references counted as 4 bytes by
L_A8BB).
Entry: (iy-127..125) = current slot.
Exit: B = size; IX = slot (bank bound).
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL, IX.

14809.synopsis:
Links the current slot (iy-127..125) into its column's list between the slots at (iy+65..67)
and (iy+68..70) (L_BA44 twice), records it as the column's cached position at the current
row (L_B9D6) and binds its bank.
Entry: (iy-127..125) = slot; (iy+65..70) = the neighbours; (iy-110..108) = column and row.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

14839.synopsis:
Records a cached position one row back: when HL is not 0, decrements the current row
(iy-109/108); then falls into L_B9D6.
Entry: HL, C = slot; DE, B = next slot.
Changes: AF, DE, HL, and as L_B9D6.

14855.synopsis:
Writes the cached position of column (iy-110) into its column entry: bytes 2-3 the row, 4-6
the slot, 7-9 the next slot. With HL = 0 the cache is reset: to the slot at DE, B as row 0
(its link giving the next slot), or to row $8000 (an empty column) with no slots when DE is
0 too.
Entry: HL, C = slot at the current row (iy-109/108); DE, B = next slot.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

14933.synopsis:
Unlinks the cached slot of column A from the column's list: reads the column entry (L_BAC8)
and falls into L_BA27.
Entry: A = column.
Exit: as L_BA27.

14936.synopsis:
Unlinks a slot from its XOR-linked list. Afterwards the slot's link is 0 and neither
neighbour points at it; the neighbours are not linked to each other.
Entry: HL, C = slot; DE, B = next slot.
Exit: (iy-117..115) = the removed slot; (iy+65..67) = previous slot; (iy+68..70) = next
slot; HL, C = previous slot; DE, B = removed slot.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

14939.synopsis:
Entry inside L_BA27 after the first L_BA44: the slot's link already holds only its previous
slot. Saves the slot and the next one, reads the previous slot from the link and unlinks it.
Entry: HL, C = slot; DE, B = next slot.
Exit: as L_BA27.

14965.synopsis:
Toggles the link between two slots of an XOR-linked list: XORs the address and bank of each
into the other's 3-byte link field (bytes 0-2). Does nothing when either address is 0.
Entry: HL, C = one slot; DE, B = the other.
Exit: HL, DE unchanged; the bank of DE is bound.
Changes: AF.

15012.synopsis:
Finds where a slot goes in at column A, row BC: stores the column and row (L_D77E), finds
the slot at the row before (L_D7AD) and stores the neighbours the new slot goes between.
Entry: A = column; BC = row.
Exit: (iy+65..67) = slot at row BC - 1 (0 for row 0); (iy+68..70) = slot at row BC.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

15047.synopsis:
Loads the current slot pointer: HL = (iy-127/126), C = bank (iy-125).
Entry: none.
Exit: HL, C = slot.
Changes: C, HL.

15057.synopsis:
Loads the pointer at (iy-117..115): HL = address, C = bank.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL, C = slot.
Changes: C, HL.

15067.synopsis:
Stores HL, C as the current slot pointer (iy-127..125).
Entry: HL, C = slot.

15077.synopsis:
Stores HL, C at (iy-117..115).
Entry: HL, C = slot.

15087.synopsis:
Loads the current slot pointer into DE, B: DE = (iy-127/126), B = bank (iy-125).
Entry: none.
Exit: DE, B = slot.
Changes: B, DE.

15097.synopsis:
Reads the cached position of column A from its 10-byte column entry (L_D890): the slot
(bytes 4-6) and the next slot (bytes 7-9).
Entry: A = column.
Exit: HL, C = slot; DE, B = next slot; A = column + 1.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

15117.synopsis:
Swaps the pointer at (iy+65..67) with the one at (iy+71..73) and the one at (iy+68..70) with
the one at (iy+74..76). Ends with L_BAF1.
Entry: none.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.

15138.synopsis:
Stores HL, C at (iy+74..76).
Entry: HL, C = pointer.

15148.synopsis:
Stores HL, C at (iy+71..73).
Entry: HL, C = pointer.

15158.synopsis:
Stores HL, C at (iy+68..70).
Entry: HL, C = pointer.

15168.synopsis:
Stores HL, C at (iy+65..67).
Entry: HL, C = pointer.

15188.synopsis:
Stores DE, B at (iy+68..70).
Entry: DE, B = pointer.

15198.synopsis:
Stores DE, B at (iy+65..67).
Entry: DE, B = pointer.

15208.synopsis:
Loads HL, C from (iy+71..73).
Entry: none.
Exit: HL, C = pointer.
Changes: C, HL.

15218.synopsis:
Loads HL, C from (iy+68..70).
Entry: none.
Exit: HL, C = pointer.
Changes: C, HL.

15228.synopsis:
Loads HL, C from (iy+65..67).
Entry: none.
Exit: HL, C = pointer.
Changes: C, HL.

15238.synopsis:
Loads DE, B from (iy+74..76).
Entry: none.
Exit: DE, B = pointer.
Changes: B, DE.

15248.synopsis:
Loads DE, B from (iy+71..73).
Entry: none.
Exit: DE, B = pointer.
Changes: B, DE.

15258.synopsis:
Loads DE, B from (iy+68..70).
Entry: none.
Exit: DE, B = pointer.
Changes: B, DE.

15268.synopsis:
Writes the current slot's content as text to the screen, at most A characters: sets L_BC17
(writes with OS_Out while the count (iy-36) lasts, skipping zero bytes) as the output
routine and continues in L_BB7E.
Entry: A = maximum number of characters.
Exit: as L_BB7E; (iy-34) = characters written.
Error: as L_BB7E.

15276.synopsis:
Writes the current slot's content as text into the buffer at ($1D3D): sets L_BC07 (stores at
($1D3D) + (iy-34) and counts) as the output routine and falls into L_BB7E.
Entry: none.
Exit: as L_BB7E; (iy-34) = bytes written.
Error: as L_BB7E.

15279.synopsis:
Turns the current slot's content back into text through the output routine in BC (stored at
$1D4B, called with the character in A). Token $14 is written as '"', a reference token
($10-$13) as a cell reference (L_BC2C, with '$' before the column when bit 1 of the token is
set and before the row when bit 0 is), and other bytes as they are; a zero is written at the
end. SP is kept at $1D47 so an output routine can abandon the work.
Entry: BC = output routine; (iy-127..125) = current slot.
Exit: (iy-34) = 0 at start, counted by the output routine; F = 0 (P/V = 0).
Error: an output routine that overflows reloads SP from ($1D47) and returns to the caller
with P/V = 1 (as L_8AA9 does).

15344.synopsis:
Writes the cell reference in A (column) and BC (row) as text without '$' markers; falls into
L_BBC6 with Fc and P/V clear.
Entry: A = column; BC = row (from 0).
Exit: as L_BBC6.

15351.synopsis:
Writes a cell reference as text through the output routine at ($1D4B): '%' first when bit 7
of the column is set, '$' when Fc = 1, the column letters (L_BC39), '$' when P/V = 1, then
the row + 1 in decimal (L_BC60).
Entry: A = column (bit 7 = invalid); BC = row (from 0); Fc = absolute column; P/V = absolute
row.
Exit: (iy-74) = 0.
Changes: AF, DE, HL, IX.

15383.synopsis:
Writes the (iy-74) bytes of the text buffer at IY+35 through the output routine (L_BBFA).
Entry: (iy-74) = count (not 0).
Exit: (iy-74) = 0; HL = after the last byte.
Changes: F, DE, HL.

15399.synopsis:
Writes '$' through the output routine (L_BBFC).
Entry: none.
Changes: A.

15403.synopsis:
Writes the byte at HL through the output routine and advances HL; falls into L_BBFC.
Entry: HL = byte.
Exit: HL + 1; A = the byte.
Changes: A, HL.

15405.synopsis:
Calls the output routine whose address is at $1D4B with the character in A; keeps AF and HL.
Entry: A = character.
Keeps: AF, HL.

15453.synopsis:
Writes the cell reference stored at HL (column, row low, row high) as text with L_BBC6; Fc
and P/V on entry select the '$' markers.
Entry: HL = reference; Fc = absolute column; P/V = absolute row.
Exit: HL = after the reference.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, IX.

15466.synopsis:
Puts the letters of column A at the start of the text buffer at IY+35: falls into L_BC3B
with C = 0.
Entry: A = column (from 0).
Exit: as L_BC3B.

15468.synopsis:
Puts the letters of column A at offset C in the text buffer at IY+35: one letter for columns
0-25 (A-Z), two for later ones (AA, AB, ...).
Entry: A = column (from 0); C = offset.
Exit: (iy-74) = C + the letters written.
Changes: AF, C, DE, HL.

15505.synopsis:
Puts BC + 1 in decimal, without leading zeros, at the start of the text buffer at IY+35
(L_EE87).
Entry: BC = row (from 0).
Exit: (iy-74) = number of digits.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX.

15511.synopsis:
Compiles the text at ($1D3D) into the token buffer at $1DAA (L_BC6D with IX and HL set).
Characters are copied; control characters are dropped and '"' becomes $14, toggling a string
state. Outside strings a '$' or a letter that does not follow a letter or digit starts a
cell reference (L_BD57), compiled as a token $10-$13 (bit 1 = '$' before the column, bit 0 =
before the row) with the column and the row word. A zero ends the buffer. With Fc = 1 on
entry (text mode) characters are copied as they are and a reference is compiled only after a
single '@' and when '@' follows it.
Entry: ($1D3D) = zero-terminated text; Fc = text mode.
Exit: Fc = 0; B = bytes written, terminator included; IX = after them; P/V = 1 when a
reference was compiled; (iy-110..108) unchanged.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $15 when the buffer reaches 245 bytes.

15732.synopsis:
Stores A at IX in the token buffer, advances IX and counts the byte in (iy-38).
Entry: A = byte; IX = buffer position.
Exit: Fc = 0; A kept.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $15 when the count reaches 245.
Changes: F, B, C, IX.

15752.synopsis:
Parses a cell reference in text after skipping spaces (L_BDBE): an optional '$', the column
letters (L_BD91), an optional '$' and the row number (L_EE29, which must be at least 1).
Entry: HL = text.
Exit: Fc = 0; (iy-110) = column; (iy-109/108) = row - 1; C = '$' flags (bit 1 before the
column, bit 0 before the row); A = next character; HL = after the reference.
Error: Fc = 1 when there is no valid reference.

15810.synopsis:
Parses one or two column letters at HL into (iy-110): A-Z is 0-25, two letters give (first +
1) * 26 + second, which must be below 64.
Entry: HL = text.
Exit: Fc = 0; (iy-110) = column; HL = after the letters.
Error: Fc = 1 (A = 0 when the first character is not a letter).

15855.synopsis:
Skips spaces from HL; falls into L_BDBF.
Entry: HL = text.
Exit: HL = first character that is not a space; A = it; Fz = 1 at the terminating zero.
Changes: AF, HL.

15865.synopsis:
Tests A for a letter (ValidateAlphabetic) and turns it into 0-25, either case.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: Fc = 1 and A = 0-25 for a letter; Fc = 0 otherwise.
Changes: AF.

15875.synopsis:
Jumps to the routine whose address is at $1D53 (set to L_BDD6 at start-up).
Entry: as the routine.

15879.synopsis:
Resets the display and falls into L_BE08. Sends the window set-up (L_E0B3 with A = 0), sets
bits 1 and 2 of (iy-99), clears bit 5 of (iy-70), writes the value OS_Nq NQ_WBOX returns in
C (L_EEFE) into byte 5 of each 6-byte entry of the table at ($1D61) (L_D590 gives the
count), runs L_EEDD and L_EFDC, sets the redraw flag (L_CA8D) and clears bit 5 of (iy-68).
Entry: none.

15929.synopsis:
Updates the display after a command (called from the main loop). Stores the cursor's column
and row (L_D0E2) at (iy+2..4). When bit 6 of (iy-99) is set it recomputes the rows on screen
(L_D104, L_C9F9, then L_D403 or L_D8AB and L_D452); when bit 1 is set the columns (L_D0D0,
L_D198). Then it acts on the pending cursor move in (iy-100) and (iy-101): none goes to
L_C1F8, a negative one to L_C1A6, otherwise (iy-101) = 0, 1 and 2 go to L_C018, L_BF0F and
L_BEC0, and other values move the column pointer ($1D5D) on.
Entry: none.

39.synopsis:
