Moves the current row forward by A rows (L_BFFC), then copies the current row (IY-26/25) to
(IY-24/23) (L_C0DB).
Entry: A = number of rows; (IY-26/25) = current row.
Exit: as L_BFFC; (IY-24/23) = (IY-26/25).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

45.synopsis:
Steps the current row (IY-26/25) forward one row at a time until A rows have been passed.
Rows found among the leading line-table entries (L_D5D1) are passed without being counted.
Stops early when the next row would reach the row count (IY-97/96) (L_C9F9).
Entry: A = number of rows; (IY-26/25) = current row.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = 0; (IY-26/25) = the row reached.
Error: Fc = 1 when the row count was reached; A = rows still to go.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

265.synopsis:
Moves the current row back by A rows (L_C0E8), then falls into L_C0DB, which copies the
current row (IY-26/25) to (IY-24/23).
Entry: A = number of rows; (IY-26/25) = current row.
Exit: as L_C0E8; (IY-24/23) = (IY-26/25).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

281.synopsis:
Steps the current row (IY-26/25) back one row at a time (L_CA21) until A rows have been
passed. Rows found among the leading line-table entries (L_D5D7) are not counted.
Entry: A = number of rows; (IY-26/25) = current row.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = 0; (IY-26/25) = the row reached.
Error: Fc = 1 when row 0 was reached; A = rows still to go, counting the one refused.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

300.synopsis:
Works out how many rows L_BFCC and L_C0AE move by. Takes the number of text lines on the
screen (L_D590), less the line-table entries with bit 7 set (L_D0F1), less the text lines
divided by (IY+7) when (IY+7) is not 0, less 1; the result is at least 1. Also makes the row
of the current line entry ($1D63) the current row (L_D8A1).
Entry: ($1D61) = line table; ($1D63) = current line entry; (IY+7).
Exit: A = number of rows (1 or more); (IY-34) = count of entries with bit 7 set; (IY-26/25)
= row of the current line entry.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

346.synopsis:
Copies the three bytes at (IY-94..IY-92) to (IY-61..IY-59). L_C13A copies them back.
Entry: none.
Exit: (IY-61..IY-59) = (IY-94..IY-92).
Changes: AF, B, IX.

363.synopsis:
Copies the three bytes at (IY-61..IY-59) to (IY-94..IY-92); the reverse of L_C129.
Entry: none.
Exit: (IY-94..IY-92) = (IY-61..IY-59).
Changes: AF, B, IX.

380.synopsis:
Returns at once when bit 5 of the current line entry ($1D63) is set. Otherwise drops its
caller's return address and continues at L_C152: sets bit 5 of (IY-72), marks lines and
cells to redraw (L_CA39, L_C9DF) and ends at L_C1F8, so the caller's caller resumes.
Entry: ($1D63) = current line entry.
Exit: returns to the caller only when bit 5 of the entry is set.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX (on the L_C152 path).

1166.synopsis:
Redraws the line-editor buffer at ($1D3D) from screen column (IY-28) on screen line (IY-27).
1. The field is (IY-89) characters wide, cut to A - (IY-28).
2. Moves the start offset (IY-88) so that the edit position (IY-87) lies in the field: at
its end when it was past it (in the middle when (IY-100) bit 7 is set), at its start when it
was before it; returns without drawing when it was already in the field and (IY-72) bit 5 is
clear.
3. Prints the buffer from that offset, codes below $20 through L_CADB; at its end, unless
(IY-85) bit 7 is set, clears up to column (IY-42) with spaces (L_C5EA). With (IY-85) bit 7
set the rest of the field is filled with spaces.
4. Ends any highlight left on (L_CA92).
Entry: A = right limit (screen column).
Exit: A = column after the last character drawn, relative to (IY-28); Fc = 1 when A = 0;
(IY-88) = new offset.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

1314.synopsis:
Redraws the screen line of line-table entry HL when the bit of the display flags (IY-99)
given in A is set; otherwise returns Fz = 1. Falls into L_C4F6.
Entry: A = flag mask ($20 or $10); HL = line-table entry.
Exit: as L_C4F6 when the bit is set.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

1318.synopsis:
Redraws one screen line, the one of line-table entry HL.
1. Keeps HL in (IY-44/43) and clears bit 5 or 4 of (IY-99) when HL is the first or last line
waiting for redraw ((IY-52/51), (IY-50/49)); makes the entry's row current.
2. Bit 5 of the entry set: fills the line with '^' characters across (IY-81) columns.
3. Otherwise moves to the line's start (L_CB02). When the 6-character left margin is on
(L_D5A7), prints the row number (L_BC60) padded to 5 with '_' (a leading entry) or spaces,
then a space.
4. When the row's column-0 cell has type bits %11 (L_D252), prints a line of '~' or the text
built by L_EE4E; otherwise draws each column of the column table (L_C612).
5. Clears with spaces what is left of the previous drawing (byte 5 of the entry) and stores
the new width there.
Entry: HL = line-table entry.
Exit: Fc = 0; byte 5 of the entry = columns drawn.
Error: Fc = 1 when L_C612 returned Fc = 1.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

1562.synopsis:
Prints A spaces. On screen it sends SOH '3N' with the count and a space (repeat character);
when (IY-70) bit 6 is set it calls L_ED8A A times instead. Does nothing when A = 0.
Entry: A = number of spaces.
Exit: none.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

1602.synopsis:
Draws the cell of one column on the screen line being drawn (line entry (IY-44/43)).
1. Takes the column from the column-table entry into (IY-38), keeps column and row in
(IY-110..IY-108) (L_D77E) and makes the line's row current (L_D24C); returns Fc = 1 at once
when that row's column-0 cell has type bits %11.
2. Works out the cell's width with overflow into empty columns (L_C917, (IY-40)), whether it
holds anything to show (L_D79A, L_C9B8), its screen position (L_D08D: column (IY-32), line
(IY-31)) and cuts the width at the screen width (IY-81).
3. When the cell is empty or has type bits %10 and is the cursor's slot ($1D5D on line
($1D63)) with (IY-71) bit 6 clear, only raises (IY-42) to the cell's right edge.
4. Otherwise sets the highlight for the marked block (L_CA99), copies bytes 3-4 of the line
entry to (IY-91/90) and draws the contents (L_CB0E) when there are any, then pads with
spaces (L_C5EA) and updates (IY-42) and byte 5 of the line entry.
Entry: HL = column-table entry.
Exit: Fc = 0; HL = the column-table entry.
Error: Fc = 1 as in step 1.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, IX.

1982.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to column (IY-32), line (IY-31) (L_EEE4) unless bit 7 of (IY-31) is set,
and then sets that bit, so the move is made only once.
Entry: (IY-32) = column; (IY-31) = line.
Exit: bit 7 of (IY-31) set.
Changes: none.
Keeps: AF, BC.

2005.synopsis:
Clears bit 2 of (IY-99) and, when the left margin is on (L_D5A7), redraws the column heading
line: moves to line 1, prints 6 spaces, then for each column-table entry the column's
letters (L_BC39) at the right of its width, the width before them filled with '_' (bit 7
set), $A0 (the cursor's column) or '.'. The cursor column's character at its second width
byte (L_D551) is marked (L_C834). Pads the rest of the line with spaces.
Entry: ($1D5B) = column table; ($1D5D) = cursor's entry.
Exit: none.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

2148.synopsis:
Prints one character of the column heading for L_C7A5 and counts the columns left in
(IY-36). When the countdown in (IY-38) reaches 0 on this character, prints SOH $FA instead
of $A0 or '.', or prints the character between two SOH 'B' (L_CD74).
Entry: A = character; (IY-36) = columns left; (IY-38) = countdown (0 = none).
Exit: Fz = 1 when (IY-36) reached 0.
Changes: F, C, E, (IY-36), (IY-38).
Keeps: A, HL.

2198.synopsis:
Draws the cursor's slot reference at the window's top-left: moves the cursor to column 0,
line 0, points ($1D4B) at L_BC17 as the output routine, prints the column and row of the
cursor's slot (L_D0E2, L_BBBF) and pads the field to 7 characters with spaces.
Entry: ($1D63), ($1D5D) = cursor's line and column entries.
Exit: none.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

2228.synopsis:
Scrolls the text area: defines window 3 over it (SOH '6#3'; from line 1, or line 2 when the
left margin is on, (IY-81) wide, (IY-80) less 1 or 2 lines high), selects it (SOH '2H3'),
sends SOH and A, selects the window that was current again (SOH '2H') and sends SOH '2D3'.
Entry: A = SD_UP ($FE) or SD_DWN ($FF).
Exit: none.
Changes: AF, BC.

2309.synopsis:
Shifts byte 5 (the drawn width) of the line-table entries one entry towards the start: each
entry takes the value of the next, for the screen's text lines (L_D590) plus one. Used with
L_C884 when the screen scrolls.
Entry: ($1D61) = line table.
Exit: none.
Changes: AF, B, DE, IX.

2334.synopsis:
Shifts byte 5 (the drawn width) of the line-table entries one entry towards the end: from
the last text line (L_D590) back to the second, each entry takes the value of the one
before. The reverse of L_C8D9.
Entry: ($1D61) = line table.
Exit: IX = ($1D61).
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL, IX.

2371.synopsis:
Works out how many characters the cell at column A of the current row may use: its column
width (L_D54A), extended over the following columns while they are empty (L_C989), up to the
column's second width byte (L_D551). Returns at once when that byte is not above the width,
or when (IY-71) bit 6 is set and the slot is the cursor's.
Entry: A = column; (IY-26/25) = current row.
Exit: A = width, the smaller of the two.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

2485.synopsis:
Tests whether the slot at column A of the current row has anything to show (L_D7B3, L_C9B8).
Entry: A = column; (IY-26/25) = current row.
Exit: Fc = 1 when the column is 0 or the slot is in the marked block (L_CFE0, tested only
when (IY-70) bit 6 and (IY-67) bit 7 are clear), with Fz = 1 when it has no cell. Otherwise
Fc = 0, Fz = 1 when there is no cell or it is blank; Fc = 1, Fz = 0 when it holds text other
than spaces. A = column; IX = cell when there is one.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

2532.synopsis:
Tests whether the current cell (L_B500) holds text other than spaces.
Entry: (IY-127..IY-125) = current cell.
Exit: Fz = 1, Fc = 0 when the cell's type bits are %11; otherwise Fc = 1 when its text is
empty or only spaces, or Fc = 0, Fz = 0 and A = the first other character, HL past it.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX.

2550.synopsis:
Marks the slot kept in (IY-110..IY-108) for redraw when it has a cell (L_D79A) and both its
row (L_D56B) and its column (L_D55D) are on the screen; falls into L_C9DF.
Entry: (IY-110) = column; (IY-109/108) = row.
Exit: Fc = 0 when the cell was marked.
Error: Fc = 1 when it was not.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

2571.synopsis:
Marks the current cell for redraw: sets bit 0 of its flags byte (byte 3) and bit 3 of
(IY-72).
Entry: (IY-127..IY-125) = current cell.
Exit: IX = cell.
Changes: A, IX.

2583.synopsis:
Adds 1 to the current row (IY-26/25) and falls into L_C9F9 to compare it with the row count.
Entry: (IY-26/25) = current row.
Exit: BC = new row; flags as L_C9F9.
Changes: F, BC.
Keeps: A.

2597.synopsis:
Compares row BC with the row count (IY-97/96).
Entry: BC = row.
Exit: Fc = 0 when BC is below the count; Fc = 1 when it is not, with Fz = 1 when equal.
Changes: F.
Keeps: A, BC.

2618.synopsis:
Adds 1 to BC and falls into L_CA0F, so the row count becomes at least BC + 2.
Entry: BC = row; A = value for (IY-95).
Exit: as L_CA0F.
Changes: F, BC.

2619.synopsis:
Raises the row count (IY-97/96) to BC + 1 when it is lower, storing A in (IY-95) as well.
Entry: BC = row; A = value for (IY-95).
Exit: BC = row + 1.
Changes: F, BC.

2634.synopsis:
Adds 1 to BC and compares it with the row count (L_C9F9).
Entry: BC = row.
Exit: BC = row + 1; flags as L_C9F9.
Changes: F, BC.

2637.synopsis:
Moves the current row (IY-26/25) back by one, through L_CA2A.
Entry: (IY-26/25) = current row.
Exit: Fc = 0; (IY-26/25) one less.
Error: Fc = 1 when the row was 0; nothing changes.
Changes: F.

2646.synopsis:
Entry inside L_CA21: subtracts 1 from the current row (IY-26/25) without testing it.
Entry: (IY-26/25) = current row.
Exit: (IY-26/25) one less.
Changes: none.
Keeps: AF.

2661.synopsis:
Adds line-table entry HL to the lines waiting for redraw. When none is waiting, HL becomes
the first ((IY-52/51), bit 5 of (IY-99)); when one is, HL becomes the second ((IY-50/49),
bit 4), and the two swap places when their high bytes differ. When two are already waiting,
draws line HL at once (L_C4F6).
Entry: HL = line-table entry.
Exit: (IY-99) and the two pointers updated.
Changes: AF, C, DE (and all of L_C4F6 on that path).

2719.synopsis:
Sets bit 5 of (IY-72) and bit 3 of the display flags (IY-99).
Entry: none.
Exit: none.
Changes: none.

2728.synopsis:
Sets bits 0 and 6 of the display flags (IY-99).
Entry: none.
Exit: none.
Changes: none.

2737.synopsis:
Sets bits 7 (L_CA8D) and 1 of the display flags (IY-99).
Entry: none.
Exit: none.
Changes: none.

2745.synopsis:
Sets bit 7 of the display flags (IY-99), the flag that has every screen line redrawn.
Entry: none.
Exit: none.
Changes: none.

2750.synopsis:
Ends a highlight left on: when bit 0 of (IY-85) is set, toggles it off and sends SOH 'R'
(L_CAF0).
Entry: (IY-85).
Exit: bit 0 of (IY-85) clear.
Changes: F.
Keeps: A.

2757.synopsis:
Sets the highlight state (IY-85) for the slot at column (IY-38) of the current row: $81 when
it is in the marked block (L_CFE0, only when (IY-67) bit 7 is clear), else 0. When (IY-71)
bit 6 is set and the slot is the cursor's (L_D0E2), the value is toggled. When bit 7 ends up
set, sends SOH 'R' (L_EFEF).
Entry: (IY-38) = column; (IY-26/25) = row.
Exit: (IY-85) set.
Changes: none.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

2823.synopsis:
Prints control code A in reverse video: a code $18-$1F (L_CE2A) as the digit 1-8, a lower
code as A + $40, between two toggles of reverse (L_CAF0).
Entry: A = control code below $20.
Exit: none.
Changes: AF.

2844.synopsis:
Toggles bit 0 of (IY-85) and sends SOH 'R' (L_EFEF) once, so the reverse-video state on
screen follows it.
Entry: (IY-85).
Exit: bit 0 of (IY-85) toggled.
Changes: none.
Keeps: AF.

2862.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to the start of the screen line of line entry (IY-44/43) (L_D0B1, L_EEE3).
Entry: (IY-44/43) = line-table entry.
Exit: B = screen line.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

2874.synopsis:
Draws the current cell's contents in a field of A columns and returns how many columns were
written. Points ($1D4D) at the cell's text (L_FAB1) and looks at its flags byte:
1. Bit 4 set: prints message (byte 4) of the table at L_EC31 through L_EB4D, sending it to
L_F020, or to L_ED93 when (IY-70) bit 6 is set; returns from there.
2. Type bits %00: formats a number through L_FE72 and L_FEF0 (byte 9), then L_FB76. Type
%01: evaluated by L_FA25; Fc = 0 goes on as %00; result type 0 prints a message as in 1, 8 a
date (L_D077), others copy the result text (L_CE31).
3. Type %11: the text built by L_EE4E. Other text: copied to $1EAA with fields expanded
(L_CE31); for format 8 its first character (not '@') separates three parts.
4. Prints the text aligned by format bits 3-1 (L_CBD9).
Entry: A = field width; (IY-127..IY-125) = current cell.
Exit: A = (IY-34) = columns written.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

3070.synopsis:
Entry inside L_CBB2 (three-part text): pads up to column A of the field, A - (IY-34) spaces,
and prints the next part through L_CC72.
Entry: A = column; (IY-34) = columns written so far.
Exit: as L_CC72.
Error: Fc = 1, nothing printed, when A is below (IY-34).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

3077.synopsis:
Prints the text at ($1D4D) in a field of (IY-36) columns, aligned by bits 3-1 of A.
1. 0: no padding. 2, 4, 6: padding before the text of none, half or all the free columns
(L_CDF2 measures it). 8: three NUL-separated parts (L_CBB2).
2. $0A, $0C: spreads the free columns over the gaps between words (L_CDEF), keeping a byte
per gap in a table on the stack ((IY-30/29), (IY-78) gaps), worked out with L_F048 and
L_F05E.
3. Prints the text through the loop at L_CC8D: highlight codes $18-$1F (L_CD49), other
control codes (L_CADB), $7F as a space, gaps widened (L_CDA6); stops when the field is full;
then frees the gap table and, on screen, ends highlights still on (L_CD74).
Entry: A = format; (IY-36) = field width; ($1D4D) = text.
Exit: (IY-34) = columns written; (IY-36) = columns left.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

3230.synopsis:
Prints A spaces, at most the (IY-36) columns left (L_C5EA), adds them to (IY-34) and takes
them from (IY-36). Then prints the text at ($1D4D), its leading spaces skipped, through the
loop at L_CC8D (see L_CBD9).
Entry: A = spaces; (IY-36) = columns left; (IY-34) = columns written; ($1D4D) = text.
Exit: (IY-34), (IY-36) updated.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

3445.synopsis:
Handles highlight code A ($18-$1F) in the text output: toggles bit A - $18 of D. On screen
codes $18-$1B send SOH and a letter from L_CD90, and codes $1C-$1F are shown as a reverse
digit (L_CADB). When (IY-70) bit 6 is set, sends $05, '1' and the letter from L_CD94.
Entry: A = code; D = highlights on.
Exit: D updated; Fc = 1 when a sequence was sent, Fc = 0 for a digit shown.
Changes: AF, BC, D.
Keeps: E, HL.

3488.synopsis:
Sends SOH and letter E of the table L_CD90 ('U', 'B', 'G', 'T'), through L_CD9C.
Entry: E = 0-3.
Exit: Fc = 1.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: DE, HL.

3516.synopsis:
Table of 4 bytes: the letters 'U', 'B', 'G', 'T' sent after SOH for the highlight codes
$18-$1B on screen (L_CD74, L_CD49).

3520.synopsis:
Table of 8 bytes: the letters 'U', 'B', 'X', 'I', 'L', 'R', 'A', 'E' sent after $05 '1' for
the highlight codes $18-$1F when output goes through L_ED93 (L_CD49).

3528.synopsis:
Outputs character A: on screen through OS_Out, or through L_ED93 when (IY-70) bit 6 is set.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: none.
Changes: as OS_Out or L_ED93.

3538.synopsis:
Returns how many columns gap E between words takes when text is spread out: the byte kept
for it in the gap table ((IY-30/29), (IY-78) entries), passed to L_CDCD. With no table it
gives 1; with E past the table, as L_CDCA.
Entry: E = gap number.
Exit: Fc = 0, C = columns; Fc = 1 when the gap is set as a pitch change (L_CDCD), A = the
table byte.
Changes: AF, C.

3574.synopsis:
Takes C from (IY+28) and falls into L_CDCD.
Entry: none.
Exit: as L_CDCD.
Changes: AF, C.

3577.synopsis:
When (IY-70) bits 7 and 4 are both set: if C differs from (IY-89), stores it there and sends
it with code $48 through L_EDF5; returns C = 1, Fc = 1. Otherwise C = 1, Fc = 0.
Entry: C = value.
Exit: C = 1; Fc as above.
Changes: AF, C.

3611.synopsis:
Measures the text at ($1D4D) counting its leading spaces; sets Fc and falls into L_CDF3, the
body of L_CDF2.
Entry: ($1D4D) = text.
Exit: as L_CDF2.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

3614.synopsis:
Measures the text at ($1D4D): its length up to its last character other than a space,
highlight codes $18-$1F not counted and leading spaces not counted (L_CDEF counts them), and
the number of gaps between words.
Entry: ($1D4D) = text.
Exit: C = length; B = gaps; HL at the closing NUL.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

3670.synopsis:
Tests for a highlight code.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: Fc = 1 when A is $18-$1F.
Changes: F.
Keeps: A.

3677.synopsis:
Copies the text at ($1D4D) into the buffer at $1EAA, at most 255 bytes, with its @ fields
expanded (L_CEEC), and points ($1D4D) at the copy.
Entry: B = 0: one string; B = 1: C is a separator: the first character is skipped when C is
not 0, each separator becomes a NUL and two more NULs end the copy.
Exit: ($1D4D) = $1EAA.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

3864.synopsis:
Copies text from HL to IX (L_CF9A) until a NUL is stored, expanding '@' fields: a compiled
reference ($10-$13) through L_CE71, '@T' through L_CEB8, '@D' as today's date (GN_Gmd,
GN_Pdt), '@P' as the number in (IY-91/90) (0 when L_D27D gives Fc = 0), and '@@' as '@'. An
'@' not starting a field is copied.
Entry: HL = text; IX = buffer; E = character stored as NUL; (IY-34) = room left.
Exit: B = last character copied; IX past the copy.
Error: Fc = 1 when the room ran out.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

4038.synopsis:
Stores character A at (IX) and advances IX, storing NUL when A equals E. Counts the room in
(IY-34): when it reaches 0 a NUL is stored instead; when it is already 0 nothing is.
Entry: A = character; E = character turned into NUL; IX = buffer; (IY-34) = room left.
Exit: Fz = 1 when a NUL was stored; Fc = 1 when the room is used up.
Changes: AF, D, IX.
Keeps: C, E, HL.

4071.synopsis:
Skips HL past the current string and its NUL and points ($1D4D) at the next one, then
measures that one (L_CDF2).
Entry: A = field width; HL = text.
Exit: A = entry A; Fz = 1 when the next string is empty; otherwise C = A - its length - 1 (0
when negative).
Error: Fc = 1 when (IY-36) is 0.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4108.synopsis:
Tests whether the slot at column A of the current row is inside the marked block (L_D014):
columns (IY-58) to (IY-55), rows (IY-57/56) to (IY-54/53).
Entry: A = column; (IY-26/25) = row.
Exit: Fc = 1 when inside; Fc = 0 when outside or when there is no mark.
Changes: AF, BC, E, IX.

4160.synopsis:
Orders the marked block's corners: copies the marks (IY-67..IY-62), column then row, to
(IY-58..IY-53) and swaps so that (IY-58), (IY-57/56) hold the first column and row and
(IY-55), (IY-54/53) the last. With no second mark ((IY-64) bit 7 set), both corners are the
first mark.
Entry: (IY-67..IY-62) = marks.
Exit: Fc = 0; corners set.
Error: Fc = 1 when there is no mark ((IY-67) bit 7 set).
Changes: AF, BC, IX.

4259.synopsis:
Converts the internal date at ($1D4D) to text at IY+35 (GN_Pdt, A = $A0, '.' between the
parts) and ends it with a NUL.
Entry: ($1D4D) = 3-byte date.
Exit: text at IY+35.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4281.synopsis:
Works out where a slot appears on screen: adds the widths (L_D547) of the column-table
entries before BC, plus 6 when the left margin is on, and finds the line of entry HL
(L_D0B1).
Entry: HL = line-table entry; BC = column-table entry.
Exit: A = screen column; B = screen line.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4317.synopsis:
Finds the screen line of line-table entry HL: its place in the table counted from 1, plus 1
when the left margin is on (L_D5A7).
Entry: HL = line-table entry.
Exit: A = B = screen line; C = place in the table from 0; DE = ($1D61).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4348.synopsis:
Finds the first column-table entry with bit 7 clear; when the end marker comes first,
returns the first entry.
Entry: ($1D5B) = column table.
Exit: HL = entry; A and flags as L_D0E8.
Changes: AF, HL.

4366.synopsis:
Gives the cursor's row (L_D8B5, from line entry ($1D63)) and falls into L_D0E5 for its
column.
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = row; HL = ($1D5D); A and flags as L_D0E8.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

4369.synopsis:
Reads the cursor's column-table entry ($1D5D) through L_D0E8.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = ($1D5D); A and flags as L_D0E8.
Changes: AF, HL.

4372.synopsis:
Reads column-table entry HL.
Entry: HL = entry.
Exit: A = column (bits 6-0); Fc = 1 for the end marker (bit 6); Fz = 1 when bit 7 is clear.
Changes: AF.

4381.synopsis:
Counts the line-table entries with bit 7 set, up to the end marker (bit 6).
Entry: ($1D61) = line table.
Exit: A = B = count.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL.

4400.synopsis:
Makes the row of the first line-table entry with bits 7 and 5 clear (L_D10E) the current row
(IY-26/25).
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = row; HL = entry.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4410.synopsis:
Finds the first line-table entry with bits 7 and 5 both clear; when the end marker comes
first, takes the first entry. Reads its row (L_D8B8).
Entry: ($1D61) = line table.
Exit: HL = entry; BC = row.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4436.synopsis:
Rebuilds the column table so that column A is on screen and is the cursor's column. When A
is not already in the table, chooses the first column so that A comes near the middle of the
width left beside the bit-7 entries, moving one column if A would be first; then falls into
L_D198.
Entry: A = column.
Exit: as L_D198.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4548.synopsis:
Rebuilds the column table at ($1D5B) from column A. Entries with bit 7 set are kept; the
others take the next columns from A upwards, skipping those already in the table (L_D5B0)
and those of width 0, until the screen width (L_D59D) is used, the columns run out or 64
entries are filled. Points ($1D5D) at column (IY-38)'s entry and ($1D5F) at the last, and
sets bit 6 (end marker) on the entry after it.
Entry: A = first column; (IY-38) = cursor's column.
Exit: table rebuilt.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4629.synopsis:
Sets the row count (IY-97/96) to 1.
Entry: none.
Exit: none.
Changes: none.

4638.synopsis:
Looks for the column to show after the last column-table entry with bit 7 clear: the next
column from it (or that column itself when it is the only such entry, or is not the last
entry ($1D5F)) whose width is not 0 and that is not in the table (L_D5B0).
Entry: ($1D5B) = column table.
Exit: Fc = 0, B = column; HL = the last entry with bit 7 clear.
Error: Fc = 1 when there is none; HL = that entry, or the last entry with bit 7 set when all
have it.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

4725.synopsis:
Makes the cursor's row (L_D8B5) current and falls into L_D24C.
Entry: ($1D63) = cursor's line entry.
Exit: as L_D252.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

4728.synopsis:
Makes row BC the current row (IY-26/25) and falls into L_D252.
Entry: BC = row.
Exit: as L_D252.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

4734.synopsis:
Tests the current row's column-0 cell (L_D7B3).
Entry: (IY-26/25) = row.
Exit: Fc = 1 when it exists and its type bits (byte 3, bits 7-6) are %11, IX = cell;
otherwise Fc = 0.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

4751.synopsis:
Stores A in byte 4 of cell IX and falls into L_D266, which tests A and byte 5 against
(IY+7): Fc = 1 when byte 5 is 0, when A is above (IY+7), or when byte 5 is at least (IY+7) -
A.
Entry: A = value; IX = cell.
Exit: flags as above.
Changes: AF, DE.

4754.synopsis:
Conditional break test for the break cell at IX: compares the lines left on the page with
the count in the cell's byte 5. A = the line on the page; the page length is (IY+7).
Entry: A = line number; IX = cell.
Exit: Fc = 1 when byte 5 of the cell is 0, when A is beyond the page length, or when byte 5
is at least the page length minus A; Fc = 0 otherwise.
Changes: AF, DE.

4772.synopsis:
Tests whether pagination applies: returns at once with Fz = 1 and Fc = 0 when the page
length (IY+7) is 0, otherwise falls into L_D27D.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fz = 1, Fc = 0 when the page length is 0; else as L_D27D.
Changes: AF.

4777.synopsis:
Tests the first entry of the row table at ($1D61) and bit 6 of (IY-70): Fc = 0 only when bit
7 of that entry's flag byte is set and bit 6 of (IY-70) is clear.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1 otherwise.
Changes: F.
Keeps: HL.

4793.synopsis:
Advances a line number by the line spacing: A = 0 gives A = 1; any other A has (IY+8) added
and falls into L_D293.
Entry: A = line number.
Exit: A = the next line number, as L_D293 returns it.
Changes: AF, E.

4799.synopsis:
Brings a line number into the page: with page length (IY+7) of 0 returns A = 1. A value
below the page length is returned unchanged (Fc = 1), one equal to it as is (Fz = 1). A
value past it, or one with bit 7 set, gives A = 0 when L_D278 returns Fc = 1 and A = 1
otherwise.
Entry: A = line number.
Exit: A = the line number on the page.
Changes: AF, E.

4826.synopsis:
Decrements the 16-bit page number at (IY-91) and (IY-90).
Entry: none.
Exit: page number one lower.
Changes: AF.

4839.synopsis:
Increments the 16-bit page number at (IY-91) and (IY-90).
Entry: none.
Exit: page number one higher.
Changes: F.

4847.synopsis:
Steps the pagination state over the row (IY-26)/(IY-25): forwards, or backwards when Fc = 1
on entry (kept in bit 7 of (IY-34)). Starts from the saved page number (IY-93)/(IY-92) and
the line (IY-94), and writes the new line to (IY-94) and the page number back to
(IY-93)/(IY-92).
1. Copies the saved page number to the working one (IY-91)/(IY-90).
2. When L_D252 finds a break cell in column 0 at this row (L_B518 gives IX = cell), forwards
it stores the current line (or page length plus spacing at line 0) in the cell's byte 4 and
starts a new page (line 1) when L_D263 says the break applies; backwards it restores the
line from byte 4 and steps back a page when L_D266 says so.
3. Otherwise (L_D326) it adds or subtracts the line spacing (IY+8), stepping the page at
line 0, and normalises the line through L_D293; a result of 0 is stored with Fc = 1.
Entry: Fc = direction (1 = backwards); (IY-26)/(IY-25) = row.
Exit: (IY-94) = line on the page; (IY-93)/(IY-92) = page number.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

4929.synopsis:
Entry inside L_D2C3: when the line (IY-94) is 0, copies the saved page number to the working
one and continues at L_D326, the step for a row without a break cell; returns at once when
the line is not 0.
Entry: Fc = direction, as L_D2C3; (IY-34) bit 7 already set from it.
Exit: as L_D2C3.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

4995.synopsis:
Brings the pagination state to the row of the first suitable row-table entry: L_D3E9 resets
the state to the document start (row 0, start page, first line) and L_D104 puts that entry's
row in (IY-26)/(IY-25); then falls into L_D35D.
Entry: none.
Exit: as L_D35E.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

5001.synopsis:
Entry inside L_D35E with Fc = 0: works out the pagination state at the row (IY-26)/(IY-25)
from the row (IY-20)/(IY-19), whose state is in (IY-94) to (IY-92).
Entry: (IY-26)/(IY-25) = target row; (IY-20)/(IY-19) = start row.
Exit: as L_D35E.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

5002.synopsis:
Walks the pagination state from the row (IY-20)/(IY-19) to the target row (IY-26)/(IY-25),
one row at a time through L_D2C3, forwards or backwards. When the target is row 0 it only
resets the state (L_D3F0).
1. Swaps the two rows (L_D3C1), so (IY-26)/(IY-25) is the moving row.
2. With Fc = 0 on entry and the line (IY-94) at 0, steps forwards over the start row first
when it holds no break cell.
3. Steps the row towards the target, applying L_D2C3 to each; a break that applies is
stepped over again and the result kept in bit 7 of (IY-36).
4. At the target swaps the rows back.
Entry: (IY-26)/(IY-25) = target row; (IY-20)/(IY-19) = start row; Fc = 1 skips step 2.
Exit: (IY-20)/(IY-19) = (IY-26)/(IY-25) = target row; (IY-94) to (IY-92) = its state; Fc =
the bit last kept in bit 7 of (IY-36).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

5101.synopsis:
Swaps the row (IY-26)/(IY-25) with the row (IY-20)/(IY-19), then rotates (IY-36) left
through the carry.
Entry: none.
Exit: rows swapped; Fc = old bit 7 of (IY-36).
Changes: AF, BC.

5130.synopsis:
Moves the row (IY-26)/(IY-25) one back (L_CA2A) when Fc = 1, otherwise falls into L_D3E1 and
moves it one forward.
Entry: Fc = direction (1 = back).
Exit: row stepped.
Changes: F.

5133.synopsis:
Increments the 16-bit row number at (IY-26) and (IY-25).
Entry: none.
Exit: row one higher.
Changes: F.

5141.synopsis:
Sets the row (IY-20)/(IY-19) to 0 and falls into L_D3F0, which resets the pagination state.
Entry: none.
Exit: as L_D3F0.
Changes: AF.

5148.synopsis:
Resets the pagination state to the document start: the line (IY-94) from (IY+12) and the
saved page number (IY-93)/(IY-92) from the start page (IY+10)/(IY+11).
Entry: none.
Exit: state reset.
Changes: A.

5167.synopsis:
Rebuilds the row table at ($1D61) (6-byte entries: flag byte, row number, page number) for
the screen with row BC as the cursor row.
1. Limits BC to the last row (one below the row count (IY-97)/(IY-96), L_C9F9) and stores it
in (IY-24)/(IY-23) and (IY-26)/(IY-25).
2. Counts the entries with bit 7 set, then moves the top row back from BC by half of the
lines L_D590 gives minus one minus that count, not counting rows those entries hold
(L_D5D7).
3. Continues at L_D452.
Entry: BC = cursor row.
Exit: row table rebuilt; ($1D63) = the cursor row's entry.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

5246.synopsis:
Entry inside L_D403: sets (IY-20)/(IY-19) to the row of the first suitable row-table entry
(L_D10E); unless the first entry has bit 7 set, brings the pagination state to the top row
(IY-26)/(IY-25) through L_D35E; then continues at L_D469.
Entry: (IY-26)/(IY-25) = top row; (IY-24)/(IY-23) = cursor row.
Exit: as L_D469.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

5269.synopsis:
Entry inside L_D403: fills the row table at ($1D61) (6-byte entries: flag byte, row number,
page number) from the top row (IY-26)/(IY-25) with the pagination state in (IY-94) to
(IY-92), one entry for each of the lines L_D590 gives. Each entry gets its row and page
number. A line where a page break falls gets flag bit 5 and does not use up a row; entries
with bit 7 set keep their own row while it is below the row count. The table ends with $40
at the first line past the last row. ($1D63) is set to the entry of the cursor row
(IY-24)/(IY-23).
Entry: (IY-26)/(IY-25) = top row; (IY-24)/(IY-23) = cursor row.
Exit: row table rebuilt.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

5491.synopsis:
Reads the column number from the column list byte at HL (L_D0E8) and falls into L_D54A.
Entry: HL = column list entry.
Exit: A = byte 0 of that column's record.
Changes: AF.

5494.synopsis:
Returns byte 0 of column A's 10-byte record at ($1D3F) (the column's width; L_D8D1 sets 12
for a new column).
Entry: A = column number.
Exit: A = byte 0 of the record.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

5501.synopsis:
Returns byte 1 of column A's 10-byte record at ($1D3F), or byte 0 when byte 1 is 0.
Entry: A = column number.
Exit: A = byte 1 of the record, or byte 0.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

5513.synopsis:
Searches the column list at ($1D5B) from its start for the column A (bit 7 of each entry
ignored, L_D0E8), up to the entry with bit 6 set.
Entry: A = column number.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1, HL = the matching entry.
Error: Fc = 1 when the end of the list is reached.
Changes: AF, E, HL.

5527.synopsis:
Looks up row BC in the row table at ($1D61) (6-byte entries: flag byte, row number, page
number), skipping entries with bit 5 set, up to the entry with bit 6 set.
Entry: BC = row number.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1, HL = the entry.
Error: Fc = 1, HL = the end entry, when the row is not in the table.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

5564.synopsis:
Returns the number of entries the row table ($1D61) covers: (IY-80) minus 1, minus one more
when bit 1 of (IY-69) is set (L_D5A7).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = number of lines; E = (IY-80) - 1; Fc as L_D5A7.
Changes: AF, E.

5577.synopsis:
Returns (IY-81), less 6 when bit 1 of (IY-69) is set (L_D5A7).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = (IY-81) or (IY-81) - 6.
Changes: AF.

5587.synopsis:
Tests bit 1 of (IY-69).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1 when the bit is set; A = (IY-69) AND 2.
Changes: AF.

5596.synopsis:
Searches the column list at ($1D5B) for column A, among the entries that have bit 7 set,
stopping at the first entry without it or after 64 entries.
Entry: A = column number.
Exit: Fc = 1 when found, Fc = 0 when not; A = column number.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

5629.synopsis:
Stores BC as the row (IY-26)/(IY-25) and falls into L_D5D7.
Entry: BC = row number.
Exit: as L_D5D7.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

5635.synopsis:
Looks for the row (IY-26)/(IY-25) among the leading entries of the row table at ($1D61)
(6-byte entries: flag byte, row number, page number) that have flag bit 7 set and bit 6
clear.
Entry: (IY-26)/(IY-25) = row number.
Exit: Fc = 1, HL = the entry, when one of them holds the row.
Error: Fc = 0 at the first entry with bit 7 clear or bit 6 set.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

5665.synopsis:
Table of 12 entries of 4 bytes read by L_D631: a word with a block size and the address of
the word that receives the block allocated for it (sizes $41, $41, $32, $100, $0F, $0F, $3C,
$3C, $32, $32, $64, $64 for the pointers at $1D5B, $1D61, $1D75, $1D3D, $1D65, $1D67, $1D69,
$1D6B, $1D6D, $1D6F, $1D71, $1D73).

5725.synopsis:
Sets up PipeDream's memory and workspace at start-up.
1. Opens a memory pool for segment 0 (OS_Mop, handle in $1D39) and allocates the 12 blocks
of L_D5F5 from it (L_D96E), storing each address in its pointer.
2. Allocates a $E5-byte block, points IY $7F bytes into it and binds its bank into segment 0
(OS_Mpb); clears some flags and variables.
3. Opens a second pool for segment 1 with multiple banks (handle in $1D3B) and builds the
fast bank switching code for segment 1 at $1D7F (OS_Fc).
4. Clears the column list ($1D5B) and the row table ($1D61); reads the PA_Iov panel setting
(OS_Nq) and sets bit 2 of (IY-71) unless it is 'I'; calls L_E0EA.
5. Sets the start page to 1 and (IY+12) to 1 and continues at L_D6D9. On a failure to open a
pool it leaves with OS_Bye and RC_Room; on a failed allocation it first closes the pool
(OS_Mcl).
Entry: none.
Exit: workspace ready; IY = workspace pointer.

5893.synopsis:
Resets the document to an empty sheet: keeps only bit 2 of (IY-71), zeroes a set of
variables (among them the column count (IY-98)), empties the strings at ($1D6D), ($1D6F) and
($1D71), sets the column pointers $1D5D and $1D5F to ($1D5B) and $1D63 to ($1D61), calls
L_D1E9, clears the 64 column records at ($1D3F) and the column list, clears the flags of the
first 8 row-table entries, calls L_E7CA and continues at L_D758, which ends both tables with
$40, lays out the screen from row 0 (L_D403) and leaves through L_D128 with A = 0.
Entry: none.

6005.synopsis:
Creates six columns (L_D8CD), sets byte 1 of their records from 72 through L_D76C (A = 0, C
= $48) and continues at L_D758: ends the row table and the column list with $40, lays out
the screen from row 0 (L_D403) and leaves through L_D128 with A = 0.
Entry: none.

6040.synopsis:
Stores C in byte 1 of the record of column A, then for each following column (up to 63)
subtracts the previous column's byte 0 from C and stores the result, stopping when the
subtraction goes below 0.
Entry: A = first column; C = value for that column.
Exit: B = column after the last one written.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

6058.synopsis:
Saves A, C and B in (IY-110), (IY-109) and (IY-108).
Entry: A = column; BC = row.
Exit: values saved.
Changes: none.

6068.synopsis:
Returns the word in bytes 2 and 3 of column A's record, or 0 when its bit 15 is set.
Entry: A = column number.
Exit: BC = the word, or 0.
Changes: F, BC, HL.

6083.synopsis:
Saves A and BC through L_D77E, then looks up the cell they name (falls into L_D79A).
Entry: A = column; BC = row.
Exit: as L_D7B3.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

6086.synopsis:
Looks up the cell whose column and row L_D77E saved in (IY-110) to (IY-108), through L_D7AD
and L_D7B3.
Entry: none.
Exit: as L_D7B3; A, BC = the saved column and row.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

6097.synopsis:
Looks up the cell of column A at row $7FFF (through L_D7AD and L_D7B3).
Entry: A = column number.
Exit: as L_D7B3.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

6102.synopsis:
Looks up the cell under the cursor: the row from the current row-table entry ($1D63) and the
column from the column list entry at ($1D5D) (L_D0E2), then L_D7AD.
Entry: none.
Exit: as L_D7B3.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

6105.synopsis:
Stores BC as the row (IY-26)/(IY-25) and falls into L_D7B3.
Entry: A = column; BC = row.
Exit: as L_D7B3.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

6111.synopsis:
Looks up the cell of column A at the row (IY-26)/(IY-25). Each column's 10-byte record at
($1D3F) remembers a row (bytes 2-3, bit 15 set when the column has no cells) and the cell
there with its neighbour (bytes 4-6 and 7-9, address and bank). The cells form a list whose
links are the XOR of the neighbours' addresses and banks; the routine walks it forwards or
backwards from the remembered row, binding each cell's bank in segment 1 (L_D887), and
stores the position it reaches back in the record.
Entry: A = column; (IY-26)/(IY-25) = row.
Exit: Fc = 0: IX = the cell, (IY-127) to (IY-125) = its address and bank, bank bound in
segment 1.
Error: Fc = 1 when A is not below the column count (IY-98), the column has no cells or no
cell has that row.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

6323.synopsis:
Binds bank A into segment 1 through the fast bank switching code at $1D7F (set up by OS_Fc)
and records it in (IY-111).
Entry: A = bank.
Exit: bank bound.
Changes: none known (the code at $1D7F is built by OS_Fc).

6329.synopsis:
Returns the record of the current column: the column number from the column list entry at
($1D5D) (L_D0E5), then L_D890.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = column number; HL = its record.
Changes: AF, HL.

6332.synopsis:
Returns the address of column A's 10-byte record: ($1D3F) + 10 * A.
Entry: A = column number.
Exit: HL = the record.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE.

6349.synopsis:
Stores the row of the current row-table entry ($1D63) in (IY-26)/(IY-25).
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = the row; HL = the entry.
Changes: BC, HL.

6359.synopsis:
Stores the row of the current row-table entry ($1D63) in (IY-24)/(IY-23).
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = the row; HL = the entry.
Changes: BC, HL.

6369.synopsis:
Returns the row of the current row-table entry: HL = ($1D63), then L_D8B8.
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = the row; HL = the entry.
Changes: BC, HL.

6372.synopsis:
Returns the row number held in bytes 1 and 2 of the row-table entry at HL.
Entry: HL = entry.
Exit: BC = the row.
Changes: BC.
Keeps: HL.

6379.synopsis:
Adds columns (L_D8CD) until column A exists, that is until A is below the column count
(IY-98).
Entry: A = column number.
Exit: Fc = 0 when the column exists.
Error: Fc = 1, C = 5 when the 64-column limit is reached.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

6393.synopsis:
Adds a column after the last one, unless there are already 64 (L_D8E9), and falls into
L_D8D1.
Entry: none.
Exit: as L_D8D1.
Error: Fc = 1, C = 5 when there are 64 columns.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

6397.synopsis:
Initialises the record of column A: byte 0 = 12, bytes 1-9 = 0 except byte 3 = $80 (no
remembered row), and increments the column count (IY-98).
Entry: A = column number.
Exit: Fc = 0; HL = record + 3; A = 0.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

6421.synopsis:
Tests the column count (IY-98) against the limit of 64 (falls into L_D8EC).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = column count; Fc = 1 and C = 5 when it is 64 or more.
Changes: AF, C.

6424.synopsis:
Tests A against the limit of 64 columns.
Entry: A = column count or number.
Exit: Fc = 1 when A is 64 or more, Fc = 0 otherwise; C = 5.
Changes: F, C.

6430.synopsis:
Initialises the cell block last allocated by L_D926: L_D948 makes it current; the three link
bytes are cleared, byte 3 gets the cell flags (IY-36), and one more byte (bit 7 of the flags
set) or six more bytes (clear) are cleared.
Entry: (IY-36) = cell flags.
Exit: Fc = 0; HL = the block, its bank bound in segment 1.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

6476.synopsis:
Allocates a cell block for C = (IY-40) and B = (IY-42) (falls into L_D926).
Entry: none.
Exit: as L_D926.
Changes: AF, BC, D, HL, IX.

6482.synopsis:
Allocates a cell block from the segment 1 pool ($1D3B) with OS_Mal: C plus 4 bytes, plus 6
more when bit 7 of B is clear; B is saved as the cell flags in (IY-36). The block's address
and bank go to $1D36-$1D38 (the previous bank there is passed to OS_Mal in A).
Entry: B = cell flags; C = length.
Exit: Fc = 0, block allocated.
Error: Fc = 1, C = 1 when OS_Mal fails.
Changes: AF, BC, D, HL, IX.

6516.synopsis:
Makes the block at $1D36-$1D38 the current cell: copies its address and bank to (IY-127) to
(IY-125) and binds the bank in segment 1 when it is not already (L_D887).
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = block address; A = its bank.
Changes: AF, HL.

6538.synopsis:
Frees the block at (IY-117)/(IY-116) in the bank bound in segment 1 (IY-111) to the segment
1 pool ($1D3B) with OS_Mfr.
Entry: BC = block size.
Exit: as OS_Mfr: Fc = 0 on success.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Changes: AF, HL, IX.

6554.synopsis:
Allocates BC bytes from the segment 0 pool ($1D39) with OS_Mal (A = 0).
Entry: BC = size.
Exit: Fc = 0, BHL = the block.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX.

6562.synopsis:
Frees the block at (IY-117)/(IY-116) to the segment 0 pool ($1D39) with OS_Mfr, taking the
bank from the binding of segment 0 (OS_Mgb).
Entry: BC = block size.
Exit: as OS_Mfr: Fc = 0 on success.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Changes: AF, HL, IX.

6582.synopsis:
Runs a form of prompts and fields (a dialog) described at HL, and returns when the user
confirms or leaves it. After a leading byte each item is a type byte (bits 0-3: type 1-12,
bit 7: it has a Yes/No part, bit 6: type 1 reads the "NAME" mailbox), its zero-ended prompt,
four more bytes for type 7, and a byte giving the Yes/No part's start value; a 0 ends the
list. Each type has a text buffer (L_DBF7) and a check routine (table L_DD1A).
1. With bit 6 of (IY-71) set it reports error 25 (L_EB07) instead.
2. Records the form in (IY-32)/(IY-31) and the Yes/No states at IY+$4D onwards.
3. Draws the prompts (L_DC5C) and edits the fields one at a time (L_DC91); the keys of
L_DBD1 edit the text, others move between items or toggle Yes/No.
4. On confirm checks each used field with its routine and reports a failure (L_EB07), going
back to editing; otherwise closes the form (L_DBB4).
Entry: HL = form description.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = the Yes/No states ORed together (Fz = 1 when none is set).
Error: Fc = 1 when the form is left with the escape key code ($35).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

6799.synopsis:
Zero-ended name "NAME": the mailbox L_D98A reads with OS_Sr (SR_RPD) into the type 1 buffer
at $1FAA (50 bytes) for an item that has bit 6 set.

7135.synopsis:
Closes a form: L_E0D4 and the sequence 1, "2D2" sent with OS_Pout, then L_B411, L_BDD2 and
L_B411 again, which it leaves through.
Entry: none.

7154.synopsis:
Sets bit 7 of C when the type byte of form item B has bit 7 set (the item has a Yes/No
part).
Entry: B = item number.
Exit: C bit 7 set for such an item; A = type byte.
Changes: AF, C, E, HL.

7163.synopsis:
Key code list for the form editor (L_D98A, through L_E593): 11 codes that are passed to
MthKeyAction while a text field is edited, ended by $FF.

7175.synopsis:
When bit 0 of (IY-72) is set, clears it and copies the zero-ended edit buffer at ($1D3D) to
the text buffer of form item B (L_DBF7).
Entry: B = item number.
Exit: buffer updated.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

7201.synopsis:
Returns the text buffer of form item B: jumps through the table L_DC1D by the item's type
(bits 0-3 of its type byte).
Entry: B = item number.
Exit: HL = buffer; C = its size (0 when the type has none).
Changes: AF, C, DE, HL.

7220.synopsis:
Returns form item B of the form at (IY-32)/(IY-31): skips B items (L_DD05).
Entry: B = item number.
Exit: HL = the item; A = its type byte.
Changes: AF, E, HL.

7239.synopsis:
Table of 12 words: for each form item type 1-12, the routine that returns its text buffer in
HL and its size in C (L_DC35 to L_DC59), read by L_DBF7.

7263.synopsis:
Text buffer of form item type 1: HL = $1FAA, C = 50.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = buffer; C = size.
Changes: C, HL.

7269.synopsis:
Text buffer of form item types 3, 7 and 12: HL = ($1D67), C = 15.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = buffer; C = size.
Changes: C, HL.

7275.synopsis:
Text buffer of form item types 2, 5, 10 and 11: HL = ($1D65), C = 15.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = buffer; C = size.
Changes: C, HL.

7281.synopsis:
Text buffer of form item type 6: HL = ($1D71), C = 100.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = buffer; C = size.
Changes: C, HL.

7287.synopsis:
Text buffer of form item type 8: HL = ($1D6D), C = 50.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = buffer; C = size.
Changes: C, HL.

7293.synopsis:
Text buffer of form item type 9: HL = ($1D6F), C = 50.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = buffer; C = size.
Changes: C, HL.

7299.synopsis:
Form item type 4 has no text buffer: C = 0.
Entry: none.
Exit: C = 0.
Changes: C.

7302.synopsis:
Draws the form at (IY-32)/(IY-31): each item's prompt on its own line from column 1
(L_EEE4), then its field (L_DC91 with C = 0) and, for an item with a Yes/No part, that part
too (C = $80).
Entry: none.
Exit: form drawn.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

7355.synopsis:
Shows the field of form item B: with bit 7 of C set, or for a type with no text buffer,
writes "Yes" or "No" from the item's state (L_DCCB); otherwise copies the item's buffer to
the edit buffer ($1D3D) and displays it for editing (L_E585, L_E5C5). The field starts at
column $28, or $2C for the text part of an item with a Yes/No part; (IY-28)/(IY-27) get its
column and line, (IY-86) the buffer size.
Entry: B = item number; C bit 7 = the Yes/No part.
Exit: Fc = 0 when a text field is ready for editing, Fc = 1 when Yes/No was written.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.
Keeps: BC.

7413.synopsis:
Shows a dialog field's Yes/No state: puts the cursor at column $28 of row B + 1, prints "No
" or "Yes" by the field's state byte (L_DCEF), and puts the cursor back at column $28, row B
+ 1.
Entry: B = field number; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Changes: AF.

7447.synopsis:
Reads a dialog field's Yes/No state byte (at IY+$4D+B, L_DCF7) and tests it.
Entry: B = field number; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: A = the state byte; Fz = 1 when it is zero (No).
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

7455.synopsis:
Returns the address of a dialog field's Yes/No state byte: IY + $4D + B.
Entry: B = field number; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: HL = IY + $4D + B.
Changes: F, HL.
Keeps: BC, DE.

7469.synopsis:
Steps over one entry of a dialog's field list. An entry is a type byte, a zero-terminated
prompt, four more bytes when the type's low nibble is 7, and a last byte (the initial Yes/No
state when bit 7 of the type is set).
Entry: HL = the entry's type byte.
Exit: HL = the entry's last byte.
Changes: AF, HL.
Keeps: BC, DE.

7490.synopsis:
Table of 12 words: the routine that checks and stores a dialog field's text, for field types
1 to 12 (the low nibble of the field's type byte). L_DB47 calls the entry through L_B8B4
with HL = ($1D65) and DE = the field's entry; a routine returns Fc = 1 with C = the message
number when the text is not accepted.

7514.synopsis:
Field type 1 (L_DD1A): parses the file name in the buffer at $1FAA with GN_Prs.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0; C = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_xxx); C = 0, so the OZ error is reported.

7525.synopsis:
Field type 4 (L_DD1A): a Yes/No field has no text, so it accepts at once.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Changes: F.

7527.synopsis:
Field type 3 (L_DD1A): reads two decimal numbers from the text at ($1D67) (L_DFFB) and
stores them as words at IY+51 and IY+54.
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0; IY+51/IY+52 = the first number; IY+54/IY+55 = the second.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $0E when a number is missing.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

7556.synopsis:
Field type 5 (L_DD1A): reads a column (L_DDBB) into IY+53 and an optional second column
(L_DFEA) into IY+54; a missing second column repeats the first.
Entry: HL = the field's text; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $21 when the first column is missing; Fc = 1, C = $0E when the second
column comes before the first.

7579.synopsis:
Field type 6 (L_DD1A): continues in L_BC6D (bank 5) with HL = ($1D71), the type's text
buffer (L_DC47), IX = ($1D73) and Fc = 0.
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.

7590.synopsis:
Field type 7 (L_DD1A): reads a decimal number from the text at ($1D67) (L_DFFB), stores it
as a word at IY+51 and checks it against the minimum and maximum words that follow the
prompt in the field's entry. An empty text gives 0.
Entry: DE = the field's entry (its type byte); IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0; IY+51/IY+52 = the number.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $11 when the number is out of range.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

7651.synopsis:
Field type 10 (L_DD1A), also called by L_DD5C: reads a column (L_DFEA) and stores it at
IY+53.
Entry: HL = the field's text; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = the column; IY+53 = the column.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $21 when no column is given.

7665.synopsis:
Field type 11 (L_DD1A): reads a slot reference (L_DFE0) and stores it at IY+$35 and IY+$38,
then reads an optional second one into IY+$38; then L_DE4A copies the six bytes from IY+$35
to IY-$3A and checks them through L_FBBD.
Entry: HL = the field's text; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $0B when a reference is not valid; Fc = 1, C = $0E when L_FBBD rejects
the pair.

7709.synopsis:
Field type 2 (L_DD1A): reads a slot reference (L_DFE0), or takes the current slot (L_D0E2,
L_D77E) when the text is blank, and stores its three bytes at IY+$38 (L_DE0D).
Entry: HL = the field's text; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0; HL = IY + $3B.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $0B when the reference is not valid.

7733.synopsis:
Copies the three bytes at IY-110, IY-109 and IY-108 (the column and row the last slot
reference parse left there) to (HL) onwards and advances HL past them. Entry inside L_DDF5.
Entry: HL = destination; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: HL = HL + 3.
Changes: A, HL.

7749.synopsis:
Field type 12 (L_DD1A): the same as L_DDC9 for the text at ($1D67): reads one or two slot
references into IY+$3B and IY+$3E, then L_DE4A copies the six bytes from IY+$3B to IY-$3A
and checks them through L_FBBD.
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $0B when a reference is not valid; Fc = 1, C = $0E when L_FBBD rejects
the pair.

7820.synopsis:
Field type 8 (L_DD1A): compiles the text at ($1D6D) into the buffer at ($1D69) (L_DEAA) with
bits 6 and 7 of IY+29 clear, then sets bit 6 and stores the end of the compiled bytes at
IY+32/IY+33.
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0; bit 6 of IY+29 set.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $20 when the text is blank or compiles to nothing (bit 6 left clear); Fc
= 1 with L_DEAA's C when it fails.

7870.synopsis:
Field type 9 (L_DD1A): compiles the text at ($1D6F) into the buffer at ($1D6B) (L_DEAA) and
sets bit 7 of IY+29 when that succeeds, clears it when it fails.
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0; bit 7 of IY+29 set.
Error: Fc = 1 with L_DEAA's C; bit 7 of IY+29 clear.

7890.synopsis:
Compiles a text into a byte string. Characters are copied as they are; a "^" and the next
character (in upper case) is looked up in L_DFA8: "^^" gives "^", the others run a routine
of L_DFC7 that appends a zero and a code byte (and for some an argument). The string ends
with $00, $0A. The output pointer is kept at IY-36/IY-35 and the count at IY-38 (L_DF88).
Entry: HL = the text (ends at a zero or CR); DE = destination.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = number of bytes written; HL = past the text and its CR.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $1F for an unknown "^" code, $1E when the string grows to 60 bytes, or
the code of a failed slot reference.

7990.synopsis:
"^R" in L_DEAA (L_DFC7): appends $00, $02, then either "#" and an optional digit (L_DF77) or
$10 and the three bytes of the slot reference that follows (L_DFE0).
Entry: HL = the "R" in the text; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0; HL = the reference's last character.
Error: Fc = 1 when nothing or no valid reference follows.

8038.synopsis:
"^B" in L_DEAA (L_DFC7): appends $00, $00; refused (Fc = 1) when bit 6 of IY+29 is set.
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1.
Changes: AF, E.

8048.synopsis:
"^#" in L_DEAA (L_DFC7): appends $00, $04 and an optional digit (L_DF77).
Entry: HL = the "#" in the text; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $1F or $1E (L_DF77, L_DF88).
Changes: AF, C, E, HL.

8052.synopsis:
"^?" in L_DEAA (L_DFC7): appends $00, $06 and an optional digit (L_DF77); shares its tail
with L_DF48.
Entry: HL = the "?" in the text; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $1F or $1E (L_DF77, L_DF88).
Changes: AF, C, E, HL.

8068.synopsis:
"^1" to "^9" in L_DEAA (L_DFC7): appends $00, $0C and the digit's character code minus $19.
Entry: HL = the digit in the text; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $1E (L_DF88).
Changes: AF, C, E.

8082.synopsis:
"^S" in L_DEAA (L_DFC7): appends $00, $08.
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $1E (L_DF88).
Changes: AF, C, E.

8095.synopsis:
Reads the optional digit after a "^#", "^?" or "^R#" code (L_DEAA). Returns at once when bit
6 of IY+29 is clear; otherwise the next character must be "1" to "9", and its value minus
one is appended (falls into L_DF88).
Entry: HL = the code character; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0; HL = the digit when one was read.
Error: Fc = 1, C = $1F, and the caller's return address is dropped (returns to its caller).
Changes: AF, C, HL.

8112.synopsis:
Appends a byte to the compiled string of L_DEAA: stores A at the pointer in IY-36/IY-35,
advances it and counts it in IY-38.
Entry: A = byte; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: when the count reaches 60: Fc = 1, C = $1E, and the caller's return address is
dropped (returns to its caller).
Changes: AF.
Keeps: HL.

8144.synopsis:
Table of the "^" codes L_DEAA knows, as pairs of a character and a code, ending with $00:
"1" to "9" give $8A, "B" $88, "R" $80, "#" $82, "?" $84, "^" "^" and "S" $86. A code with
bit 7 set selects a routine of L_DFC7 (bits 0-6 are its offset); one without is stored as it
is.

8175.synopsis:
Table of 6 words: the routines of L_DEAA's "^" codes, by the offset in L_DFA8's code: L_DF0E
("R"), L_DF48 ("#"), L_DF4C ("?"), L_DF6A ("S"), L_DF3E ("B"), L_DF5C ("1"-"9").

8187.synopsis:
Skips spaces in a text.
Entry: HL = the text.
Exit: HL = the first character that is not a space; A = that character; Fz = 1 when it is a
zero or a CR (the end of the text).
Changes: AF, HL.

8200.synopsis:
Skips spaces and parses a slot reference (L_BD57); the column and row are left at IY-110 to
IY-108.
Entry: HL = the text; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fz = 0; Fc = 0; HL = past the reference; E = 1.
Error: Fz = 1, Fc = 1 when the text is blank; Fz = 0, Fc = 1 when the reference is not
valid.

8210.synopsis:
Skips spaces and parses a column name (L_BD91).
Entry: HL = the text; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fz = 0; A = the column (IY-110); E = 1; HL = past the column name.
Error: Fz = 1 when the text is blank or holds no column name.

8227.synopsis:
Skips spaces and reads a decimal number (L_EE29, GN_Gdn).
Entry: HL = the text.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0: BC = the number, HL = past it; Fc = 0, Fz = 1: no number.
Error: Fz = 1, Fc = 1 when the text is blank.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

8238.synopsis:
Waits for a one-key answer: purges the keyboard buffer (L_EB49) and reads a key without a
timeout (L_E02C). Callers use it for questions such as "Overwrite text?".
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0: A = the character, a command code below $20, or $20 for any other command.
Error: Fc = 1, A = $1B for ESCAPE; Fc = 1, A = RC_Esc after a pre-emption has redrawn the
screen (L_BDD2); Fc = 1, A = RC_OK or RC_Time otherwise.

8276.synopsis:
Reads a key: switches the cursor on, waits with OS_Tin (L_E090), switches the cursor off,
fetches a command with OS_In after a zero, and ignores control codes. RC_Quit leaves
PipeDream (Exit_PipeDream).
Entry: Fc = 1 for a timeout of $2D centiseconds (unless bit 5 of IY-68 is set); Fc = 0 waits
without a timeout.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fv = 0: A = the character (>= $20); Fc = 1, Fv = 0: A = the MTH command code
minus one (for MthKeyAction); ESCAPE gives A = $35.
Error: Fv = 1 (Fc = 0): A = RC_OK after the timeout, RC_Esc after RC_Draw (pre-emption),
RC_Time for any other error.
Changes: AF, BC.

8376.synopsis:
Reads a byte with OS_Tin and acknowledges an ESCAPE (L_E097).
Entry: BC = timeout in centiseconds.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = the byte.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_xxx).
Changes: AF.

8383.synopsis:
Acknowledges an ESCAPE and flushes the input buffer (OS_Esc, SC_ACK).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1.
Changes: F.
Keeps: A.

8391.synopsis:
Puts the cursor back at the position L_E0A7 saved in $1D7D (L_EEE4).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = column + $20; BC = the saved position.
Changes: AF, BC.

8399.synopsis:
Saves the cursor position of the current window (OS_Nq, NQ_WCUR) in $1D7D for L_E09F.
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = the position (C = column, B = row).

8411.synopsis:
Defines window 1, PipeDream's text window, at the top left of the screen with 8 rows and
selects it (falls into L_E0D4). With A = 0 the width leaves room for the map (L_E0EA);
otherwise it is A columns.
Entry: A = 0, or the width; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: IY-81 = width - 1; IY-80 = 8.

8443.synopsis:
Selects window 1 (VDU 1, "2H1").
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, C.

8447.synopsis:
Selects window 2 (VDU 1, "2H2"); shares its tail with L_E0D4.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, C.

8465.synopsis:
Defines the map in window 5 with OS_Map (MP_DEF) at the panel's width; stores the map's
pixel width at IY+100 (0 when there is no map) and 64 rows at IY+101; then sets the text
window's size from the columns left over (falls into L_E0FC).
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: IY-81 = $5D - the map's character width (the text window's width - 1); IY-80 = 8.

8483.synopsis:
Sets the text window's size variables: IY-81 = A - 1 (width - 1) and IY-80 = 8 (rows).
Entry: A = width; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: A = A - 1.
Changes: AF.

8492.synopsis:
Draws the page map when the panel has one (IY+100 > 0); the main loop calls it when it has
waited for a key without one coming.
1. Clears the map's variables at $1D77-$1D7B and its pixel line at $1FDD (L_E309).
2. Lays the current page out again from its first row with the output routine L_E1F9, which
turns each printed character into a pixel (L_E2A9) and each line into a map line (L_E2D8).
3. Stops when a key is waiting (L_E31D), ESCAPE is pressed (L_F023) or the map is full,
writes the remaining lines and restores the saved row variables.
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0 when the map was finished; Fc = 1 when it was stopped.

8912.synopsis:
Sets the map pixel of the current column ($1D77) in the pixel line at $1FDD (bit 7 is the
leftmost pixel of each byte), then advances the column (falls into L_E2CB).
Entry: none.
Exit: as L_E2CB.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

8946.synopsis:
Advances the map column $1D77 by one unless that reaches the map's width (IY+100).
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0 when advanced.
Error: Fc = 1 at the right edge (column unchanged).
Changes: AF.

8959.synopsis:
Writes the pixel line at $1FDD to the map at row $1D78 (OS_Map, MP_WR, window 5), clears it
(L_E309), sets the column $1D77 to 0 and advances the row. When the row reaches IY+101 it
sets bit 7 of $1D79 (the map is full).
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 when the map is (or becomes) full.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

9008.synopsis:
Clears the map's pixel line at $1FDD: (IY+100 + 7) / 8 bytes.
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: A = 0; B = 0; HL = past the line.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

9028.synopsis:
Examines the input with OS_Xin (is a key or pre-emption waiting).
Entry: none.
Exit: as OS_Xin: Fc = 0 when input is waiting.
Changes: AF.

9031.synopsis:
Runs the command whose MTH code minus one is in A, through MthKeyJmpTable. A code of $5F or
above is not a command and returns at once.
Entry: A = command code - 1 (as L_E02C returns it).
Exit: as the command's routine; Fc = 0 when A >= $5F.
Changes: AF, DE, HL, and what the command changes.

9047.synopsis:
Table of 95 words: the routine of each PipeDream command, by its MTH command code minus one
(the codes of mthcmd in mth/appmth.asm): 0 Mark Block, 6 Sort, 18 ENTER, 32 the COBRA easter
egg, 52 Swap Case, 57 Load, 58 Save, 59 Name, 81 Options Page, 82 Print, ... Read by
MthKeyAction.

9237.synopsis:
The Options Page command (<>O). Shows the page (L_E614) and lets the user edit the 22
options of L_E8F4. IY-44 holds the current option.
1. Cursor Up and Down, ENTER, move between the options, wrapping round; each move stores the
edited value first (L_E747).
2. A typed character is inserted (numbers in overtype); in a field with choices it must be
one of the choices and replaces the value; Next Option (<>J) steps through the choices.
3. Other commands run only when they are in L_E5A2 (MthKeyAction); the rest beep.
4. ESCAPE or <>O again stores the value, applies the options (L_E7CA), restores the text
window and redraws the screen (L_BDD2).
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.

9578.synopsis:
Copies the current option's field width (the byte before its code, at (IY-48) - 1) to IY-86.
Entry: IY-48/IY-47 = the option's code (L_E7A5).
Exit: A = IY-86 = the width.
Changes: A, HL.

9590.synopsis:
Returns the text of an option of L_E8F4: its value in the document's option list when it has
one (L_EA7C), otherwise its default (falls into L_E559).
Entry: A = option number (1-22); IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: HL = the zero-terminated value.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX; IY-4, IY-48/IY-47 (L_E7A5).

9600.synopsis:
Copies the current option's default value to IY+$23: the whole text after the two-letter
code for a number, only its first character for a text or a field with choices.
Entry: IY-48/IY-47 = the option's code; IY-4 = its flags (L_E7A5).
Exit: HL = IY + $23 (the default, zero-terminated).
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

9644.synopsis:
Copies a zero-terminated string to the edit buffer at ($1D3D).
Entry: HL = the string.
Exit: HL = its terminator; DE = the copy's terminator.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

9658.synopsis:
Looks up a command code in a $FF-terminated list of bytes, comparing bits 0-6 of each.
Entry: A = code; HL = the byte before the list.
Exit: Fc = 0; B = the matching byte (bit 7 is the entry's flag); HL = its address.
Error: Fc = 1 when the code is not in the list.
Changes: AF, B, E, HL.

9673.synopsis:
List of the command codes (MTH code minus one) the Options Page (L_E3EE) lets run, ending
with $FF; bit 7 of an entry is a flag L_E3EE tests after the command. Searched by L_E593.

9708.synopsis:
Sets bit 5 of IY-72 and shows the edit line (falls into L_E5C9).
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.

9712.synopsis:
Shows the edit line in the current field and puts the cursor at the edit position. The end
column is the field width IY-86, plus the field's column IY-28 when the width is less than
the text window's (IY-81); it goes to IY-42 and IY-89, IY-85 is cleared, then L_C45E (with A
= the window's width - 1) and L_C43C do the work.
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.

9743.synopsis:
Starts editing the current option (IY-44): copies its value (L_E54F) to the edit buffer
(L_E585), takes its width (L_E543) and sets its screen position (L_E7A5, falls into L_E5FC).
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: as L_E5FC.

9763.synopsis:
Sets the screen position of an option's value: the column after its label plus one space to
IY-28 and its row to IY-27.
Entry: HL = the option's entry in L_E8F4 (its column byte); IY-48/IY-47 = its code.
Exit: A = the column; B = the row; HL = the entry's row byte.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL.

9787.synopsis:
Draws the Options Page: defines and clears the text window, prints the file name (or "No
File"), "Insert" or "Overtype", "Microspace" when it is on, the page number and the free
memory (OS_Nq, NQ_Mfs) on the right, then each of the 22 options of L_E8F4 with its label
and its value (L_E54F).
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.

10058.synopsis:
Starts editing the current option (L_E5E8), puts the cursor at its value, points IY-52/IY-51
at its choices (two bytes past its code) and marks the edit line unchanged (bit 0 of IY-72
clear, bit 7 set).
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.

10087.synopsis:
Stores the edited value of the current option when it was changed (bit 0 of IY-72): makes a
node for it in the document's option list (L_EA9C) and copies the text into it (L_E775); an
empty value only removes the old node. A failure is reported (L_EB07).
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.

10133.synopsis:
Binds the option node (L_B518) and copies a zero-terminated string into it from IX+5.
Entry: HL = the string; IY-127..IY-125 = the node's address.
Exit: HL = past the terminator; IX = past the copy.

10147.synopsis:
Reads the current option's two-letter code into BC and points HL at the option list's head.
Entry: IY-48/IY-47 = the code's address (L_E7A5).
Exit: C = the first letter; B = the second; HL = $1D43.
Changes: BC, HL.

10160.synopsis:
Reads an option's value (L_E54F). For an option that holds a number (bit 0 of IY-4) it
converts the text with GN_Gdn (L_EE29); otherwise it returns its first character.
Entry: A = option number (1-22); IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = the first character, or the number's low byte (BC = the number).
Error: Fc = 1, A = 0 when a number option does not hold a number.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10181.synopsis:
Finds an option's entry in L_E8F4 and records its flags in IY-4 and the address of its
two-letter code in IY-48/IY-47.
Entry: A = option number (1-22).
Exit: HL = the entry (its column byte); DE = the entry's terminator.
Changes: AF, C, DE, HL.

10218.synopsis:
Applies the options to the workspace: decimal places to IY+9, line spacing to IY+8, the
start page to IY+10-IY+12, the lines per page left after the margins, header and footer
(L_E8CF, L_E8DE) to IY+7, the leading and trailing characters to IY+$16 and IY+$10 (lengths
at IY+14 and IY+15), and the flags in IY-69: Text (bit 5), Columns (4), Auto (3), Minus (2),
Insert on wrap Row (0), Borders (1, redrawing them when changed), Justify (6), Wrap (7).
Entry: IY = PipeDream's workspace.

10419.synopsis:
Sets the bit mask A in IY-69 when option B is "Y", clears it otherwise (falls into L_E895
with C = "Y").
Entry: A = mask; B = option number; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10421.synopsis:
Sets the bit mask A in IY-69 when the first character of option B (in upper case) is C,
clears it otherwise.
Entry: A = mask; B = option number; C = the letter; IY = PipeDream's workspace.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10455.synopsis:
Copies a zero-terminated string from HL to DE + 1 onwards and counts its characters.
Entry: HL = the string; DE = the byte before the destination.
Exit: B = the length; HL, DE = the terminator and its copy.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL.

10467.synopsis:
Skips spaces and tests for the end of the text.
Entry: HL = the text.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = the first character that is not a space; HL = its address.
Error: Fc = 1 at the zero terminator.
Changes: AF, HL.

10479.synopsis:
Adds up the numeric values (L_E790) of options $0F to $0E + B (the top, header, footer and
bottom margins of L_E8F4).
Entry: B = number of options.
Exit: A = C = the sum; B = 0.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10494.synopsis:
Counts the non-blank options among $14 and $15 (the header and footer texts, L_E8C3).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = the count (0-2).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10516.synopsis:
The Options Page's 22 options. Each entry is a column and a row, the label (right-aligned in
three columns), a flag byte ($80 text, $81 number, $82 choices, $83 choices and number), the
field width, the two-letter code the option is saved under, and the default (for a field
with choices, the choices), zero-terminated. Read by L_E7A5 and L_E614.

10908.synopsis:
Finds an option in the document's option list: follows the chain of nodes from the word at
(HL) to one whose code (IX+3, IX+4) is C, B. A word with a zero high byte ends the chain.
Entry: HL = the head (or a link); BC = the two-letter code.
Exit: Fc = 1, Fz = 0: found; IX = the node; HL = its value (IX+5); DE = the link to it.
Error: Fc = 0 when not found; DE = the last link.
Changes: AF, DE, HL, IX.

10940.synopsis:
Replaces an option's node in the document's option list: allocates A + 6 bytes (L_D96E),
unlinks and frees the old node with this code (L_D976), and links the new one at the end of
the chain with its size and code. With A = 0 it only removes the old node.
Entry: A = the value's length; BC = the two-letter code; HL = the list's head.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = the new node (bound, L_B518) when A > 0.
Error: Fc = 1, C = 1 when the memory cannot be allocated.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

11045.synopsis:
The COBRA easter egg command (MTH code 33): reports message $25 through L_EB07 (falls into
it with C = $25).
Entry: none.
Changes: as L_EB07.

11047.synopsis:
Shows an error message on the status line (row 0, from column 7) after a beep, then purges
the keyboard buffer. C = 0 prints the last OZ error's own text (OS_Erc, GN_Esp); C = $14
prints the file name in the buffer at $1FAA followed by " not found"; any other C is a
PipeDream message number from the L_EC31 table, expanded by L_EB4D. The printed length is
kept in (iy-84) so that L_EFC4 can erase it.
Entry: C = message number (1-37), or 0 for the last OZ error.
Exit: Fc = 1; (iy-84) = length of the message; bit 2 of (iy-72) set (by L_EED0).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL; IX for a numbered message.

11112.synopsis:
Shared exit of L_EB07: purges the keyboard buffer with OS_Pur and returns Fc = 1.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1.

11116.synopsis:
Expands message number A of the compressed table at L_EC31 and writes it, one character at a
time, through the routine in IX, at most C characters. The table's messages follow one
another, each ending with a byte that has bit 7 set; in a message a byte whose low 7 bits
are below $20 stands for that word (1-based) of the dictionary at L_EBDB. The first
character written is made upper case.
Entry: A = message number (1-based); C = room for characters; IX = output routine (A =
character).
Exit: A = E = number of characters written; (iy-74) = room left.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

11183.synopsis:
Writes one character of an expanded message (for L_EB4D). When there is room (C not 0) it
writes A with bit 7 cleared through the routine in IX, upper case when it is the first (E =
0, through GetUppercase), and counts it.
Entry: A = message or dictionary byte; C = room left; E = characters written so far; IX =
output routine.
Exit: A = byte as given; Fs = its bit 7 (end of word or message); Fc = 0; C one less and E
one more when the character was written.

11203.synopsis:
Prints the text of the last OZ error (OS_Erc, then GN_Esp for its message), reading it with
GN_Rbe and writing it with OS_Out, at most C characters.
Entry: C = room for characters (not 0).
Exit: C = number of characters printed; Fz = 1 when the whole message was printed.
Changes: AF, BC, E, HL.

11224.synopsis:
Sets C to the width of the current window (L_EEFE), keeping AF.
Entry: none.
Exit: C = window width.
Changes: C.

11231.synopsis:
PipeDream's error handler, installed with OS_Erh and called by OZ with A = error code, Fz =
1 for a fatal error and Fc = 1.
1. A fatal error returns at once with Fc = 1, so OZ shows its error box.
2. RC_Quit leaves PipeDream through Exit_PipeDream.
3. RC_Dvz to RC_Exr ($46-$4B), the arithmetic errors, return Fc = 0, Fz = 0 and HL = L_F3AD:
OZ then jumps to L_F3AD, which unwinds the function call in progress (SP from $1D55) and
turns the error into a PipeDream error value.
4. Every other code, RC_Bdn included, returns Fz = 1, Fc = 0, and the error goes back to the
call that raised it.
Entry: A = error code; Fz = 1 if fatal; Fc = 1.
Exit: as above.

11258.synopsis:
Data: the dictionary of 16 words used by the messages at L_EC31, each ending with a byte
that has bit 7 set: "bad ", "field", "file", "not ", "error", "no ", "too many ",
"overflow", "column", "too ", "long", "expression", "range", "list", "mark", "argument".
L_EB4D finds word n by counting end bytes from L_EBDB-1.

11344.synopsis:
Data: PipeDream's 37 messages, compressed. The label is the last byte of the dictionary at
L_EBDB; message 1 starts at the next byte. Each message ends with a byte that has bit 7 set,
and a byte whose low 7 bits are below $20 stands for a dictionary word. They are 1 "Memory
full", 2 "FP overflow", 3 "Stack overflow", 4 "Escape", 5 "too many columns", 6 "Divide by
0", 7 "-ve root", 8 "bad argument", 9 "no marked block", 10 "Typing error", 11 "bad slot",
12 "Loop", 13 "Log range", 14 "bad range", 15 "Lookup", 16 "bad index", 17 "bad number", 18
"too few arguments", 19 "Propagated", 20 "file not found", 21 "Line too long", 22 "bad
date", 23 "bad option", 24 "bad list file", 25 "Editing expression", 26 "no list file", 27
"End of list", 28 "no name for save", 29 "Edge", 30 "too long", 31 "bad ^ field", 32 "no
target", 33 "bad column", 34 "All columns zero width", 35 "Overlap", 36 "Exp range", 37
"mark Colton". Read by L_EB4D.

11593.synopsis:
Copies 51 ($33) bytes from the buffer that ($1D75) points to into the buffer at $1FAA.
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = 0.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.

11601.synopsis:
Copies 51 ($33) bytes from the buffer at $1FAA into the buffer that ($1D75) points to.
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = 0.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.

11614.synopsis:
Reads the last segment of the file name that ($1D75) points to (GN_Esa, A = 0, B = -1) into
the buffer at $1FAA and names the current activity with it through DC_Nam.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = $1FAA.

11634.synopsis:
Clears bits 6 and 0 of (iy-70) and falls into L_ED5B.
Entry: none.

11642.synopsis:
Entry inside L_ED53: when bit 7 of (iy-70) is set, clears it and sends the printer filter
sequence $05 "1]" (filter off) through the output vector (L_EDC2).
Entry: none.

11659.synopsis:
Points the output vector at the routine that sends characters to the printer filter with
OS_Prt (L_EDCF) and falls into L_ED6F.
Entry: none.

11662.synopsis:
Entry inside L_ED6C: sets the output vector ($1D49) to HL and clears the pending space count
(iy-83) and (iy-89). When bit 0 of (iy-70) is set it then sends the printer filter sequence
$05 "1[" (filter on) through the vector and sets bit 7 of (iy-70).
Entry: HL = output routine (takes the character in A).

11689.synopsis:
Writes a space: to the screen through L_F015 when bit 6 of (iy-70) is clear, otherwise
through L_ED93.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = $20 when written to the screen.

11698.synopsis:
Writes character A through the output vector ($1D49), holding spaces back: a space only adds
one to the count in (iy-83), unless bit 4 of (iy-70) is set; a CR drops the count; any other
character first writes the counted spaces.
Entry: A = character.
Changes: AF.

11728.synopsis:
Calls the routine in the output vector ($1D49) with the character in A, keeping HL (a jump
through the vector).
Entry: A = character.

11745.synopsis:
Writes the zero-terminated string that follows the call instruction through the output
vector (L_EDB1) and returns to the byte after its terminator.
Entry: the string follows the CALL.
Exit: A = 0.

11781.synopsis:
Sends the printer filter sequence $05 "1S" (reset the attributes) through the output vector.
Entry: none.

11789.synopsis:
Gets the value L_E790 returns for A = 5 and sends it as the printer filter's page length:
falls into L_EDF5 with C = "P".
Entry: none.

11796.synopsis:
Sends the printer filter sequence $05 "2", C, A + $20 through the output vector (L_EDC2,
L_EDB1). The source shows the inline string's terminator and the following LD A,C as one LD
(nn),A.
Entry: A = parameter; C = command letter.
Exit: A as given.

11800.comment: LEDE1 string: $05 "2", 0 (printer code prefix; code in A)

11848.synopsis:
Reads a decimal number at (HL) with GN_Gdn, at most 30 characters, into BC.
Entry: HL = text.
Exit: a number was read: A = 1, Fz = 0, BC = value; otherwise Fz = 1.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

11866.synopsis:
Writes the zero-terminated text in the buffer at IY+$23 with OS_Out, stopping early when the
count in (iy-74) runs out.
Entry: (iy-74) = most characters to write (not 0).
Exit: (iy-74) counted down.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

11885.synopsis:
Builds "~ " and the number in (ix+5) of the record L_B518 points IX to, in decimal, as a
zero-terminated text in the buffer at IY+$23.
Entry: none.
Exit: (iy-74) = length of the text plus one.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL, IX.

11909.synopsis:
Stores A in the buffer at IY+$23 at index (iy-74) and adds one to (iy-74). The output
routine L_EE88 gives L_EE8F.
Entry: A = character.
Changes: none but (iy-74).

11931.synopsis:
Writes HL in decimal to the screen (OS_Out through L_F020), without leading zeros.
Entry: HL = value.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL, IX.

11937.synopsis:
Appends A in decimal to the buffer at IY+$23 (L_EE66), without leading zeros.
Entry: A = value; (iy-74) = index of the next character.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL, IX.

11942.synopsis:
Writes HL in decimal at the start of the buffer at IY+$23: falls into L_EE88 with A = 0.
Entry: HL = value.

11943.synopsis:
