Writes HL in decimal into the buffer at IY+$23 from index A, without leading zeros. Then
L_EE8F (also reached from L_EE7C) divides HL by each power of ten in L_EEC6 and passes each
digit to the routine in DE through L_EEBA.
Entry: A = index; HL = value.
Exit: (iy-74) = index after the last digit.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL, IX.

11993.synopsis:
Passes digit A, as ASCII, to the routine in DE, unless it is a leading zero (A = 0 while bit
7 of B is clear); B becomes $FF once a digit is written.
Entry: A = digit (0-9); B = 0 before the first digit written; DE = output routine.
Changes: AF, B.

12005.synopsis:
Data: the words 10000, 1000, 100 and 10 and a zero word that ends the table; the divisors of
the decimal conversion in L_EE8F.

12015.synopsis:
Erases the status message (L_EFC4), sets bit 2 of (iy-72) and moves the cursor to column 7
of row 0 (L_EEE4).
Entry: none.

12028.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to column 7 of row 0 of the current window (L_EEE4).
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, B.

12034.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to column 0 of row B: falls into L_EEE4 with A = 0.
Entry: B = row.

12035.synopsis:
Moves the cursor of the current window to column A, row B, with the VDU sequence $01 "3@" x
y (OS_Out).
Entry: A = column; B = row.
Exit: A = column + $20.
Changes: AF.

12061.synopsis:
Returns the width of the current window: OS_Nq NQ_Wbox for window 0, keeping BC.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = width in characters.
Keeps: BC.

12072.synopsis:
Data: the activity words "Load", "Save", "Sort", "Calculat", "Replicat" and "Search", each
ending with a byte that has bit 7 set. L_EF34 shows the word at the byte offset in bits 0-6
of (iy+6) and adds "ing".

12105.synopsis:
Tests whether the status line is free for an activity message.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fz = 0 when bit 2 of (iy-72) or bit 6 of (iy-70) is set; Fz = 1 when both are clear.
Changes: F.

12115.synopsis:
Shows the activity message ("Loading", "Saving", ...) once the small timer has run out. It
returns at once when L_EF2A gives Fz = 0 or the message is already shown (bit 7 of (iy+6)).
It reads the small timer with OS_Ust, putting the old value back when it has not run out.
When it has run out it sets bit 7 of (iy+6), prints the word from L_EF09 at offset (iy+6)
and "ing" in flash and reverse from column 7 of row 0, stores the length in (iy-84) and
stops the timer (L_EF7B).
Entry: BC = value given to OS_Ust for a moment (put back when the timer has not run out).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

12184.synopsis:
Stops the small timer: OS_Ust with BC = 0.
Entry: none.
Exit: BC = the timer's old value; Fz = 1 when it had run out.
Changes: AF, BC.

12189.synopsis:
Starts an activity: stores its code in (iy+6) and, unless bit 6 of (iy-70) is set, clears
the status line (L_EFBB) and starts the small timer at 30 ($1E) with OS_Ust, after which
L_EF34 shows the activity's name.
Entry: A = byte offset of the activity's word in L_EF09.
Changes: AF, BC.

12206.synopsis:
When bit 2 of (iy-72) is set it clears that bit and returns. Otherwise it calls L_D7AA, and
unless that gives Fc = 1 or bit 7 of (ix+3) is set, writes text from column 7 of row 0
through L_BB73 (with A = space), records its length (iy-34) in (iy-84) and writes spaces
over the rest of a longer old message (L_C5EA). In the other cases it erases the status
message (L_EFC4).

12248.synopsis:
Stops the small timer (L_EF7B) and, when L_EF2A gives Fz = 1, erases the status message
(L_EFC4).
Entry: none.

12257.synopsis:
Erases the status message: when its length (iy-84) is not 0, moves the cursor to column 7 of
row 0, sets (iy-84) to 0 and writes that many spaces (L_C5EA).
Entry: none.

12274.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to column 40 ($28) of row 0 and clears to the end of the line (L_EFDC).
Entry: none.

12281.synopsis:
Clears the current window's line from the cursor to its end: the VDU sequence $01 "2C" $FD
(OS_Pout).
Entry: none.

12289.synopsis:
Writes a form feed ($0C), which clears the current window, with OS_Out (L_F020).
Entry: none.

12293.synopsis:
Sounds the bell: writes $07 with OS_Out.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1.

12299.synopsis:
Toggles reverse video: the VDU sequence $01 "R" (OS_Out).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF.

12310.synopsis:
Turns the cursor off: falls into the VDU sequence $01 "2-C" (OS_Out).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC.

12315.synopsis:
Turns the cursor on: the VDU sequence $01 "2+C" (OS_Out).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC.

12348.synopsis:
Tests for Escape with OS_Esc (SC_BIT).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1 when an Escape is pending, otherwise Fc = 0.
Keeps: A.

12361.synopsis:
Writes the zero-terminated string at HL with OS_Out and counts its characters.
Entry: HL = string.
Exit: C = number of characters; HL = byte after the terminator; A = 0.
Changes: AF, C, HL.

12372.synopsis:
Multiplies HL by A (shift and add, 8 steps).
Entry: HL = multiplicand; A = multiplier.
Exit: HL = product; A = high byte of the product; Fc = 1 when the product is over 255.
Changes: AF, HL.
Keeps: BC, DE.

12394.synopsis:
Divides HL by A (restoring division, 8 steps).
Entry: HL = dividend, H less than A; A = divisor.
Exit: L = quotient; A = remainder; H = 0.
Changes: AF, HL.
Keeps: BC, DE.

12411.synopsis:
Evaluates an expression. It sets up the evaluation stack (($1D45) = $1EAA, growing down to
$1DAA) and the source pointer ($1D4F), saves SP in ($1D47) for the error exit L_F0A6, and
parses with L_F0AF; anything left before the end token ($0F) is a "Typing error" (message
10). The result is taken off the stack (L_F309) and passed to L_F9D2. An error leaves type 0
with the message number in ($1D4D).
Entry: HL = expression; B = its bank (stored in (iy-112)).
Exit: C = type of the result (iy-79); HL = ($1D4D), the result or a pointer to it; B =
(iy-124).

12475.synopsis:
Parses an expression at the lowest precedence: operands parsed by L_F0CA, joined by OR
(operator token C = $0D, L = $2A, FuncID_Or). Each operator is applied through L_F225 to the
two values on the evaluation stack.
Entry: the next token waiting (L_FD0C, L_FD2E).
Exit: the value pushed on the evaluation stack.

12502.synopsis:
Parses operands of L_F0E5 joined by AND (operator token L = $1E, FuncID_And), applying each
through L_F225. One level of the expression parser under L_F0AF.

12529.synopsis:
Parses operands of L_F103 joined by a comparison (operator tokens L = $23-$28, FuncID_Less
to FuncID_GreaterEqual), applying each through L_F225. One level of the expression parser.

12559.synopsis:
Parses operands of L_F122 joined by + or - (operator tokens L = $20, $21), applying each
through L_F225. One level of the expression parser.

12590.synopsis:
Parses operands of L_F141 joined by * or / (operator tokens L = $1F, $22), applying each
through L_F225. One level of the expression parser.

12621.synopsis:
Parses operands of L_F15F joined by ^ (operator token L = $29, FuncID_Raise), applying each
through L_F225. One level of the expression parser.

12651.synopsis:
Parses a unary operand of the expression parser and pushes its value.
1. A leading +, - or NOT (operator token L = $20, $21, $1D) parses a further operand here; +
adds nothing, - applies FuncID_Negate and NOT applies FuncID_Not (L_F225).
2. "(" parses a whole expression (L_F0AF) and needs ")".
3. A value token (type $03, $05, $07 or $08) is pushed as it is (L_F237).
4. A function token ($0E) gives the function ID in bits 0-5 of L and its arguments in bits
6-7: none, one in brackets, or a list in brackets (L_F1E0); the function is then applied
through L_F225. Anything else is a "Typing error" (message 10, L_F1DB).

12780.synopsis:
Parses a function's argument list, each argument through L_F1FE, separated by commas, and
pushes the number of arguments as a type 1 value (L_FD3F, L_F237).
Entry: the first argument's token waiting.
Exit: the arguments and their count on the evaluation stack.

12810.synopsis:
Parses one function argument: a type $04 token is taken and pushed as it is (L_F237);
anything else is parsed as a whole expression (L_F0AF).

12849.synopsis:
Applies function or operator L: calls its routine from FunctionRoutineTable through L_F3A3,
which keeps SP in ($1D55) for the error handler. When the routine returns Fc = 1, its A
becomes an error value (L_F339). Then the current value, type (iy-79) at ($1D4D), is pushed
on the evaluation stack: it reserves the type's size (L_F375), fails with "Stack overflow"
(message 3) when the stack reaches $1DAA, stores the value through the type's handler
(L_F291, L_F281) and the type byte below it (L_F273).
Entry: L = FuncID_xxx.
Exit: the result pushed on the evaluation stack.

12941.synopsis:
Data: table of 8 words, the handlers that store a value pushed on the evaluation stack
(L_F225), selected through L_F291: L_F29C, L_F2BE, L_F2C2, L_F2C6, L_F2A1, L_F2D4, L_F2F1,
L_F2A5.

12957.synopsis:
Data: 11 bytes, one per value type 0-10: the index of the type's store handler in L_F281 (0,
0, 1, 2, 3, 0, 2, 5, 4, 6, 7). L_F344 uses the same index with L_F366 when it takes a value
off the stack.

12968.synopsis:
Store handler for value types 0, 1 and 5: stores the byte in ($1D4D) at HL.
Entry: HL = last byte of the new stack entry.
Changes: A.

12973.synopsis:
Store handler for value type 8: copies 4 bytes from the value that ($1D4D) points to
(L_F2C8).
Entry: HL = last byte of the new stack entry.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.

12977.synopsis:
Store handler for value type 10: converts the floating-point value in the FPP registers to
an integer with FP_INT and stores its 4 bytes as a type 8 value.
Entry: HL = last byte of the new stack entry.
Exit: (iy-79) = 8.

13002.synopsis:
Store handler for value type 2: copies 5 bytes from the value that ($1D4D) points to
(L_F2C8).
Entry: HL = last byte of the new stack entry.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.

13006.synopsis:
Store handler for value types 3 and 6: copies 3 bytes from the value that ($1D4D) points to
(L_F2C8).
Entry: HL = last byte of the new stack entry.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.

13010.synopsis:
Store handler for value type 4: copies 7 bytes from the value that ($1D4D) points to.
L_F2C8, shared by the copying handlers, copies C bytes downwards so that the last lands at
HL.
Entry: HL = last byte of the new stack entry.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.

13024.synopsis:
Store handler for value type 7: stores it as a type 2 value, copying the 5 bytes at
$1D96-$1D9A (L_F2DC).
Entry: HL = last byte of the new stack entry.
Exit: (iy-79) = 2.
Changes: DE, HL.

13032.synopsis:
Entry inside L_F2D4: copies the 5 bytes at $1D96-$1D9A to HL upwards.
Entry: HL = destination.
Changes: A, DE, HL.

13053.synopsis:
Store handler for value type 9: stores the floating-point value in the FPP registers as a
5-byte type 2 value.
Entry: HL = last byte of the new stack entry.
Exit: (iy-79) = 2.

13077.synopsis:
Takes the top value off the evaluation stack and makes it the current value: (iy-79) = its
type and ($1D4D) a pointer to it, or for types 0, 1 and 5 its byte in ($1D4D) (L_F344).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = C = type; B = 0; HL = ($1D45), the new top.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

13096.synopsis:
Fetches an argument of a function that takes an argument list; the top of the evaluation
stack holds the number of arguments. When there are more than A, it makes argument A
(counted from 0) the current value (L_F325) and returns Fc = 1. Otherwise the current value
becomes the error "too few arguments" (message 18), the arguments and the count are dropped
(L_F380), and it returns to its caller's caller.
Entry: A = argument index.
Exit: Fc = 1 with the argument current; or the error, returned past the caller.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

13105.synopsis:
Reads argument A of a function's argument list. The item at the top of the evaluator stack
(pointer in ($1D45)) is the argument count (type 1); when the count is above A, L_F341 skips
to argument A (arguments are numbered from the deepest) and reads it. Otherwise the current
item becomes error $12 through L_F339.
Entry: A = argument index (0 = first).
Exit: Fc = 1; C = item type, also in (iy-79); B = item size; HL and ($1D4D) = its data (for
a one-byte item ($1D4D) holds the byte itself).
Error: Fc = 0; A = $12; (iy-79) = 0, ($1D4D) = $12.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

13125.synopsis:
Shared exit: makes the current evaluator item an error: (iy-79) = 0 (type error) and the
error number in ($1D4D). Flags are left as they are.
Entry: A = PipeDream error number.
Changes: none (memory only).

13133.synopsis:
Skips A items from the top of the evaluator stack (L_F38D) and falls into L_F344 to read the
item reached.
Entry: A = number of items to skip.
Exit: as L_F344.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

13136.synopsis:
Reads the evaluator stack item at HL: its type byte goes to C and (iy-79), ($1D4D) is set to
the data after it, and B gets the item's size from L_F375. Then it continues through the
handler of the type's class (L_F29D, a table outside this slice, indexes L_F366): for class
0 (types 0, 1 and 5, one byte of data) L_F370 puts the data byte itself in ($1D4D).
Entry: HL = item (its type byte).
Exit: C = type; B = size in bytes, type byte included; HL = data; (iy-79), ($1D4D) set.
Changes: A (class 0), BC, DE, HL.

13170.synopsis:
Table of 5 words: the handler L_F344 runs for each class of item type (class from the table
at $F29D). Class 0 is L_F370, which copies the data byte into ($1D4D); classes 1-4 are
L_F374, a plain return. Only types 0-6 and 8 (classes 0-4) are kept on the stack: the push
code stores result types 7, 9 and 10 as type 2 or 8.

13180.synopsis:
Class 0 handler of L_F344: stores the item's one data byte at (HL) in ($1D4D), replacing the
pointer's low byte; falls into L_F374.
Entry: HL = item data.
Changes: A.

13184.synopsis: Shared exit: a plain return. The class 1-4 handler of L_F344 (table L_F366).

13185.synopsis:
Table of 11 bytes: the size in bytes, type byte included, of an evaluator stack item of each
type 0-10 (2, 2, 6, 4, 8, 2, 4, 6, 5, 6, 5). Read when items are pushed (L_F237) and skipped
(L_F38D, L_F344).

13196.synopsis:
Drops a function's argument list from the evaluator stack: reads the count from the top
item, skips count + 1 items (the count item and the arguments) and stores the new top in
($1D45). L_F386 is the entry that drops A items.
Entry: count item at the top of the stack ($1D45).
Exit: ($1D45) and HL = new top of the stack.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL, IX.

13209.synopsis:
Steps over A items of the evaluator stack, starting at its top ($1D45), adding each item's
size from L_F375.
Entry: A = number of items.
Exit: HL = the item reached ($1D45 itself when A = 0); B = 0.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL, IX.

13231.synopsis:
Calls a function routine: saves SP in ($1D55) and jumps to the routine at DE (through
L_9223, JP (HL)). A floating point error inside it ends at L_F3AD, which restores SP and
returns from here with Fc = 1 and A = a PipeDream error number.
Entry: DE = routine address (from FuncRoutineTable).
Exit: Fc = 0; result as the routine leaves it ((iy-79), ($1D4D) or HL'HLC).
Error: Fc = 1, A = PipeDream error number (from L_F3AD).

13264.synopsis:
Table of 4 bytes: the OZ floating point errors that L_F3AD translates: RC_Dvz ($46), RC_Nvr
($48), RC_Lgr ($49) and RC_Exr ($4B).

13268.synopsis:
Table of 4 bytes: the PipeDream error numbers for L_F3C4's errors. CPIR leaves BC = entries
after the match, so the order is reversed: RC_Exr gives $24, RC_Lgr $0D, RC_Nvr $07 and
RC_Dvz $06. Any other error gives $02.

13272.synopsis:
Table of 44 words: the routine of each spreadsheet function and operator, in FuncID order
(fnAbs ... fnYear, then fnNot, fnAnd, the arithmetic and comparison operators, fnRaise, fnOr
and fnNegate). L_F225 indexes it with the function ID ($3F mask) and calls the routine
through L_F3A3.

13360.synopsis:
ABS function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_ABS. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13363.synopsis:
Entry inside fnAbs: applies FP_ABS to the number in HL'HLC and returns.
Entry: HL'HLC = number.
Exit: HL'HLC = absolute value.

13366.synopsis:
ACS function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_ACS. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13372.synopsis:
ASN function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_ASN. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13378.synopsis:
ATN function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_ATN. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13384.synopsis:
CHOOSE function: returns the argument chosen by the first one. The first argument must be a
number from 1 to 65535 (L_FBFE), else error $10; the count goes to (iy-30..29) and L_FADF
walks the arguments from the second on, ranges slot by slot, with L_F46A counting down. The
item reached becomes the result; when the list runs out the result is error $12. The
argument list is dropped.
Entry: argument list at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: result in (iy-79) and ($1D4D).

13451.synopsis:
COL function: returns the current column (iy-110) plus 1 as a number, through L_F666.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL'HLC = column number (integer form); (iy-79) = 9.

13459.synopsis:
COS function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_COS. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13465.synopsis:
COUNT function: counts the numeric, non-blank values among its arguments, ranges slot by
slot (L_FADD with L_F4A4 counting in (iy-30..29)), and returns the count as a number.
Entry: argument list at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = count (integer form); (iy-79) = 9.

13500.synopsis:
DAY function: takes a date argument through L_F924 and returns its day of the month (bits
4-0 of C from GN_Die) as a number.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = day (integer form); (iy-79) = 9.
Error: a non-date argument gives error $16 (L_F924).

13512.synopsis:
DEG function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_DEG. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13518.synopsis:
EXP function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_EXP. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13524.synopsis:
IF function: evaluates the first argument; when it is a non-zero number the second argument
is the result, when it is zero or not a number the third one is. The chosen argument goes
through L_F9BE, its type becomes (iy-79), and the argument list is dropped.
Entry: argument list at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: result in (iy-79) and ($1D4D).

13558.synopsis:
INDEX function: takes a column and a row number (both from 1, through L_FC0C and L_FBFE;
otherwise error $10) and returns a reference to that slot (L_FB68, type 3, column - 1 and
row - 1). The argument list is dropped.
Entry: argument list at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: (iy-79) = 3; ($1D4D) = the reference at (iy+35).

13615.synopsis:
INT function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_INT. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13621.synopsis:
LN function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_LN. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13627.synopsis:
LOG function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_LOG. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13633.synopsis:
LOOKUP function: finds the first argument in the range given as the second and returns the
slot at the same position in the range given as the third.
1. A numeric key is stored at $1DA0; a string key's address and bank go to (iy-120..118). An
error or range key gives error $0F.
2. Walks the second range (L_FB35, L_FB55), counting in (iy-28..27), until a slot of the
key's type matches: FP_CMP for numbers, L_F7DF (with wildcards) for strings.
3. Walks the third range the same number of steps and makes its slot the result. A missing
match, a range argument that is not a range or a range too short gives error $0F. The
argument list is dropped.
Entry: argument list at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: result in (iy-79) and ($1D4D).

13827.synopsis:
MAX function: clears bit 7 of (iy-30) for MAX and continues in fnMin's body (L_F5FB), which
returns the largest numeric value among the arguments, ranges slot by slot. Non-numeric and
blank values are ignored; without any number the result is zero.
Entry: argument list at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9.

13830.synopsis:
MIN function: sets bit 7 of (iy-30) and returns the smallest numeric value among the
arguments, ranges slot by slot. The value kept so far is at $1DA0; bit 7 of (iy-29) marks
the first number, and L_F61F compares each number with it. Non-numeric and blank values are
ignored; without any number the result is zero.
Entry: argument list at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9.

13910.synopsis:
MONTH function: takes a date argument through L_F924 and returns its month (B from GN_Die)
as a number.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = month (integer form); (iy-79) = 9.
Error: a non-date argument gives error $16 (L_F924).

13919.synopsis:
PI function: returns pi (FP_PI).
Entry: none.
Exit: HL'HLC = pi; (iy-79) = 9.

13926.synopsis:
RAD function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_RAD. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13932.synopsis:
ROW function: returns the current row (iy-109..108) plus 1 as a number, falling into L_F666.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL'HLC = row number (integer form); (iy-79) = 9.

13949.synopsis:
SGN function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_SGN. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13955.synopsis:
SIN function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_SIN. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13961.synopsis:
SQR function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_SQR. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

13967.synopsis:
SUM function: adds the numeric values among its arguments, ranges slot by slot, into the
total at $1DA0 (L_FADD with L_F69F); non-numeric and blank values are ignored.
Entry: argument list at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = sum; (iy-79) = 9.

14020.synopsis:
TAN function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_TAN. A non-numeric
argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

14026.synopsis:
YEAR function: takes a date argument through L_F924 and returns the year modulo 100 (GN_D24
divides GN_Die's year by 100) as a number.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = year mod 100 (integer form); (iy-79) = 9.
Error: a non-date argument gives error $16 (L_F924).

14043.synopsis:
NOT operator: takes a numeric operand through L_FAC7 and returns 1 when it is zero, 0
otherwise.
Entry: operand at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = 0 or 1 (integer form); (iy-79) = 9.

14053.synopsis:
AND operator: takes both operands through L_F93F and returns 1 when both are non-zero, 0
otherwise (L_F6EE on each). A non-numeric operand becomes the result instead.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = 0 or 1 (integer form); (iy-79) = 9.

14074.synopsis:
Turns the number in HL'HLC into a truth value with FP_TST.
Entry: HL'HLC = number.
Exit: A = 0 and Fz = 1 when it is zero; A = 1 and Fz = 0 otherwise.
Changes: AF.

14082.synopsis:
Multiplication operator: takes both operands through L_F93F and applies FP_MUL. A
non-numeric operand becomes the result instead.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = result type from L_F93F.

14088.synopsis:
Addition operator: takes both operands through L_F93F and applies FP_ADD. A non-numeric
operand becomes the result instead.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = result type from L_F93F.

14094.synopsis:
Subtraction operator: takes both operands through L_F93F and applies FP_SUB. When both
operands are dates (type $0A) the result type is 9, a plain number. A non-numeric operand
becomes the result instead.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = result type from L_F93F.

14110.synopsis:
Division operator: takes both operands through L_F93F and applies FP_DIV. A non-numeric
operand becomes the result instead.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = result type from L_F93F.

14116.synopsis:
"<" operator: compares the two operands with L_F770 and returns 1 (L_F732) when the left
operand is less than the right one, 0 (L_F769) otherwise. Operands that cannot be compared
give 0.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = 1 or 0; (iy-79) = 9.

14123.synopsis:
"<=" operator: compares the two operands with L_F770 and returns 1 (L_F732) when the left
operand is less than or equal to the right one, 0 (L_F769) otherwise. Operands that cannot
be compared give 0.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = 1 or 0; (iy-79) = 9.

14130.synopsis:
"<>" operator: compares the two operands with L_F770 and returns 1 (L_F732) when the
operands differ, 0 (L_F769) otherwise. Operands that cannot be compared give 0.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = 1 or 0; (iy-79) = 9.

14137.synopsis:
"=" operator: compares the two operands with L_F770 and returns 1 (L_F732) when the operands
are equal, 0 (L_F769) otherwise. Operands that cannot be compared give 0.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = 1 or 0; (iy-79) = 9.

14149.synopsis:
">" operator: compares the two operands with L_F770 and returns 1 (L_F732) when the left
operand is greater than the right one, 0 (L_F769) otherwise. Operands that cannot be
compared give 0.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = 1 or 0; (iy-79) = 9.

14156.synopsis:
">=" operator: compares the two operands with L_F770 and returns 1 (L_F732) when the left
operand is greater than or equal to the right one, 0 (L_F769) otherwise. Operands that
cannot be compared give 0.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = 1 or 0; (iy-79) = 9.

14163.synopsis:
Power (^) operator operator: takes both operands through L_F93F and applies FP_PWR. A
non-numeric operand becomes the result instead.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = result type from L_F93F.

14169.synopsis:
OR operator: takes both operands through L_F93F and returns 1 when either is non-zero, 0
otherwise (L_F6EE on each). A non-numeric operand becomes the result instead.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = 0 or 1 (integer form); (iy-79) = 9.

14187.synopsis:
Unary minus function: takes its numeric argument through L_FAC7 and applies FP_NEG. A
non-numeric argument (a slot reference resolved first) becomes the result as it is.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = result; (iy-79) = 9 (number).

14204.synopsis:
Compares the two operands of a comparison operator and drops them from the evaluator stack.
1. Reads the left operand (L_F97F, A = 1) and the right one (A = 0). An error operand, or
one L_F909 does not accept, drops both and returns from the operator with 0 (L_F765).
2. Keeps the left type in (iy-36), a left string's address and bank in (iy-123..121), a
right one's in (iy-120..118), and a left number at $1DA5. A blank ($0C) takes the other
operand's type; any other type mismatch gives 0.
3. Numbers, dates and blanks are compared with FP_CMP; strings with L_F7DF.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: Fz = 1 when equal; Fc = 1 when the left operand is the smaller (as fnLess reads it).

14315.synopsis:
Compares the string at (iy-123..121) (address, bank) with the one at (iy-120..118), ignoring
letter case and leading spaces and codes $18-$1F (L_F8B4, L_F8CB). The second string may
hold wildcards read by L_F8E8: ^? matches any one character, ^# any run of characters (with
backtracking through (iy-36..33)), ^^ a caret. Trailing spaces are ignored. Banks are bound
through L_D887 as needed. Also called by fnLookup.
Entry: strings in (iy-123..118).
Exit: Fz = 1 on a match; otherwise flags of comparing the first differing characters (Fc = 1
when the first string's is lower; codes $C0 and above are adjusted by L_F874).

14528.synopsis:
Skips spaces and codes $18-$1F (L_CE2A) in the string at HL, binding its bank C first when
it is not (iy-111) (L_D887); each character is passed with L_A8BB.
Entry: HL = string; C = its bank.
Exit: HL = first other character; A = that character.

14551.synopsis:
Skips spaces and codes $18-$1F (L_CE2A) in the string at DE, binding its bank B first when
it is not (iy-111) (L_D887); each character is passed with L_A8BB.
Entry: DE = string; B = its bank.
Exit: DE = first other character; A = that character.

14569.synopsis:
Tests whether the string at HL ends after any spaces and codes $18-$1F (L_F8B4), leaving HL
where it was, and falls into L_F8E2.
Entry: HL = string; C = its bank.
Exit: Fz = 1 when the next other character is $00 or $14; A = that character.

14574.synopsis:
Tests A for a string end: Fz = 1 when A is $00 or $14.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: Fz = 1 for $00 or $14.
Changes: F.

14580.synopsis:
Reads a pattern character at HL (bank C bound first when it is not (iy-111)) and decodes the
caret escapes: ^^ gives '^', ^? gives $16 and ^# gives $15, HL then on the escape's second
character. Any other character, a lone '^' included, is returned with HL unchanged.
Entry: HL = pattern; C = its bank.
Exit: A = character or $15/$16; HL as above.
Changes: AF, HL.

14613.synopsis:
Classifies a comparison operand's type: $09 (number), $0A (date) and $0C (blank) are
accepted as they are; $05 and $06 (strings) are accepted as type $0B; anything else is
refused.
Entry: C = type.
Exit: Fc = 1 when accepted, C = type ($0B for a string); Fc = 0 when refused.
Changes: AF, C.

14640.synopsis:
Takes a date argument for DAY, MONTH and YEAR: pops the top item (L_F309), resolves it
(L_F9D2) and, when it is a date (type 8), converts its 3-byte internal date with GN_Die.
Otherwise, or when GN_Die fails, the current item becomes error $16 and it returns from its
caller as well.
Entry: argument at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: C = day of month (bits 4-0) and weekday (bits 7-5); B = month; DE = year.
Error: returns to the caller's caller with (iy-79) = 0, ($1D4D) = $16.

14667.synopsis:
Takes the two operands of an arithmetic or logical operator and drops them from the
evaluator stack.
1. Reads the left operand (L_F97F, A = 1) and keeps it at $1DA5, then the right one (A = 0).
When either is not a number it drops both and returns from the operator, the non-number
being the result.
2. The result type in (iy-79) is $0A when the left operand is a date, 8 when the right type
is 8, otherwise 9.
Entry: two operands at the top of the evaluator stack.
Exit: HL'HLC = left operand; DE'DEB = right operand; A = left type; Fz = 1 when both types
are equal.

14726.synopsis:
Drops the two top items of the evaluator stack (L_F386 with A = 2).
Entry: none.
Exit: ($1D45) = new top.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL, IX.

14731.synopsis:
Reads the item A below the top of the evaluator stack (L_F341) and resolves it (L_F9D2) into
an operand.
Entry: A = items to skip (0 = top).
Exit: a number: Fc = 0, P/V = 0, DE'DEB = value, C = 9; a blank: Fc = 0, P/V = 0, DE'DEB =
0, C = $0C; a date in a slot: Fc = 0, DE'DEB = its value with B = 0, C = $0A.
Error: Fc = 1, C = type for any other item; P/V = 1 when it is an error (type 0).

14752.synopsis:
Shared exit: clears the P/V flag, keeping A and the other flags.
Changes: F.

14787.synopsis:
Shared exit: sets the P/V flag, keeping A and the other flags (marks a blank or error
value).
Changes: F.

14794.synopsis:
Resolves the current item with L_F9D2 and requires a number. A date (type 8) or a range
(type 4) makes the current item error $08.
Entry: current item in C (type) and ($1D4D).
Exit: Fc = 0: a number at HL (or a blank, P/V = 1).
Error: Fc = 1 for anything else; C = type, or (iy-79) = 0 with error $08.

14814.synopsis:
Resolves the current evaluator item into a value. A slot reference (type 3) is looked up
(L_D887, L_FA04) and gives the slot's value; a number (type 2) returns Fc = 0 with HL = its
5 bytes. A string in the expression text (type 5) gives HL = (iy-114..113) + offset and B =
(iy-112); a date (type 8) gives B = (iy-124). Every other type returns Fc = 1.
Entry: C = type; ($1D4D) = data.
Exit: Fc = 0: a number at HL (P/V = 1 for a blank slot); Fc = 1: another value, C = type, HL
= its data (B = bank for a text); P/V = 1 when it is an error item.

14864.synopsis:
Entry inside L_F9D2's slot lookup: reads a slot reference at HL (L_B4F9: column A, row BC)
and falls into L_FA07.
Entry: HL = reference (3 bytes).
Exit: as L_FA07.

14867.synopsis:
Finds the slot at column A, row BC (L_D7AD) and makes its value the current item. The slot's
flags at (ix+3) decide:
1. Column $80 or above: error $0B. No slot: number zero marked blank (P/V = 1).
2. Bit 7 (text): a text of only spaces is blank; otherwise a string (type 6) at slot + 4.
3. Bit 4: error $0C when (ix+4) is $0C, otherwise error $13.
4. Bits 7-6 = 11: number zero (L_FA50); 00: the number at slot + 4 (L_FAB1).
5. Bits 7-6 = 01 (L_FA25): (ix+4) = 0 is a reference to another slot, followed (error $0C
when it is the current slot); 2 a date (type 8) at slot + 5; else a string (type 6) at slot
+ 10 + (ix+5).
Entry: A = column; BC = row.
Exit: (iy-79) = type; ($1D4D) or HL, B = data; Fc and P/V as L_F9D2, except that the errors
made here return Fc = 1 with P/V = 0.

14897.synopsis:
Entry inside L_FA07 for a slot whose flag bits 7-6 are 01: binds the slot (L_B518) and reads
(ix+4). Zero means the slot refers to the slot at (ix+5..7), which is followed through
L_FA07, or error $0C when that is the current slot ((iy-110..108)). 2 gives a date (type 8)
at slot + 5; other values a string (type 6) at slot + 10 + (ix+5).
Entry: slot found by L_D7AD ((iy-127..125)).
Exit: as L_FA07.

14940.synopsis:
Makes the current item the number zero: FP_ZER stored at $1D9B, ($1D4D) = $1D9B, (iy-79) =
2, then returns with Fc = 0 and P/V = 0.
Entry: none.
Exit: (iy-79) = 2; ($1D4D) = $1D9B; HL'HLC = 0; Fc = 0.

15037.synopsis:
Points ($1D4D) at offset 4 of the slot found by L_D7AD (address in (iy-127..126)), the
slot's number, and copies the slot's bank (iy-125) to (iy-124). L_FAB3 is the entry with
another offset in A.
Entry: slot in (iy-127..125).
Exit: ($1D4D) = HL = slot + 4; B = bank.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

15039.synopsis:
Entry inside L_FAB1 (which loads A = 4): points the value pointer at $1D4D at offset A into
the block whose address is held at (IY-127)/(IY-126), and copies the bank byte (IY-125) to B
and to (IY-124), the bank that goes with $1D4D.
Entry: A = offset; (IY-127)/(IY-126) = block address; (IY-125) = its bank.
Exit: HL = ($1D4D) = block address + A; B = (IY-124) = (IY-125).
Changes: AF, B, HL.

15059.synopsis:
Fetches the single argument of a one-argument function (fnAbs, fnCos, fnSin and the like) as
a number. L_F309 loads the next item of the argument list at ($1D45) and steps past it, and
L_F9D2 resolves it. When L_F9D2 returns Fc = 0 (a number), the number at ($1D4D) is loaded
into HL' HL C with L_FE8E and the result type (IY-79) becomes 9, so the caller can apply its
FPP operation and return. Otherwise the routine drops its caller's return address and
returns to the caller's caller with the value L_F9D2 left.
Entry: ($1D45) = argument list pointer.
Exit: HL' HL C = the number; IX = ($1D4D); (IY-79) = 9.

15081.synopsis:
Runs the callback in IX for every value in the current function's argument list, from the
first argument: C = 0, then falls into L_FADF. fnCount, fnMax, fnMin and fnSum use it.
Entry: IX = callback.
Exit: as L_FADF.

15083.synopsis:
Runs the callback in IX for every value in the current function's argument list, from
argument C on (counted from 0); a range argument is visited cell by cell. fnChoose starts at
argument 1.
1. Stores the argument number in (IY-38) and sets bit 7 of (IY-40) (not inside a range).
2. Loads argument (IY-38) with L_F325 and resolves it with L_F9D2.
3. A range (type 4) is set up with L_FB35, which makes its first cell the current value; bit
7 of (IY-40) is cleared and the cell is resolved by L_F9D2 again.
4. Any other value goes to the callback (through L_B8B4) with the flags from L_F9D2 (Fc = 0
for a number); a callback returning Fc = 1 stops the walk.
5. Inside a range, L_FB55 moves to the next cell and the walk goes back to L_F9D2; at the
range's end bit 7 of (IY-40) is set again.
6. Steps (IY-38) to the next argument until it reaches the count at ($1D45)+1, then sets
(IY-79) = 7. Last, L_F380 steps ($1D45) past the function's argument list.
Entry: IX = callback; C = first argument number; ($1D45) = argument list pointer.
Exit: Fc = 0 when every value was visited.
Error: Fc = 1 when the callback stopped the walk, or a range was empty (error $0E, L_FB35).
Keeps: IX.

15169.synopsis:
Starts the walk through the range value at ($1D4D): copies the range's first reference
(column, row word) to (IY-58)..(IY-56) and the second, past its marker byte, to
(IY-55)..(IY-53), sets the current cell (IY-61)..(IY-59) to the first with L_FBBD and, when
the range is not empty, makes that cell the current value (type 3) through L_FB68.
Entry: ($1D4D) = address of the range's two 3-byte references, with a marker byte between
them.
Exit: Fc = 0; C = 3; ($1D4D) = IY+35, holding the first cell's reference.
Error: Fc = 1 when the range is empty, with error $0E set by L_F339.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

15201.synopsis:
Moves the range walk at IY-61 to its next cell with L_FB93 and makes that cell the current
value (type 3) with L_FB68; its tail, L_FB5A, also ends L_FB35.
Entry: the range block at (IY-61)..(IY-53) (layout at L_FB9D).
Exit: Fc = 0, C = 3 and ($1D4D) = IY+35, holding the next cell's reference; Fc = 1 when the
range is finished.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

15220.synopsis:
Makes a cell reference the current value: writes column A and row CB (C low, B high) at
(IY+35)..(IY+37), sets the result type (IY-79) to 3 and falls into L_FB76, which points
$1D4D at that copy.
Entry: A = column; C = row low byte; B = row high byte.
Exit: C = 3; HL = ($1D4D) = IY+35; A = (IY-124) = (IY-111).
Changes: AF, C, DE, HL.

15234.synopsis:
Points the value pointer $1D4D at the reference buffer at IY+35 and sets its bank byte
(IY-124) to (IY-111), the bank L_D887 last bound.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = ($1D4D) = IY+35; A = (IY-124) = (IY-111); DE = $0023.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

15251.synopsis:
Copies 3 bytes from (HL) to (IX).
Entry: HL = source; IX = destination.
Exit: HL and IX advanced by 3; A = last byte copied; B = 0.
Changes: AF, B, HL, IX.

15263.synopsis:
Moves the range walk in the block at IY-61 to the next cell: IX = IY-61, then falls into
L_FB9D. Callers outside the formula evaluator use the same block.
Entry: the range block at (IY-61)..(IY-53).
Exit: as L_FB9D; IX = IY-61.
Changes: AF, DE, HL, IX.

15273.synopsis:
Moves a range walk to the next cell: the next column along the row, and after the last
column the first column of the next row. The block at IX holds the current cell at (IX+0)
(column) and (IX+1)/(IX+2) (row), the first cell at (IX+3)..(IX+5) and the last at
(IX+6)..(IX+8).
Entry: IX = range block.
Exit: Fc = 1 when the new current cell is inside the range; Fc = 0 when the walk has passed
the last row.
Changes: AF.

15305.synopsis:
Starts the range walk in the block at IY-61: IX = IY-61, then falls into L_FBC7.
Entry: the first and last cells at (IY-58)..(IY-53).
Exit: as L_FBC7; IX = IY-61.
Changes: AF, DE, HL, IX.

15315.synopsis:
Starts a range walk: copies the first cell (IX+3)..(IX+5) to the current cell (IX+0)..(IX+2)
and checks that the range is not empty, the first column not after the last (IX+6) and the
first row not after the last (IX+7)/(IX+8); falls into L_FBE1 for the row.
Entry: IX = range block (layout at L_FB9D).
Exit: Fc = 1 when the range holds at least one cell; Fc = 0 when it is empty.
Changes: AF.

15341.synopsis:
Compares the current row (IX+1)/(IX+2) of a range walk with its last row (IX+7)/(IX+8).
Entry: IX = range block (layout at L_FB9D).
Exit: Fc = 1 when the current row is not after the last row; Fc = 0 when it is.
Changes: AF.

15358.synopsis:
Tests whether the current row of the range block at IY-61 has passed its last row: IX =
IY-61, then L_FBE1.
Entry: the range block at (IY-61)..(IY-53).
Exit: as L_FBE1; IX = IY-61.
Changes: AF, DE, HL, IX.

15370.synopsis:
Converts the number in HL' HL C to an integer of 1 to 65535 with FP_FIX: it is accepted when
the high word of the result (HL) is 0 and the low word (HL') is not. The routine executes
EXX before testing the low word, so it returns with the register sets exchanged and the
value in BC of the set now current.
Entry: HL' HL C = number.
Exit: Fc = 0; BC = the integer.
Error: Fc = 1 with error $10 set through L_FC14 ((IY-79) = 0, ($1D4D) = $10); a zero value
fails after the EXX, a large or negative one before it.

15384.synopsis:
Converts the number in HL' HL C to an integer with L_FBFE and rejects one whose low byte is
0; fnIndex reads its column number with it. B is not tested, so a value over 255 with a
non-zero low byte also passes.
Entry: HL' HL C = number.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = C = low byte of the integer.
Error: Fc = 1 with error $10 set through L_FC14.

15392.synopsis:
Makes error $10 the current value: A = $10, then L_F339 sets the result type (IY-79) to 0
and stores the code at $1D4D. The flags are not changed; L_FC13, the instruction before it,
sets Fc = 1.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = $10; (IY-79) = 0; ($1D4D) = $10; flags as on entry.
Changes: A.

15403.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for ACS: data byte FuncID_Acs + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: the ASN node; less link: the ABS node; then "ACS" with bit 7 set on its last letter.
Every node is laid out this way: the data byte (function ID in bits 5-0, the argument form
in bits 7-6, which the parser tests after L_FD64 returns a function token), the offset + 1
from FunctionTree of the node to try when the name sorts after this one, the same for a name
that sorts before it (0 = none), then the name in capitals. L_FD64 searches the tree with
BinaryTreeSearch.

15409.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for ASN: data byte FuncID_Asn + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: none; less link: none; then "ASN" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15415.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for ATN: data byte FuncID_Atn + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: the CHOOSE node; less link: the ACS node; then "ATN" with bit 7 set on its last
letter.

15421.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for CHOOSE: data byte FuncID_Choose + $80 (an argument list in brackets);
greater link: none; less link: none; then "CHOOSE" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15430.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for COL: data byte FuncID_Col (bits 7-6 = 0: no argument list); greater
link: the EXP node; less link: the ATN node; then "COL" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15436.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for COS: data byte FuncID_Cos + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: none; less link: none; then "COS" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15450.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for DAY: data byte FuncID_Day + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: the DEG node; less link: none; then "DAY" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15456.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for DEG: data byte FuncID_Deg + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: none; less link: none; then "DEG" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15462.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for EXP: data byte FuncID_Exp + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: the INT node; less link: the COUNT node; then "EXP" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15468.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for IF: data byte FuncID_If + $80 (an argument list in brackets); greater
link: the INDEX node; less link: none; then "IF" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15473.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for INDEX: data byte FuncID_Index + $80 (an argument list in brackets);
greater link: none; less link: none; then "INDEX" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15481.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for INT: data byte FuncID_Int + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: the LN node; less link: the IF node; then "INT" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15487.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for LN: data byte FuncID_Ln + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: none; less link: none; then "LN" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15492.synopsis:
FunctionTreeRoot, the root of FunctionTree, where L_FD64 starts BinaryTreeSearch: the node
for LOG (FunctionTreeLog in the source). Data byte FuncID_Log + $40 (one argument in
brackets); greater link: the ROW node; less link: the COL node; then "LOG" with bit 7 set on
its last letter.

15507.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for MAX: data byte FuncID_Max + $80 (an argument list in brackets);
greater link: none; less link: none; then "MAX" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15519.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for MONTH: data byte FuncID_Month + $40 (one argument in brackets);
greater link: none; less link: none; then "MONTH" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15527.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for PI: data byte FuncID_Pi (bits 7-6 = 0: no argument list); greater
link: none; less link: the MONTH node; then "PI" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15532.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for RAD: data byte FuncID_Rad + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: none; less link: the PI node; then "RAD" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15538.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for ROW: data byte FuncID_Row (bits 7-6 = 0: no argument list); greater
link: the SUM node; less link: the MIN node; then "ROW" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15544.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for SGN: data byte FuncID_Sgn + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: none; less link: none; then "SGN" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15550.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for SIN: data byte FuncID_Sin + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: the SQR node; less link: the SGN node; then "SIN" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15556.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for SQR: data byte FuncID_Sqr + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: none; less link: none; then "SQR" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15568.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for TAN: data byte FuncID_Tan + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: the YEAR node; less link: none; then "TAN" with bit 7 set on its last letter.

15574.synopsis:
FunctionTree node for YEAR: data byte FuncID_Year + $40 (one argument in brackets); greater
link: none; less link: none; then "YEAR" with bit 7 set on its last letter. The last node of
FunctionTree; OperatorTree starts after it at $FCDD with the node for "!" (NOT).

15585.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for "&": data byte FuncID_And; greater link: none; less link: the "!"
node; then "&" with bit 7 set on its last character. The nodes have FunctionTree's layout
(data byte, greater link, less link, text); the data byte is the plain function ID, which
L_FD64 returns in L with token type $0D.

15589.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for "*": data byte FuncID_Multiply; greater link: the "+" node; less link:
the "&" node; then "*" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15593.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for "+": data byte FuncID_Add; greater link: none; less link: none; then
"+" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15597.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for "-": data byte FuncID_Subtract; greater link: the "/" node; less link:
the "*" node; then "-" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15601.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for "/": data byte FuncID_Divide; greater link: the "<" node; less link:
none; then "/" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15605.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for "<": data byte FuncID_Less; greater link: none; less link: none; then
"<" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15614.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for "<>": data byte FuncID_NotEqual; greater link: none; less link: none;
then "<>" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15619.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for "=": data byte FuncID_Equal; greater link: the ">" node; less link:
the "<>" node; then "=" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15623.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for ">": data byte FuncID_Greater; greater link: none; less link: none;
then ">" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15627.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for ">=": data byte FuncID_GreaterEqual; greater link: the "^" node; less
link: the "=" node; then ">=" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15632.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for "^": data byte FuncID_Raise; greater link: the "|" node; less link:
none; then "^" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15636.synopsis:
OperatorTree node for "|": data byte FuncID_Or; greater link: none; less link: none; then
"|" with bit 7 set on its last character.

15640.synopsis:
Returns the next token of the formula text without taking it. It first checks the stack:
when SP is below the word at $1D51 (saved from DE by main_entry), the parse is abandoned
through L_F27C (error 3, L_F0A6). A token already waiting in (IY-77)..(IY-75) (bit 7 of
(IY-77) clear) is returned again; otherwise L_FD2E scans one and it is kept there as the
waiting token.
Entry: none.
Exit: C = token type; HL = token value (see L_FD64); (IY-79) = C, ($1D4D) = HL and (IY-124)
= (IY-112) (L_FD3F).
Error: an invalid token abandons the parse through L_F0A6.

15674.synopsis:
Takes the next token of the formula text. A token waiting from L_FD0C (bit 7 of (IY-77)
clear) is taken and marked as used; otherwise the text's bank (IY-112) is bound with L_D887
when it is not the one in (IY-111), L_FD64 scans the token at ($1D4F) and $1D4F moves past
it. Ends in L_FD3F.
Entry: ($1D4F) = position in the formula text.
Exit: C = token type; HL = token value; (IY-79) = C; ($1D4D) = HL; (IY-124) = (IY-112).
Error: an invalid token abandons the parse through L_F0A6 with L_FD64's error code.

15691.synopsis:
Makes a token the current value: stores the type C in (IY-79), the value HL at $1D4D and the
formula text's bank (IY-112) in (IY-124). The parser also calls it with C = 1 and L = the
argument count at the end of an argument list.
Entry: C = token type; HL = token value.
Exit: A = (IY-112).
Changes: A.

15728.synopsis:
Scans one token of the formula text at HL and returns its type in C.
1. A zero byte ends the text: C = $0F (DE is not changed).
2. A letter starts a function name, looked up in FunctionTree with BinaryTreeSearch: C =
$0E, L = node data (function ID and argument form); for INDEX, ROW and COL (table L_FDB5)
bit 7 of (IY-44) is set. An unknown name is error $0A.
3. A digit or "." is a number read with FP_VAL into $1D96 (HL'), $1D98 (HL) and $1D9A (C): C
= 7. When FP_VAL fails the text is read as a date with GN_Gdt into IY+35: C = 8, HL = IY+35;
a failure there is error $16.
4. A byte $10-$13 (L_FE32) starts a cell reference: C = 3, HL = address of its 3 bytes; a
second reference straight after makes a range, C = 4.
5. A $14 byte starts a string that runs to the next $14: C = 5, HL = offset of its first
character from the text start (IY-114)/(IY-113); a missing end is error $0A.
6. Anything else is looked up in OperatorTree: C = $0D, L = function ID; a character that is
no operator is returned as itself, C = the character.
Entry: HL = position in the formula text.
Exit: Fc = 0; C = token type; HL = token value; DE = address after the token.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code ($0A or $16).

15809.synopsis:
Table of 3 function IDs that L_FD64 checks a function name against: FuncID_Index ($0C),
FuncID_Row ($16) and FuncID_Col ($05). A formula that calls one of them gets bit 7 of
(IY-44) set.

15933.synopsis:
Loads A from (HL) and falls into L_FE32.
Entry: HL = address of the byte.
Exit: as L_FE32; A = (HL).
Changes: AF.

15934.synopsis:
Tests whether A is $10-$13, a marker byte that starts a cell reference in formula text
(L_FD64), or $14, the string delimiter.
Entry: A = byte.
Exit: Fc = 1 when A is $10-$13; Fz = 1 when A is $14.
Changes: F.

15998.synopsis:
Copies the 5-byte number at ($1D4D) to the number buffer: the first word to $1D96, the
second to $1D98 and the fifth byte (the exponent) to $1D9A, the layout L_FD64 writes and
L_FEF0 reads.
Entry: ($1D4D) = address of the number.
Exit: HL = address after it; DE = second word; A = exponent.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

16022.synopsis:
Loads the 5-byte number at ($1D4D) into the first FPP operand: IX = ($1D4D), then L_FE8E.
Entry: ($1D4D) = address of the number.
Exit: HL' HL C = number; IX = ($1D4D).
Changes: C, HL, IX, HL'.

16026.synopsis:
Loads the 5-byte number at IX into the first FPP operand: (IX+0)/(IX+1) to HL',
(IX+2)/(IX+3) to HL and (IX+4), the exponent, to C.
Entry: IX = address of the number.
Exit: HL' HL C = number.
Changes: C, HL, HL'.

16044.synopsis:
Stores the first FPP operand HL' HL C as a 5-byte number at IX (layout at L_FE8E).
Entry: IX = destination; HL' HL C = number.
Exit: none.
Changes: none.

16062.synopsis:
Loads the 5-byte number at ($1D4D) into the second FPP operand: IX = ($1D4D), then L_FEB6.
Entry: ($1D4D) = address of the number.
Exit: DE' DE B = number; IX = ($1D4D).
Changes: B, DE, IX, DE'.

16066.synopsis:
Loads the 5-byte number at IX into the second FPP operand: (IX+0)/(IX+1) to DE',
(IX+2)/(IX+3) to DE and (IX+4), the exponent, to B.
Entry: IX = address of the number.
Exit: DE' DE B = number.
Changes: B, DE, DE'.

16084.synopsis:
Stores the second FPP operand DE' DE B as a 5-byte number at IX (layout at L_FEB6).
Entry: IX = destination; DE' DE B = number.
Exit: none.
Changes: none.

16102.synopsis:
Exchanges the two FPP operands: HL' with DE', HL with DE and C with B.
Entry: HL' HL C and DE' DE B = numbers.
Exit: the two numbers exchanged; A = the old B.
Changes: A, BC, DE, HL, DE', HL'.

16124.synopsis:
Converts the number in the number buffer ($1D96..$1D9A) to text at IY+35, formatted by the
byte in A.
1. Unless bit 6 of A is set, L_88E0 adds the default options: bit 7 when bit 2 of (IY-69) is
clear, and the bits of (IY+9).
2. The width B is (IY-36). Bit 4 reserves room for the trailing text at IY+16 ((IY+15)
bytes); bit 5 for the leading text at IY+22 ((IY+14) bytes), which is copied first with
L_FF99.
3. With bit 7 a negative number is written in brackets, and a positive one gets a $7F byte
where the ")" would go; without it a negative number gets "-".
4. FP_STR writes the digits: the low 4 bits of A are the decimal places, or, when they are
$F, the general format with as many digits as fit, at most 10.
5. Bit 4 appends the trailing text with L_FF99; the text ends in a zero byte. When the width
runs out the text is "%" and (IY-74) is set to 1 (L_FEE3).
Entry: A = format byte; number at $1D96 (HL'), $1D98 (HL) and $1D9A (C); (IY-36) = width.
Exit: IY+35 = text, zero-terminated.

16294.synopsis:
Copies A bytes from the workspace at IY+DE to (HL).
Entry: A = count (0 copies 256 bytes); DE = offset from IY; HL = destination.
Exit: HL = address after the copy; E = 0; IX = IY+DE+count.
Changes: AF, E, HL, IX.

labels.name: init_crash
labels.synopsis: Hangs in a loop to itself: OS_Bye does not come back.

labels.name: Exit_crash
labels.synopsis: Hangs in a loop to itself: OS_Bye does not come back.

109.synopsis:
The main loop of the Panel and PrinterEd: edits the current entry and runs the command that
ends the edit.
1. Empties the buffer, then copies the entry's saved value into it (StrcpyIX_Buffer).
2. Moves to the field, blanks it and moves back.
3. Edits it: an option list through HandleComboBox, anything else through HandleInputLine,
which return a command code in C ($20-$2E; other codes go back to main_1, which reloads the
saved value).
4. Clears the message line and stores the input (ValidateInput). An error is printed and the
entry edited again (main_2), except for Escape ($20), Next option ($26) and New ($2C).
5. Jumps to the command's handler in CommandTable with MainLoop as its return address.
Entry: IY = the variables (p_ubEntryID); the setting pool and buffers allocated.
Exit: never returns; the commands leave through Exit.

124.synopsis:
Entry inside MainLoop: edits the current entry again without reloading the buffer, so the
text that failed validation stays in the field. MainLoop jumps here after printing the
error.

492.synopsis:
Table of 15 words: the handler of each command code $20-$2E, in order CmdEscape, CmdEnter,
CmdLeft, CmdRight, CmdUp, CmdDown, CmdNextOption, CmdChgPage (twice, $27 and $28), CmdLoad,
CmdSave, CmdName, CmdNew, CmdUpdate and CmdTranslations. MainLoop indexes it with (code -
$20) * 2.

522.synopsis:
The Enter command ($21). In the Panel it applies every setting (CmdUpdate) and leaves
through Exit; in PrinterEd it moves to the next entry like CmdDown.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: PrinterEd: p_ubEntryID = the next entry. Panel: does not return.

533.synopsis:
The Escape command ($20): acknowledges the escape (ClearEsc). The Panel then leaves through
Exit without applying anything; PrinterEd returns to the main loop.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: PrinterEd only: A = the page ID; Fz = 0.

542.synopsis:
Acknowledges a pending escape with OS_Esc (SC_ACK).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF.

549.synopsis:
The cursor-up command ($24): selects the previous entry of the page; from the first entry
($20) it wraps to the last one.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: p_ubEntryID = the new entry.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

576.synopsis:
The cursor-down command ($25): selects the next entry of the page; after the last one it
wraps to the first ($20). CmdEnter falls back on it in PrinterEd.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: p_ubEntryID = the new entry.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

592.synopsis:
The page commands ($27, $28): in PrinterEd switches between page 1 and page 2 (from the
translation page it goes to page 1), selects the first entry and redraws the screen through
DrawScreenLabels. The Panel has one page and returns at once.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: p_ubPageID and p_ubEntryID set; the screen redrawn.

614.synopsis:
The translations command ($2E): selects the first entry of PrinterEd's ISO translation page
(page $22) and redraws the screen through DrawScreenLabels.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: p_ubPageID = $22; p_ubEntryID = $20.

735.synopsis:
The cursor-left command ($22): selects the entry that comes before the current one in
reading order (the nearest one above it, or left of it on the same row), comparing the
fields' screen positions. With none before it, it wraps to the last entry of the page. Keeps
a 6-byte work area on the stack and leaves through CmdRight's ending.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: p_ubEntryID and p_ubPageID = the new entry.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

845.synopsis:
The next-option command ($26) for a number field with an option list (the baud rates): finds
the buffer's text in the list (MatchComboOption), takes the option after it, copies that
text into the buffer, stores it (ValidateInput) and prints an error if that fails. Does
nothing for a field without a list.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: the buffer and the setting hold the next option.

982.synopsis:
The New command ($2C): resets every parameter of every page to its default with OS_Sp (A =
255), and in PrinterEd the printer name (PA_Ptr) too, then reads the settings back
(StoreDefSettings) and redraws the screen through DrawScreenLabels.
Entry: IY = the variables.

1025.synopsis:
The Load command ($29): asks for a file name (AskFilename), starts a new setting list
(is_1), opens the file and reads it line by line: each line is the entry ID, the page ID and
the value text, stored through vi_4. The end of the file ends it. On an error the file name
is cleared and the settings are read back from OZ (StoreAllSettings). Then closes the file,
redraws the screen and prints any error (CmdSave's ending).
Entry: IY = the variables.
Error: printed; ERR_BadFile for a line without its two ID bytes or a last line without a CR.

1108.synopsis:
The Save command ($2A): asks for a file name (AskFilename), opens it for output and writes
one line for every entry of every page that has a saved value: the entry ID, the page ID,
the value text and a CR (SaveBuffer). Then closes the file, redraws the screen and prints
any error.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Error: printed (PrintError); 0 means the system error.

1215.synopsis:
The Name command ($2B): asks for a file name (AskFilename) and redraws the screen with it,
or prints the error. In PrinterEd the name is the printer's name (PA_Ptr), and its file part
names the application.
Entry: IY = the variables.

1227.synopsis:
Clears the file name and the flag that says the setting pool is bound in, then falls into
is_1: selects the first entry, frees the setting pool and opens a new one.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: Fc = 0; p_pSettingPool = the new pool; p_pSettings = 0 (no settings).
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from OS_Mop.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX.

1235.synopsis:
Entry inside InitSettings that keeps the file name: selects the first entry of the first
page (InitPagePtrs), closes the setting pool if one is open, opens a new one in segment 1
with OS_Mop and empties the setting list. CmdLoad uses it.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: Fc = 0; p_pSettingPool = the new pool; p_pSettings = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from OS_Mop.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX.

1279.synopsis:
Writes the buffer as one line of a saved file: replaces its 0 terminator with a CR and
writes the text and the CR to the open file with OS_Mv.
Entry: the buffer = a 0-terminated text; p_pPrinterFileHandle = the file.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = 0 (the system error; OS_Erc gives it).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

1414.synopsis:
Opens the file name window: defines window 2 (60 by 8 characters at column 10, with a
border), selects and clears it and prints "Filename" at row 1.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

1443.synopsis:
Closes the file name window: selects window 1 again and sends 1,"2D2" for window 2.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

1511.synopsis:
Leaves the Panel or PrinterEd: closes the setting pool and the memory pool with OS_Mcl and
calls OS_Bye with A = 0. Also reached from MayRedraw and ErrorHandler on RC_Quit.
Entry: none.
Exit: does not return.

1569.synopsis:
Prints the last system error: falls into PrintError with A = 0, which sounds the bell and
prints OZ's text for the error (OS_Erc, GN_Esp), at most 16 characters, on row 2.
Entry: the error to print is OZ's last one.
Exit: Fc = 1.

1637.synopsis:
Table of 7 words: the texts of the program's own errors ERR_OutOfMemory (1) to ERR_BadName
(7), indexed by the code - 1. PrintError reads it.

1651.synopsis: Error text 1 (ERR_OutOfMemory): "Out of memory", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1664.synopsis: Error text 2 (ERR_BadFile): "Bad file", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1672.synopsis: Error text 3 (ERR_Escape): "Escape", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1678.synopsis: Error text 4 (ERR_BadCodeString): "Bad code string", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1693.synopsis: Error text 5 (ERR_StringTooLong): "String too long", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1708.synopsis: Error text 6 (ERR_BadValue): "Bad value", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1717.synopsis: Error text 7 (ERR_BadName): "Bad name", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1725.synopsis:
Sounds the bell: writes BEL with OS_Out.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

1730.synopsis:
Hides the cursor: writes 1,"2-C" through CursorOn's ending (CursorOnOff).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

1735.synopsis:
Shows the cursor: writes 1,"2+C".
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

1757.synopsis:
Clears the message line: moves to row 2, column 0 and writes 15 spaces.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

1769.synopsis:
Prints the 0-terminated text that follows the CALL and returns past it. A byte $A0-$BF is a
move: with the next byte it makes a cursor position, row = byte - $A0, column = next byte -
$20 (KprintSpecial). Other bytes go out with OS_Out.
Entry: the text after the CALL.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

1785.synopsis:
KPrint's handler for a byte with bit 7 set. For $A0-$BF it writes 1,"3@", the next byte
(column + $20) and the byte with bit 7 cleared (row + $20), and returns the byte after the
pair for KPrint to print. Other bytes are returned unchanged.
Entry: A = the byte; HL = its address.
Exit: A = the byte to print; HL = its address.
Changes: AF, HL.

1840.synopsis:
Draws the whole screen: defines window 1 (92 by 8 characters), selects and clears it, prints
the current page's labels (ShowPanel, ShowPrEdPg1, ShowPrEdPg2 or ShowPrEdTrans) and every
entry's value. In PrinterEd with a printer name it also prints "PRINTER" and the name
centred under it, and names the application (DC_Nam) after the name's file part.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

1994.synopsis:
Toggles tiny and reverse text: writes 1,"T",1,"R".
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

2084.synopsis:
Copies the 0-terminated text at IX into the buffer (p_pMem_Buffer_100).
Entry: IX = the text.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

2202.synopsis:
Says whether the Panel is running: reads the page ID and compares it with the Panel's page
($2A).
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: A = the page ID; Fz = 1 for the Panel, 0 for PrinterEd.
Changes: AF.

2208.synopsis:
Returns an entry's OS_Sp/OS_Nq reason: $80 and the entry record's fifth byte.
Entry: HL = the entry record (from GetEntryData).
Exit: BC = the reason; HL = HL + 4.
Changes: BC, HL.

2216.synopsis:
Checks the buffer's text for the current entry and stores it as its setting.
1. A number field with an option list (the baud rates) must match one option (ERR_BadValue).
2. In the Panel the default device and directory are parsed as names (CheckName,
ERR_BadName); in PrinterEd text is checked as a code string (EncodeTranslate).
3. Falls into vi_4 to store it. Option-list fields skip the checks.
Entry: IY = the variables; the buffer = the text.
Exit: Fc = 0, the setting stored.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (ERR_xxx); out of memory is printed here.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

2262.synopsis:
Entry inside ValidateInput: stores a text as the setting of one entry, replacing the one it
had (StoreSetting), and copies the text into the new record. CmdLoad stores each line's
value through it.
Entry: HL = the 0-terminated text; B = the page ID; C = the entry ID.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1; "Out of memory" printed (PrintError).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

2295.synopsis:
Returns the length of the 0-terminated text in the buffer; falls into StrLen.
Entry: the buffer = the text.
Exit: A = the length; HL = past the terminator; BC = - the length.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

2483.synopsis:
Applies every setting (the Panel's Enter): for every entry of every page sends its value to
OZ with OS_Sp. A Panel number is converted with FP_VAL, FP_ABS and FP_FIX and sent as a byte
or a word; a PrinterEd code string is encoded (EncodeTranslate), and for a field with a
placeholder (flags bit 5) a non-zero placeholder byte is sent to reason + 3 first; text goes
as it is; an entry without a value is sent with A = 255. PrinterEd also sends the printer
name (PA_Ptr). Ends with OS_Sp PA_Gfi, which installs the changed settings. Errors are
printed (PrintSysError).
Entry: IY = the variables.

2940.synopsis:
Entry inside StoreDefSettings, after InitSettings: reads every entry's current value from OZ
(OS_Nq) and stores it as a text setting. A Panel number becomes decimal text (FP_STR); a
PrinterEd code becomes a comma-separated list of decimal numbers (GN_Pdn, built on the
stack); text is kept. PrinterEd first reads the printer name (PA_Ptr) into the file name
buffer.
Entry: IY = the variables; a setting pool open.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 when memory runs out.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

3118.synopsis:
Table of control character names for PrinterEd's code strings: each record is the name in
capitals followed by its code ($00-$1F), from "NUL" to "US", with synonyms such as "BELL",
"TAB", "XON" and "XOFF"; -1 ends it. EncodeTranslate looks names up in it.

3378.synopsis:
Prints the labels of PrinterEd's page 1 (the printer codes 1-8 and their ON, OFF and Off at
CR fields) through KPrint.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

3611.synopsis:
Entry table of PrinterEd's page 2: 25 records (printer on and off, end of page, allow line
feed, the HMI prefix, suffix and offset, then the nine translations' characters and codes),
-1 ends it. Each record is 5 bytes: x + $20, y + $20, the field width, the flags (bit 7
number, bit 6 option list, bit 5 has a placeholder, bit 4 text (with bit 7, a list of
numbers), bits 3-0 the option list's offset in ComboBox_tbl) and the low byte of the
OS_Sp/OS_Nq reason ($80xx). GetEntryData reads it.

3737.synopsis:
Prints the labels of PrinterEd's page 2 (printer on/off, end of page, line feed, HMI and the
translations A to C) through KPrint.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

4008.synopsis:
Entry table of PrinterEd's ISO translation page: 64 records in 8 columns of 8, alternating a
character (a number, width 5) and what it changes to (a code string, width 8), for reasons
$80-$BF; $FF ends it. Each record is 5 bytes: x + $20, y + $20, the field width, the flags
(bit 7 number, bit 6 option list, bit 5 has a placeholder, bit 4 text (with bit 7, a list of
numbers), bits 3-0 the option list's offset in ComboBox_tbl) and the low byte of the
OS_Sp/OS_Nq reason ($80xx). GetEntryData reads it.

4329.synopsis:
Prints the labels of PrinterEd's ISO translation page (Ch and To on alternate rows) through
KPrint.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

4438.synopsis:
Entry table of the Panel: 15 records (auto repeat, keyclick, insert/overtype, default device
and directory, timeout, sound, map, map size, date format, the baud rates, parity, Xon/Xoff
and the keyboard), -1 ends it. Each record is 5 bytes: x + $20, y + $20, the field width,
the flags (bit 7 number, bit 6 option list, bit 5 has a placeholder, bit 4 text (with bit 7,
a list of numbers), bits 3-0 the option list's offset in ComboBox_tbl) and the low byte of
the OS_Sp/OS_Nq reason ($80xx). GetEntryData reads it.

4514.synopsis:
Prints the Panel's labels and its "PRESS ENTER TO UPDATE" note through KPrint.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

4763.synopsis:
Table of 6 words: the option lists YesNoTxt_tbl, CursorTxt_tbl, FormatTxt_tbl,
ParityTxt_tbl, BaudTxt_tbl and Keymap_tbl, indexed by bits 3-0 of an entry's flags (0, 2,
... 10). GetComboBox reads it.

4775.synopsis:
Option list "Yes" and "No": the texts separated by 0, -1 ends it. An option's key is its
first capital letter or digit.

4782.synopsis: Option list "Insert" and "Overtype", separated by 0, -1 ends it.

4798.synopsis: Option list of the date format, "European" and "American", separated by 0, -1 ends it.

4816.synopsis:
Option list of the parity: "None", "Space", "Mark", "Odd" and "Even", separated by 0, -1
ends it.

4841.synopsis:
Option list of the baud rates: 9600, 19200, 38400, 75, 300, 600, 1200 and 2400, separated by
0, -1 ends it. CmdNextOption steps through it.

4880.synopsis:
Option list of the keyboard layouts: "Uk", "France", "Denmark", "Sweden", "finLand",
"Germany", "usA", "sPain", "Italy" and "Norway", separated by 0, -1 ends it. The capital
letter is each option's key.

5132.synopsis: The Terminal's application name, "VT52" and a 0, given to DC_Nam.

5310.synopsis:
Table of 14 bytes: the control code the Terminal sends for menu commands 3 to 16: DEL, BS,
BEL, HT, LF, FF, CR, SO, SI, DC1, DC3, CAN, SUB and ESC.

5324.synopsis:
Sends a byte to the serial port with OS_SI (SI_PBT) and a 100 ms timeout. On a timeout it
sounds the bell.
Entry: A = the byte.
Exit: Fc = 0 when sent.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code for an error other than RC_Time.
Changes: AF, BC.
Keeps: DE, HL.

5455.synopsis:
The text 1,"3@" and a 0: the Terminal writes it before the column and row of a VT52 ESC Y
cursor move.

5556.synopsis:
Table of the VT52 escape sequences the Terminal turns into screen codes: each record is the
letter after ESC and the 0-terminated text written for it (A up, B down, C right, D left, H
home, I reverse line feed, J erase to the end of the screen, K erase to the end of the line,
L clear); a 0 ends it.

5819.synopsis:
The Calculator's Enter key: presses the highlighted button. Drops the return address that
IndirectJump left, takes the character of button row * 5 + column from Key2Button_tbl and
dispatches it as a typed key (main_5).
Entry: IY = the Calculator's variables (calc_ActiveRow, calc_ActiveCol).

5904.synopsis:
Table of the Calculator's keys, a 0 at the end: the 25 buttons row by row (C, DEL, S, R, +,
7, 8, 9, U, *, 4, 5, 6, Y, -, 1, 2, 3, I, /, 0, ., %, F, =), the convert keys P, T, X, M, D,
\ and E, then the cursor keys ($FF, $FE, $FC, $FD), Enter, Escape and $12. A key's place
gives the button's row and column and its handler in KeyTable.

5944.synopsis:
Table of 39 words: the handler of each key in Key2Button_tbl, in the same order. The main
loop calls it through IndirectJump with the key's number.

6022.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the digit keys (KeyTable). Clears a shown error (ClrError). With no
command pending the digit goes to the number being typed (PutNum); with StoM, RclM or Fix
waiting for its digit, it calls the command's handler in CmdTable (DoStoM, RclM, Fix)
through IndirectJump.
Entry: A = key, '0' to '9'; IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: to PutNum; or to the command's handler with A = digit (0-9); DE = IX = address of the
byte after the command code in calc_CmdBuffer.

6055.synopsis:
Calculator: the StoM command, reached from key_Num through CmdTable. Takes the shown value
(ldFH_F1NumBuf) into FReg1 and Float1, points IX at memory A (GetMemPtrA) and jumps through
StoM_tbl, indexed by the operator stored after StoM (none, +, -, x, /), to store, add,
subtract, multiply or divide the value into that memory. The memory's address is left on the
stack for StoM_plain.
Entry: A = memory number (0-9); DE = address of the operator byte in calc_CmdBuffer (0 for
none, 5-8 for + - x /); IY = calculator workspace.

6092.synopsis:
Calculator: table of 5 words, the StoM handlers: StoM_plain, StoM_add, StoM_sub, StoM_mul
and StoM_div. DoStoM indexes it with 0 for a plain StoM or the operator byte minus 4 (1-4).

6102.synopsis:
Calculator: StoM+. Loads the memory into FReg2 (RclM_FReg2), adds it to the value (FpAdd)
and goes on to StoM_plain to store the sum in the memory.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value; IX = memory slot; the slot's address on the stack.

6110.synopsis:
Calculator: StoM-. Loads the memory into FReg2 (RclM_FReg2), computes memory - value (FpSub)
and goes on to StoM_plain to store the result in the memory.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value; IX = memory slot; the slot's address on the stack.

6118.synopsis:
Calculator: StoMx. Loads the memory into FReg2 (RclM_FReg2), multiplies it by the value
(FpMul) and goes on to StoM_plain to store the product in the memory.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value; IX = memory slot; the slot's address on the stack.

6126.synopsis:
Calculator: StoM/. Loads the memory into FReg2 (RclM_FReg2), computes memory / value (FpDiv)
and falls into StoM_plain to store the quotient in the memory.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value; IX = memory slot; the slot's address on the stack.

6132.synopsis:
Calculator: plain StoM, and the end of every StoM handler. Pops the memory slot's address
into IX, stores FReg1 in it (StoM_FReg1) and falls into ClearCommand.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value to store; the memory slot's address on the stack.

6137.synopsis:
Calculator: ends a command. Resets the command flag (CF_B_Command) and empties the command
buffer (calc_CmdBuffer).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Changes: F, DE, HL.
Keeps: A, BC.

6151.synopsis:
Calculator: the RclM command, reached from key_Num through CmdTable. Drops the number being
typed, loads memory A into FReg1 and Float1 (the shown value) and goes to ClearCommand.
Entry: A = memory number (0-9); IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Float1 = memory A.

6166.synopsis:
Calculator: the Fix command, reached from key_Num through CmdTable. Stores 2 * A + 1 in
varFix (bit 0 marks a Fix as set; the display code, sub_FEBC, takes A back as the number of
decimals, 9 selecting a different FP_STR format) and goes to ClearCommand.
Entry: A = digit (0-9); IY = calculator workspace.

6173.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the '.' and 'E' keys (KeyTable). Ignores the key when the number
being typed already holds that character; otherwise falls into PutNum, which also starts a
new number with it.
Entry: A = '.' or 'E'; IY = calculator workspace.

6194.synopsis:
Calculator: adds a character to the number being typed (calc_NumBuffer, at most 17
characters). Ignored while a command is pending. Starts an empty buffer when no number is
being typed (sets CF_B_HasNumBuf), and a new character other than '.' replaces a leading '0'
that is not followed by '.'. A full buffer drops the character (NumBufferFull).
Entry: A = character; IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: calc_BufferPos advanced; buffer zero-terminated.
Changes: F, C, DE, HL.

6270.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the Clear key (KeyTable). Cancels a pending command (ClearCommand),
clears the number-entry, operator, error, constant and CF_B_3 flags, and falls into ZeroNums
to zero X and Y (Float1 and Float2).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL.

6311.synopsis:
Fills B bytes from HL with zero. Reached from ZeroNums, from key_DiamR (falls in, clearing
the memories and varFix) and from the start-up code (the workspace).
Entry: HL = start; B = byte count (1-256).
Exit: HL = byte after the block; A = 0; B = 0.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

6317.synopsis:
